records.title: Gambling Insights
records.description:
Stockton-on-Tees Borough Council (SBC) is seeking expressions of interest (EOI) from suitably experienced providers to undertake insight research exploring gambling-related harms within Stockton-on-Tees.
This work will complement a rapid Health Needs Assessment (HNA) and its associated recommendations, providing a more detailed understanding of local experiences, perceptions and impacts.
The purpose of the project is to develop a deeper understanding of the nature, extent and impact of gambling-related harms across the borough, including the experiences of affected individuals, families, communities and key stakeholders.
The findings will strengthen the local evidence base, enhance understanding of the scale and impact of gambling-related harms in Stockton-on-Tees, and inform future prevention, early intervention and support approaches. The insights generated will support future prevention and commissioning activity, helping to ensure that interventions are accessible, responsive to local need, and appropriately targeted.

records.title: Welcome and Integration Programme
records.description:
Stockton-on-Tees Borough Council (SBC) are seeking an organisation who is based or has a strong visible presence in Stockton-on-Tees, to deliver a comprehensive Welcome and Integration Programme for refugees and asylum seekers residing within the Borough. The organisation could deliver all of the elements of the contract or collaborate with other organisations or VCSE partners to fulfil the contract requirements.
The programme would provide welcome and orientation support on arrival, practical assistance, and facilitate access to volunteering, training and employment opportunities that support integration and independence for refugees under various Government resettlement schemes.
In addition to the above, we require the facilitation of positive integration outcomes for newly granted refugees while ensuring asylum seekers are well informed, prepared, and supported throughout the asylum decision-making process regardless of the outcome of their asylum claim, to prevent avoidable crises, particularly homelessness, income gaps and destitution.
An element of lived experience within the team would be beneficial to the delivery of this contract.
This programme aims to strengthen collaboration between the voluntary sector in the Borough and the SBC's Migration Support Team, creating opportunities for shared learning, coordinated service delivery and improved integration outcomes. Through a partnership approach, the programme will support asylum seekers and refugees to build resilience, develop meaningful community connections, access opportunities for volunteering, training and employment, and contribute positively to the local economy and wider community.
The recent introduction of Refugee and Asylum Seeker Service Fairs has demonstrated how valuable these fairs are to connect residents to local support services. Feedback from schools, families and partner organisations have highlighted the benefits of bringing services together in accessible locations, helping to address financial pressures, increase awareness of available support and improve access to key services.
The programme will support the continuation and expansion of this successful model through the delivery of Service Fairs across the Borough and support the growth and development of wider programme activity, ensuring that the lived experiences of people who have navigated the asylum and resettlement systems continue to inform service design and delivery.
By investing in a contractual partnership, SBC and the Recipient will maximise the reach and impact of existing projects, strengthen community cohesion, and support the successful long-term integration of asylum seekers and refugees within Stockton-on-Tees.

records.title: Network Micro-Segmentation
records.description:
The Senedd Commission is undertaking preliminary market engagement to inform a potential procurement of a network micro-segmentation platform. A future contract may cover supply, implementation, ongoing support and platform development, with associated professional services and training.
The Commission wishes to explore how micro-segmentation could improve visibility of communications between systems and provide more granular control of network access. The intended outcomes are stronger protection of its digital environment, less unnecessary connectivity and reduced potential for lateral movement, while maintaining the availability of legitimate business services.
Interested suppliers are invited to describe current market capability, delivery models and approaches to implementation and ongoing service provision.
The scope remains under development. We welcome information on approaches for server and application workloads and options for wider corporate-network coverage, including client and other network-connected devices. We welcome details on the capabilities, dependencies and limitations of different deployment and enforcement models, together with the trade-offs between workload-focused and wider network segmentation, to help us assess their suitability.
As part of this early-stage activity, we are inviting interested suppliers to submit a short questionnaire designed to help us understand current market capability, delivery models, and potential approaches to service provision.
The Senedd Commission currently anticipates procuring any subsequent requirement through Lot 2 of the Welsh Government IT Products and Services (iii) framework. The information gathered through this engagement will support the Senedd Commission in shaping any subsequent procurement strategy. The Commission reserves the right to amend its proposed procurement route following market engagement. Participation is voluntary, and responses will be used for research and planning purposes only. Completion of the questionnaire does not form part of any formal procurement process, nor does it create any obligation or advantage in any future tender.
Your insights will help ensure that any future approach is well-informed, proportionate, and aligned with best practice. 
To obtain a copy of the questionnaire please email Helena Grant at helena.grant@senedd.wales. Responses must be submitted to Helena Grant at helena.grant@senedd.wales by 16:00 on Monday 7th December 2026. 
We appreciate your time and contribution to this engagement exercise and look forward to hearing from you.

records.title: ESPH782: Rother Housing Maintenance and Repair
records.description:
Rother District Council is seeking to appoint a suitably experienced contractor to provide housing repair, maintenance, compliance and refurbishment works across its housing portfolio, including temporary accommodation and newly acquired properties.
The contract will cover a range of responsive, planned and improvement works, including property refurbishment; kitchen and bathroom works; electrical, plumbing, heating and gas works; statutory servicing, inspection and certification; fire safety works; building fabric and roofing repairs; damp, mould and ventilation works; environmental and energy-efficiency improvements; accessibility adaptations; void works and clearance; and emergency attendance and making-safe works.
Works will be instructed as required through individual works orders under a measured term arrangement. The nature, frequency and value of works will vary during the contract term and no minimum volume or value of work is guaranteed.
The initial contract term will be 24 months, with the option for the Council to extend for up to a further two periods of 12 months.

records.title: Carrow Works - Early Works Enabling Package
records.description:
Norwich City Council (NCC) are developing the Carrow Sites as part of the East Norwich Strategic Regeneration Area. NCC is procuring this demolition and enabling works package at Carrow Works in advance of the proposed Phase 1 redevelopment. The main construction works for Phase 1 will be procured separately.
The Council will be conducted as a two-stage open procedure comprising a suitability assessment stage (Stage 1) followed by an Invitation to Tender (Stage 2). Stage 1 will include a Supplier Selection Questionnaire through which suppliers will be assessed against the published Conditions of Participation selection criteria, including financial standing, technical capability and relevant experience. Suppliers meeting the minimum requirements will be scored against the published selection criteria and the five highest-scoring suppliers will be shortlisted and invited to participate in Stage 2.
Stage 2 will comprise an Invitation to Tender (ITT), with the confirmed shortlisted suppliers invited to submit a full tender response, including quality and pricing information. The contract will be awarded to the supplier submitting the Most Advantageous Tender.
This procurement is for a below-threshold works contract under the Procurement Act 2023. As the estimated value of the works contract exceeds £207,720, the Council will undertake a separate supplier suitability assessment stage prior to issuing the Invitation to Tender. This approach is consistent with Section 85(3)(b) of the Procurement Act 2023.
The Stage 1 submission deadline is 4 December 2026 at 12:00 noon.
The estimated contract duration is between 6 and 9 months.

records.title: Enterprise Search
records.description:
Requirements Overview:
The Metropolitan Police Service (MPS) is seeking to implement a modern Enterprise Search capability that enables officers and staff to securely search and retrieve information from across the organisation through a single, trusted service.
The MPS has already invested in an Enterprise Data Platform (EDP), which acts as the organisation's strategic data platform and contains curated operational and corporate data sourced from key policing systems. As the data is already being consolidated within the EDP, the primary challenge is no longer data integration, but providing users with a fast, intuitive and intelligent way to discover, interrogate and exploit that information.
The service will be designed to provide a consistent and intuitive user experience across multiple device types, including desktop, laptop and mobile devices, enabling officers and staff to securely access relevant information wherever operationally required.
The MPS is therefore seeking a scalable, AI-enabled search capability that improves access to information, supports operational decision-making, reduces reliance on legacy search technologies and provides a foundation for future analytics, Copilot and AI-enabled policing capabilities.
Business Outcome:
A secure, enterprise-scale search capability that allows officers and staff to find the right information, from the right data sources, at the right time, through a single trusted service built upon the MPS Enterprise Data Platform, accessible across multiple devices and supporting both office-based and mobile operational use.

records.description:
This procurement process is being advertised and run by First Greater Western limited on its own behalf and on behalf of the successor operator of the rail passenger transport services in respect of Great Western Railway (GWR). That successor operator will be a public sector company, is expected to be a wholly owned subsidiary of DfT OLR Holdings Limited and will be ultimately owned by the Secretary of State for Transport. The date for transfer of the current operations to the successor operator is not yet confirmed. Where the transfer is completed before contract award under this procurement process, the successor operator may elect (but will not be obliged) to carry on with this procurement process in place of GWR, by taking on the role of contracting entity from the date of completion of the transfer (with this notice and all other procurement documents to be interpreted accordingly). Where the transfer is not yet completed by the time of contract award, contractual rights may be included in the contractual arrangements to enable transfer to the successor operator. Bidders should note that this procurement process (if ongoing), or any awarded contract, may be included in a transfer scheme made by the Secretary of State under section 12 of the Railways Act 2005, or the transfer may be effected outside of, or separate from, such a scheme.
If transfer takes place before the contract award the successor operator shall assume all the rights of the Client set out in this document. All references to the Client shall be deemed to refer to the successor operator for the purposes of this procurement and the successor operator shall be entitled to continue or terminate this procurement as if it was involved.
Great Western Railway (GWR) is seeking to establish a multi-supplier framework for the provision of fabrication, structural repair and composite repair services in support of its Train & Rolling Stock (T&RS) maintenance operations.
The objective of this procurement is to establish a reliable, responsive and technically competent supply base capable of supporting GWR with both planned and ad hoc fabrication and repair requirements.
The Framework is divided into the following Lots:
Lot 1 - Metal Fabrication and Non-Structural Repairs: metal fabrication, replacement panel production and non-structural bodywork repairs.
Lot 2 - Structural Repairs: structural repair services to vehicle body shells and load-bearing structures, including specialist welding and associated engineering activities.
Lot 3 - Composite Repairs: specialist repair and refurbishment of composite components and structures.

records.title: Occupational Health Services 2028-2033 - Supplier 1
records.description:
The Authority is seeking a Contract Term of 5 years from Services Go-Live, with an option for the contracting parties to extend to 7 years
Services to be procured are as follows:
- Occupational Health Case Management services, namely through the provision (usually through an Authority Line Manager-led referral) of appropriately qualified clinical assessment and advisory expertise, alongside specialist psychological and physiological treatment modalities where indicated. Case Management services will be expected to provide advice, treatment and ultimately the resolution of health and wellbeing matters affecting the productivity and availability of MPS personnel. 
-Specialist policing 'Fitness for Task' assessments, including provision of Job Related Fitness Testing, to ensure that Authority personnel meet mandated standards of fitness to perform their particular roles.
-Specialist policing Health Surveillance to monitor health risks applicable to Authority personnel performing specific roles.
-Management of an Occupational Health Case Management System alongside in-house MPS personnel.
-Legally required Eyecare provisions to all MPS personnel
-Blood-borne Virus and Infectious Disease Management in order to protect Authority personnel from related health risks and provide treatment where required.
-Provision of Vaccination courses in order to provide immunity for Authority personnel against Hepatitis B, and potentially other transmittable viruses. 
-Provision of Selected Medical Practitioners for the assessment of potential Ill Health Retirement cases.
-Provision of physical space across Greater London and the Home Counties from where Services can be delivered to Authority personnel. 
-Configuration and integration of an Occupational Health Case Management system, from which the Services can be administered.
A single supplier is sought for the Services, so that all required Services components can be delivered efficiently and holistically to Authority personnel. It is also beneficial to have a single supplier managing the Occupational Health Case Management System. The Authority has also extracted the Employee Advisory Programme service as a separate procurement (tender to be launched in 2027), such that further disaggregation of the supplier ecosystem would confer additional complexity and risk to the Authority occupational health ecosystem.
Total value (estimated)
The Maximum contract value includes all possible extensions and reflects modelled costs of the Services using the current outsourced pricing model, and untested assumptions relating to the potential future participation of neighboring organisations to the Authority. 
This figure does not reflect the Authority's ambition to transform the Services' pricing model, nor does it guarantee that non-Authority organisations will be in a position to seek supply of the contracted Services from the Supplier. Thus, the figure is highly indicative and should not be used to interpret the initial annualised contract value

records.title: LIBRTI RISE - (Remote Inspection for Safe Entry) UAV/Drone Requirements
records.description: The Remote Inspection for Safe Entry (RISE) project has been established to develop and demonstrate a remote inspection capability that enables evidence-based decisions regarding personnel access into potentially hazardous fusion-related facilities following operation. Following production operations, there may be uncertainty regarding radiological conditions, thermal conditions, equipment status, environmental conditions and the overall suitability of the area for human entry. Traditional inspection methods require personnel to enter the facility to collect this information, potentially exposing workers to unnecessary risk and delaying access decisions. The RISE project seeks to reduce this uncertainty through the deployment of remotely operated robotic inspection systems capable of collecting high-confidence evidence before personnel access is considered

records.title: Provision of Home to School Transport for Alt Bridge

proposedAmendments.rationale:
To provide continuity of transport provision and to allow time to undertake a new procurement process for these services the Council is proposing to modify, in accordance with Contract Procedure Rule 9.1.3 (Schedule 1) and Paragraph 8 of Schedule 8 of the Procurement Act 2023 (Additional goods, services, or works), of the following emergency contracts for the delivery of Home to School transport.
The Council has not been able to satisfactorily resolve the issues with the providers who had been successful in the original procurement process to allow for services to be mobilised by the end of the current emergency contract periods. The Council is obliged to secure the delivery of statutory services to ensure children can attend school without disruption to services. 
Therefore, the Council considers it appropriate to modify the contracts awarded as an emergency for a short period of time to allow the Council to undertake a new procurement for these services.
The proposed modifications are justified under the provisions of the Paragraph 8 of Schedule 8 of the Procurement Act 2023 (Additional goods, services, or works).
This allows for modifications to contracts provided the modification does not exceed 50% of the value of the contract at the time of its modification, and the modification is for the provision of goods, services, or works already provided for in the contract, using a different supplier would result in the supply of services that are different from, or incompatible with, those already provided for in the contract and we consider the difference or incompatibility would result in disproportionate technical difficulties in operation or maintenance or other significant inconvenience and the substantial duplication of cost to the authority.

records.description:
Engineering Construction Industry Training Board (ECITB) is pleased to announce the commencement of pre-market engagement for our forthcoming 2027 ECITB and Mersey Dee Clean Energy Scholarships procurement, which will commence in September 2027.
Scholarships are the ECITB's flagship new entrant programmes, designed to address skills shortages in the UK engineering construction industry by providing employer-led, full-time technical training that leads directly into employment or accelerated apprenticeships. This scholarship will be delivered in conjunction with the Mersey Dee Alliance.
The programme aims to:
•	Create a sustainable pipeline of skilled entrants into the engineering construction industry, in this instance with a focus on the clean energy sectors in the northwest of England and north Wales
•	Deliver training in disciplines where regional demand has been identified through labour market intelligence.
•	Connect learners directly with employers throughout their training, rather than simply delivering college-based education.
•	Ensure learners receive a thorough grounding in industry best practise and safe behaviours before being presented to employers.
•	Support the industry's workforce needs across England, Scotland and Wales
•	Maximise available public and ECITB funding to create a sustainable and cost-effective delivery model.
Regions and Disciplines
Tenders are planned to be launched in January 2027 covering the following Regions and Disciplines:
-Regions: Mersey - Dee & North Wales region around River Dee
-Disciplines: Mechanical, Pipefitting, Fab/Weld, Electrical and General Engineering (foundation)
*These may be subject to change at ECITB's and supporting partners discretion
About the ECITB
The Engineering Construction Industry Training Board (ECITB) is the statutory skills organisation for the Engineering Construction Industry (ECI) in Great Britain.
An Arm's Length Body of government, the ECITB works with employers and governments to attract, develop and qualify the engineering construction workforce in a wide range of craft, technical and professional disciplines.
Employer-led, the ECITB is accountable to parliament and funded by a levy that it is required to collect from the industry.
The levy is used to support employers to train and upskill their workforce to industry standards, develop qualifications and courses that meet employer needs and regulate a network of approved training providers.
The ECITB is also an Awarding Organisation accredited by the Office of the Qualifications and Examinations Regulation (Ofqual), Qualifications Wales and Qualifications Scotland Accreditation.
The ECITB plays a vital role, along with the education sector, government and employers, in ensuring Britain has workers with the skills to meet the needs of the engineering construction industry.
We invest more than £28 million every year to enhance skills across the engineering construction industry, support growth through workforce training, and tackle labour shortages and skills gaps. This includes technical, management and professional training as well as support for apprenticeships and graduates entering industry.
About the Mersey Dee Alliance
The Mersey Dee Alliance (MDA) is a cross-border partnership supporting economic growth across North East Wales, West Cheshire and Wirral. It brings together public sector, education and business partners to support key industries, strengthen skills and employment opportunities, and attract investment.
With a strong concentration of engineering, manufacturing and energy industries, the region provides an important setting for collaboration on the skills needed to support future growth and the transition to a low-carbon economy.

records.title: Strategic Planning
records.description:
We want to use Monday.com for three clearly defined purposes. 
The first two activities are covered by the proposed contracts 75 editable-user license's and include portfolio management and in train testing/development activities and the third activity is an opportunity to test new service improvements.  
1. Manage the Transformation and Digital Services roadmap
Monday.com will be used to manage and report on the Transformation and Digital Services roadmap. It will provide a clearer view of priorities, progress, dependencies and how resources are being used.
This will help leadership understand what work is under way, where there may be delivery pressures and whether resources are focused on the organisation's agreed priorities.
2. Continue tactical service-improvement workflows
Monday.com will continue to support the tactical service-improvement workflows that are already in place. Disposals is the most obvious example.
These workflows are an interim step. They allow teams to move away from spreadsheets, email and other manual ways of coordinating work and begin to manage the process in a more structured and visible way.
The longer-term intention is to move suitable customer and service workflows into Customer Central or other enterprise platforms. This cannot happen immediately because MRI Web must be deployed first. Until that dependency is complete, Monday.com provides a practical way to improve and test workflows without waiting for the full strategic solution.
3. Use Monday.com as a controlled sandbox
Where appropriate, Monday.com may also be used as a sandbox to test new service improvements ideas and workflows before they are moved into Customer Central or another strategic system.

records.title: 2627-0252 Security and Associated Services
records.description:
The London Borough of Islington is preparing to procure a new contract for the provision of security and associated services across Council buildings and other locations. The anticipated core requirement includes static guarding, front of house and reception security, access control, key holding and alarm response, planned and reactive mobile patrols, CCTV monitoring, emergency response, and planned and ad-hoc security and guarding, including event and civic security support and door supervision where required.
As part of developing the future service, the Council is exploring opportunities to consolidate additional security requirements currently delivered under separate contractual arrangements. This includes:
•Security Services at Islington Assembly Hall, including event security, crowd management, door supervision, access control and customer safety functions. The current service supports a range of events including live music, civic, community, and commercial events.
•Vacant property Security Services, including securing and protection of vacant Council-owned properties, site inspections, temporary site security arrangements, emergency attendance, property protection measures and associated services. The current service supports the management and safeguarding of vacant sites pending disposal, redevelopment or reoccupation.
The final scope and service delivery model are yet to be determined and will be informed through stakeholder engagement and preliminary market engagement. The Council is particularly interested in understanding whether the requirements would be best delivered through a single contract or through separate lots.
In line with the Council's objectives, the Council is committed to reducing barriers to entry and encouraging a diverse and competitive marketplace. The Council therefore welcomes feedback from organisations of all sizes, including SMEs and local suppliers.
The estimated value of the proposed contract has not yet been finalised. However, based on current projections and anticipated service requirements, the total contract value over the maximum proposed term of five (5) years is anticipated to be in excess of £7 million.

records.title: Ruislip Depot Wheel Lathe Replacement (MobiTurn)
records.description:
Description of the Contract
TfL intends to award this contract directly under section 41 and Schedule 5, paragraphs 7(a) and 7(b) of the Procurement Act 2023, because competition is absent for objective technical reasons and only Hagenscheidt MFG (UK) Limited can supply the requirement.
The existing wheel lathe installation at Ruislip depot, including the foundation pit, rail interfaces and control systems, is specific to Hagenscheidt equipment. A lathe from any other manufacturer would require substantial civil and system re-engineering, a significantly longer outage of a critical depot asset and disproportionate cost and safety risk.
There is no reasonable alternative or substitute, and the absence of competition is not the result of an artificial narrowing of the requirement. The contract will not be awarded until after the 8-working-day standstill period. 
The Wheel Lathe is a critical maintenance asset supporting wheel reprofiling activities required to maintain rolling stock wheelsets, fleet availability and operational reliability across the London Underground network.
The contract includes: Manufacture and supply of a replacement Hegenscheidt MobiTurn Wheel Lathe. Delivery to Ruislip Depot. Installation and commissioning activities. Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT). Site Acceptance Testing (SAT). Operator and maintainer training.
Technical documentation. Warranty support. Operational handover and acceptance.
Supplier Awarded the Contract:
HAGENSCHEIDT MFG (UK) LIMITED
06360710
registered at Unit 7 Meadows Drive, Staveley, Chesterfield, Derbyshire, S43 3LH
Estimated Contract Value: £1.427 million (CAPEX)
The contract value includes manufacture, supply, delivery, installation, commissioning, testing, training, warranty and associated contractual deliverables.
Contract Term
Anticipated Contract Award Date: March 2027
Anticipated Delivery and Commissioning Period: March-April 2028
Operational Handover: April-May 2028
Applicable Procurement Act 2023 Ground
The award has been made in reliance on: proposed direct award justified under Section 41(6) and Schedule 5, Paragraph 7(a) and 7(b) of the Procurement Act 2023, which permit the award of a public contract without a competitive tendering procedure where additional goods, services or works are required from an existing supplier  which are intended as an extension to, or partial replacement of, existing goods, services or works in circumstances and a change of supplier cannot be made because:
•	(a) a change in supplier would result in the contracting authority receiving goods, services or works that are different from, or incompatible with, the existing goods, services or works, and
•	(b) the difference or incompatibility would result in disproportionate technical difficulties in operation or maintenance.
Benefits of the award includes the following:
Operational continuity.
Infrastructure compatibility.
Maintenance standardisation.
Asset reliability.
Whole-life cost optimisation.
Delivery confidence.
Fleet availability protection.
Union by-in
HAGENSCHEIDT MFG (UK) LIMITED was the only supplier to submit quotations when the ITT was published.

records.buyer: Tyne and Wear Passenger Transport Executive T/A Nexus
records.title: NEX26/18 Battery Locomotives Refurbishment
records.description:
Nexus are tendering for the detailed design and refurbishment of three battery locomotives, bespoke to the Nexus Metro network, which have become unreliable and not fit for purpose.
The locomotives were originally supplied by Hunslet-GMT in the early 1990's and are a key asset in the emergency recovery of Nexus' rolling stock and movement of the rail head treatment train across the Metro railway. Currently the network operates from a 1500V DC overhead line system, the battery locos are approved to operate on Network Rail assets, although is not necessarily required to maintain this approval.
The refurbishment will encompass:
Traction and Solid State Power Systems
- Modernisation of the traction equipment (motor alternator and motor generator set) using solid state power technology and power electronics.
Mechanical Systems & Running Gear
- Overhaul of structural components, suspension, wheelsets, and key mechanical assemblies.
Electrical & Control Systems
- Renewal of high voltage and auxiliary electrical systems upgraded control equipment, and readiness for future signalling integration.
Braking Systems
- Refurbishment and commissioning of brake discs and brake system.
Cab and Operator Environment
- Improvements to the cab environment (sealing, comfort, ergonomics) and general enhancements
Design Requirements
The design requirements for the battery locomotives are:
- Maximum speed 55kph
- Pantograph height above rail when lowered - 3555mm
- Pantograph height when fully raised - 5666mm
- Vehicle width - 2600mm
- Wheel diameter - 838mm
- Cab height above rail - 3160mm
- Wheelbase - 2500mm
- Length over buffers - 7500mm
- Length over extended coupler - 9000mm
- Tare / gross weight - 26.25t
- Couplers are Bergische Stahl Industrie (BSI) with a standard screw coupling
- Wheel arrangement is 0-4-0
- Continuous power rating of 180hp
- High voltage circuit - supply from 1500V DC overhead line system
- Indusi track brake equipment
- Lead Acid traction battery - 540V, 116kWh at 5-hour discharge
- Low voltage circuits, - 110V, 24V
- Traction motor (one) - 180hp, 540V DC force ventilated.

records.buyer: The Police and Crime Commissioner for Devon and Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly
records.title: Stalking Perpetrator Intervention, Independent Victim Advocacy and System Wide Training
records.description:
The Authority seeks to commission a specialist stalking service across Devon, Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly. The Service shall address stalking-related harm through assessment, perpetrator intervention, independent victim advocacy, safeguarding, dynamic risk management, professional development, monitoring and system learning.
The Service shall operate as part of the wider multi-agency response. It shall complement and strengthen existing police, probation, safeguarding, victim support and protective order arrangements, but it shall not replace statutory agency responsibilities.
The Service is intended to support the objectives of the Home Office Domestic Abuse and Stalking Perpetrator Interventions Fund, subject to confirmation of funding. The Service shall contribute to improved victim safety, strengthened perpetrator accountability, earlier intervention, improved multi-agency responses and learning about effective stalking perpetrator intervention.
Commissioning rationale:
• Create a dedicated referral and intervention pathway for stalking perpetrators.
• Improve victim safety through functionally independent advocacy and safety planning.
• Strengthen multi-agency risk management, information sharing and escalation.
• Improve professional confidence, referral quality and stalking identification.
• Generate reliable learning about implementation, engagement, outcomes and future commissioning requirements.
Strategic Outcomes:
The Provider shall be accountable for delivery of activities and outputs within its control. Some system-level impacts depend on police, probation, safeguarding, courts, health, local authorities and other agencies and cannot be attributed solely to the Provider.
For contract management and evaluation purposes, outcomes shall be understood at three levels:
• Provider-Controlled Deliverables: activities and outputs directly within the Provider's control, including referrals processed, assessments completed, advocacy offers made, interventions delivered, risk reviews undertaken, safeguarding escalations made, reports submitted and training delivered.
• Provider-Influenced Outcomes: changes to which the Provider is expected to make an evidence-informed contribution, including improved victim safety, increased perpetrator accountability, reduced dynamic risk indicators, improved engagement, improved referral quality and stronger multi-agency risk management.
• System-Level Impacts: longer-term changes to which the Service may contribute but which cannot be attributed solely to the Provider, including reduced repeat victimisation, reduced serious harm, reduced repeat police contact and a stronger local response to stalking.

records.title: Let’s Get Active: Community Physical Activity and Wellbeing Service
records.description:
Leicester City Council (LCC) is seeking to commission a Let’s Get Active: Community Physical Activity and Wellbeing Service to support Leicester-based adults aged 18 years and over to become more physically active, improve their wellbeing, strengthen community connections and reduce health inequalities. The service forms part of the Council’s wider Prevention Programme and complements Leicester’s Let’s Get… network of community wellbeing services. The proposed contract is expected to commence on 01/03/2027 and run until 28/02/2030, with the option to extend until 28/02/2032 subject to terms.
The Let’s Get Active service will provide a minimum of five free physical activity sessions each week in accessible community settings across Leicester. Activities may include walking groups, gentle exercise classes, seated activities, multi-sport sessions, recreational sport, women-only activities and physical activity sessions focused on mental wellbeing. The service will support people to build their confidence, sustain their participation in physical activity and access wider wellbeing, volunteering, training and community opportunities.
The provider will be expected to work with Leicester City Council, community organisations and trusted partners to promote the service and engage people who experience the greatest barriers to physical activity. The service must be inclusive, culturally appropriate and accessible to people with varying abilities, with delivery locations and activities adapted in response to community need and participation levels.

records.title: Provision of Servicing and Maintenance of Blowers and Compressors, and the Performance Testing of Aeration System Process
records.description:
The framework is divided into two lots: Lot 1 - Blower and Compressor Servicing and Maintenance and Lot 2 - Aeration Systems Performance Evaluation and Improvement. Suppliers will be required to deliver services that improve asset reliability, operational performance, energy efficiency, and whole-life value across activated sludge process (ASP) systems.
Lot 1 covers the planned preventative maintenance, condition monitoring, repair, overhaul, breakdown response, and lifecycle management of air blowers, air compressors, gas blowers, and gas compressors, including associated control and instrumentation equipment.
Lot 2 focuses on identifying and delivering energy and process efficiency improvements through blower performance testing, aeration system assessments, ASP process optimisation, diffuser performance evaluation and acid cleaning, whole-life cost analysis, and support for capital improvement projects. Suppliers may also be required to provide independent technical advice, project management, and Principal Contractor or Principal Designer services under CDM 2015.
The framework aims to support reduced energy consumption, improved process performance, enhanced asset lifespan, and continuous improvement across the Utilities' wastewater treatment operations. Suppliers will be expected to operate to defined performance standards, provide regular management information, and proactively identify innovation and efficiency opportunities throughout the contract term

records.buyer: Armagh City Banbridge and Craigavon Borough Council
records.title: The Development and Delivery of Armagh City, Banbridge and Craigavon Borough Council Local Economic Partnership Future Focused Technologies Programme 2027-2028
records.description: The LEP is funded by the DfE Regional Balance Fund (£4.509m, 2025-2029) and is tasked with addressing structural economic barriers and designing local interventions. The Action Plan focuses on three priority themes: 1. Land Availability and Development (capital) 2. Business Workspace Development (capital) 3. Supporting Business Growth (revenue) The Future Focused Technologies Programme forms a key component of the Supporting Business Growth theme within the ABC Local Economic Partnership (LEP) Action Plan. The programme will support the strategic ambition of equipping businesses within the agri-food sector, agri-supply chain and wider rural economy with the skills, knowledge and capabilities required to embrace emerging technologies, improve productivity and drive innovation. It will also support the future development and utilisation of the Mid South West Agri Bio Innovation Centre as a focal point for innovation, technology adoption and business growth. The programme must complement and align with the wider LEP Action Plan themes, namely Land Availability and Development and Business Workspace Development, while creating a pipeline of innovation-ready businesses capable of engaging with the future services, facilities and opportunities provided through the Agri Bio Innovation Centre. The programme should support businesses to identify and adopt practical solutions that enhance competitiveness, sustainability and operational performance. The Council seeks to appoint a suitably qualified and experienced contractor to design and deliver a comprehensive Future Focused Technologies Programme that addresses identified skills gaps in business fundamentals, digital capability, automation, productivity improvement and emerging technologies. The programme will provide bespoke support to businesses operating within the agri-food sector and rural economy, enabling them to adopt future-focused technologies including Artificial Intelligence (AI), automation, Agri-Tech, digital systems and green technologies. Through tailored business support, diagnostics and action planning, the programme will strengthen business resilience, improve productivity, foster innovation and contribute to sustainable economic growth across the Borough, whilst supporting the strategic objectives and long-term success of the Agri Bio Innovation Centre.

records.title: Updating the QualitTEE model
records.description:
To support councils in assessing these requirements, RED Scientific developed an Excel-based decision-support tool, known as QualiTEE. The tool enables users to evaluate and compare different collection scenarios against the four exemption criteria using a combination of economic, environmental, technical and material quality considerations. 
During 2025 and 2026, WRAP has been working with RED Scientific to develop the tool and develop supporting guidance. records.title: Skerryvore Lighthouse Major Refurbishment
records.description:
The NLB are seeking to appoint a Principal Contactor to plan and manage the full refurbishment of Skerryvore Lighthouse, the works are expected to take around 4 years working in the summer months only, with the contractors living in a camp based on Hynish, Tiree. The works will be in 5 distinct phases.  
Camp Set Up
The Principal Contractor  will be required to set up a semi-permanent site camp, with designated site office,  welfare facilities and lie in accommodation for the duration of the project. 
Strip-Out.
The eleven-storey granite tower is to be completely stripped out back to bare stone. This will include the removal of existing steel fuel tanks, water tanks, all partitions, diesel generators and all fixtures and fittings. The internal walls of the tower have previously been sprayed with Gunite, and asbestos containing material, as part of the initial strip out a registered asbestos removal company will require to be sub-contracted to removal all remaining traces of the Gunite on each floor.
Solar Installation.
The new Optic for Skerryvore it to be solar powered. To do this a cantilevered aluminium platform will be erected from the lighthouse balcony, this will support at 24 panel solar array, also constructed from aluminium. The solar gain will charge a battery bank housed in one of the 11 levels which will in turn run the optic. At this stage a new aluminium access platform will also be installed at the entrance level.
Domestic Installation
Stage three will be the domestic installation for both power and water supply/drainage. Power will be generated through a small generator and supplemented by any surplus solar power. New fuel tanks and supply lines will be installed. The water supply will be using an unvented cylinder, storage tanks and a house pump.
Fit out and Decoration
The final stage of the project will be the establishment of welfare, bedrooms, kitchen and decoration internally where required and externally at the lightroom.

records.buyer: Improvement and Development Agency for Local Government (IDeA)
records.title: Learning from Section 75 agreements that have ended
records.description:
This project will identify the practical implications of "uncoupling" Section 75 (S.75) agreements made by health and social care partners and will identify, test, and disseminate best practice approaches for managing transition and mitigating risk.
The work will examine the organisational, operational, cultural, financial, legal and governance impacts arising when integrated arrangements established under Section 75 of the National Health Service Act 2006 are reduced, reconfigured, or terminated.
Through evidence gathering, facilitated peer learning, practical support and publication of findings, the project will support local authorities, NHS organisations, and integrated care systems to navigate uncoupling processes in ways that safeguard outcomes for people who draw on care and support whilst maintaining organisational and partnership sustainability.
The work will commence in December 2026 and complete at the end of March 2027.
This project is funded in whole or in part by grant funding provided by the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) to the Improvement and Development Agency for Local Government (IDeA).
The award of this contract and any payments under it are conditional upon IDeA maintaining in force a Grant Funding Agreement with DHSC covering the relevant Funding Period.
In the event that:
•	the Grant Funding Agreement is not executed,
•	funding is reduced, withheld, suspended, or terminated, or
•	IDeA is required by DHSC to vary or terminate delivery of the relevant Funded Activities.
IDeA reserves the right to vary, suspend or terminate this contract on written notice without liability beyond payment for services properly delivered up to the date of termination.

records.description:
Hywel Dda University Health Board (HDUHB) are looking to commission a service provider to deliver a digital intervention for Level 2 Weight Management service for adults, supporting them to lose and maintain a healthier weight, which will form an integral part of the local weight management care pathway. This will form an essential part of a programme of work which falls under the MyPath Cymru work
The Health Board was successful, alongside national partners, in securing innovation UK grant funding, for the Obesity Pathway Innovation Programme. Locally MyPath Cymru will link a commissioned level 2 digital service, enhanced clinical and dietic support, safe access to medication for an initial cohort of up to 100 eligible adults, healthy coaching and community-based support

It will ensure that those living in our most deprived communities have the greatest access to services, whilst balancing the access needs of those who are likely to benefit from the intervention, i.e., have an identified health risk or linked to a clinical pathway. 
As the Commissioner, HDUHB expects to build an effective and strong working relationship with the Service Provider, with shared values and vision regarding the delivery of this contract. The Commissioner intends to purchase a pre-agreed number of participant places within the available contract budget. records.title: London Gateway - Second Rail Terminal Phase 2
records.description:
Description
DP World is undertaking the expansion of its London Gateway Port facility at Stanford le
Hope, through the development of a new second rail terminal located to the west of the
existing eastern operational rail facility. This investment will significantly increase the
port's rail freight capacity, improve operational resilience, and support the continued
growth of DP Worlds sustainable, low carbon logistics solutions.
This expansion represents a strategic enhancement of the port's intermodal capability,
enabling faster, more efficient movement of goods across the UK and supporting national
objectives for greener freight transport. The new terminal will play a key role in
accommodating future demand and maintaining London Gateway's position as a world
class logistics and supply chain hub.
The Scope of Works covered under this tender include, but are not limited to, the following
key elements:
Permanent Way Works
Construction of new railway infrastructure to serve the second terminal including plain line
track, and associated components in a phase installation sequence delivering five new
sidings (7 to 11) to compliment the two sidings (12 and 13) already constructed during Phase 1/1A of the works, which are currently in operation. Installation and integration of
21 new switches and crossings (S&C) required to connect the new terminal to the existing
rail network corridor as well as providing more route paths for trains entering and exiting
the existing eastern rail terminal.
Civil Engineering Works
Installation of a circa 850m long reinforced concrete crane rail beam with pre-cast
concrete pile foundations and its associated mechanical chambers to allow Rail Mounted
Gantry Crane (RMGC) operations within the new terminal. Earthworks, formation
preparation, track drainage and utility diversions necessary to support the new terminal
infrastructure. Construction of numerous ancillary civils foundation bases, walkways,
cable routes and under track crossings for the new signalling, telecommunications and
electrical plant equipment, shunters cabin and REB building.
Telecommunications Works
Installation of new and relocation of existing Operational Telecoms and SiSS systems
assets including CCTV cameras, signal post and point zone telephones and the shunters
panel concentrator.
Signaling Works
Provision of new and relocation of existing signaling assets, including lineside equipment,
control system modifications in the form of new Shunters Cabin housing an updated
control panel to operate both rail terminals, and associated REB for the signaling system
interlocking. These assets will be constructed in a staged delivery to align with the
permanent way phasing, to ensure full operational compatibility. Installation of new
signaling track circuits to both the western and eastern terminals will enable operation of
both facilities from the one new control panel. Testing, commissioning and integration of
all new rail systems with existing operational infrastructure as well as update to the
Upminster IECC workstation screens.
Electrical and Plant Works
New power supplies to the various disciplines line side equipment, shunters cabin and
REB, as well as new points heating assets for both the western and existing eastern rail
terminal S&C units.
Interfaces and Integration
Management of all interfaces with existing rail infrastructure, port operations, utilities, and
third party stakeholders. Development of staging plans to minimise operational disruption
and ensure safe working adjacent to live rail and port environments. Coordination with existing port operations to ensure safe and continuous functionality during construction.
Project Goals
Upon completion, the new rail terminal will provide; increased rail served capacity for
containerised freight, enhanced operational flexibility and resilience, deliver infrastructure
capable of supporting robotic next generation RMGC equipment and improved efficiency
as well as reduce the ports carbon impact through expanded rail freight capability.

records.title: Responsive Repairs and Void Works Framework
records.description:
Irwell Valley Homes (IVH) is seeking to establish an open framework for the provision of repairs and maintenance services in property owned, controlled or occupied by IVH. IVH provides a wide range of inhouse maintenance and repair services but also requires a reliable supplier network to support the IVH repairs team.
The Framework will have one (1) Lot, with options to add further Lots in the future.
Lot 1 - Responsive Repairs and Void Works
Responsive Repairs - Day to Day Responsive Repairs including Emergency Work arising during the normal working hours of the day
Void Works - Any repairs, renewals, reinstatement, replacement, internal redecoration, upgrading, cleaning and clearing out ordered in accordance with the provisions of the Contract arising as a result of a change of tenancy. IVH will carry out "Void Property Inspections". This means inspection of the Void Property to establish what Works are required. Once scoped and priced the Work would then be passed to the Supplier to complete with a target completion date.
The framework will appoint three contractors to deliver services over a two (2) year term, with an optional one (1) year extension, with options to re-open annually. Any decision regarding the re-opening of the framework remains entirely at the discretion of IVH and will be exercised in accordance with its strategic and operational requirements which may change during the initial set term of the framework.

records.title: Open Framework for Prevention Accommodation and Housing Support Services
records.description:
Rochdale Borough Council, acting on behalf of itself and its partners, is seeking to establish an Open Framework for Prevention Accommodation and Housing Support Services aimed at preventing homelessness, promoting independence and improving housing outcomes for vulnerable residents.
The Framework will provide a range of accommodation-based and housing-related support services for children, young people, young parents, women and adults with varying support needs. Services will include supported accommodation, housing-related support, outreach provision, tenancy sustainment, homelessness prevention interventions and planned move-on support into independent living.
The procurement is divided into four Lots. Successful providers will be required to deliver flexible, person-centred, strengths-based services that support individuals to access and maintain safe and suitable accommodation, develop independent living skills and achieve sustainable housing outcomes.
Lots 1, 2 and 4 require providers to supply and manage suitable accommodation alongside support services. Lot 3 requires providers to secure and sustain access to suitable accommodation, including private rented sector and supportive living arrangements, supported by effective tenancy sustainment and bond guarantee arrangements.
The estimated total value of the Framework is £5,310,000 over the Framework term. Providers may apply for one or more Lots and may be appointed to multiple Lots. Services will be commissioned on an outcomes-focused basis, with performance measures linked to homelessness prevention, tenancy sustainment, move-on outcomes and service user wellbeing.

This procurement is for a Contract, which is an exempted contract under s 3(6) and Schedule 2, Part 2 (Subject-matter exempted contracts), paragraph 22 (Research and Development Services) of the Procurement Act 2023 (the 'Act').
Exempted contracts are not public contracts as defined in s3 of the Act and therefore are not required to be procured in accordance with the provisions of the Act that relate to a covered procurement.
For this procurement the Authority has operated a transparent competition process, to which any potential supplier was able to respond. In doing so the procurement process has reflected processes and requirements set out in the Act in relation to covered procurements, or elements thereof. This commitment to transparency includes the publication of this notice, for information, on Find a Tender.
The UK Active Debris Removal Phase 3 Research and Development Service (ADR Mission) is a UK national project that aims to support the In-Orbit Servicing and Manufacturing ("ISAM") and Sustainability priorities set out in the UK Space Agency's Corporate Plan as well as the National Space Strategy (NSS) ambitions to lead the global effort to make space more sustainable.
The ADR Mission requires the safe capture and subsequent removal of two UK-licensed defunct satellites in the congested LEO region (Client Satellites) by the Servicer Satellite.
Through this Procurement, the Authority has selected one Supplier to deliver the UK ADR Mission.

records.buyer: NHS HAMPSHIRE AND THE ISLE OF WIGHT INTEGRATED CARE BOARD
records.title: Carers Support Services
records.description:
The service aims to provide high-quality support for carers that is accessible, equitable and responsive to the needs of our local Isle of Wight population.
The service will be delivered to carers resident on the Isle of Wight, ensuring timely access to information, advice, and guidance during a cared-for person's acute hospital admission-whether for physical or mental health needs. Its purpose is to improve outcomes, experiences, and long-term resilience, helping individuals remain in their chosen place of residence for longer, reducing reliance on statutory services, and delaying or preventing permanent admission to residential care. The provider will offer care that is standardised, transparent and coordinated, enabling carers to feel supported throughout the acute stay of their cared for individual, receive optimal interventions and support the first time, and experience improved independence and ability to remain in or return to their caring responsibilities.
A collaborative approach involving all stakeholders in the health and social care pathway will be essential to ensure equitable outcomes and a positive experience for both carers and cared for individuals.

records.title: Healthcare and Forensic Services in Custody (Ref. 049-POL-24)
records.description:
West Yorkshire Combined Authority (WYCA) as the Contracting Authority ("CA") for West Yorkshire Police (WYP) has awarded a single Provider Contract for the provision of Healthcare and Forensic Services in Custody. The CA tendered this requirement in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023, following the Competitive Flexible Procedure.
The Supplier is required to deliver a high quality and cost effective service, which meets the healthcare requirements of detainees and assists with the recovery of forensic evidence, whilst working to reduce re-offending.
The Supplier must deliver a 24/7/365 embedded service in all Force custody suites, at;
- Elland Rd (Leeds DHQ)
- Trafalgar House (Bradford)
- Halifax (Calderdale)
- Dewsbury (Kirklees HQ) 
- Havertop (Wakefield DHQ)
There is also a resilience suite at Stainbeck (Leeds) and an Overspill Suite at Pudsey (Leeds) which are occasionally used.
Plus the North East Counter Terrorism Unit (CTU) is also based in West Yorkshire.
The CA requires Healthcare Professionals (HCP) to be embedded at each of the five custody suites. One additional HCP is required as peripatetic cover, referred to locally as resilience cover, to work across all custody suites providing additional assistance and support as required by fluctuations in demand for service. The peripatetic HCP will initially be based at Trafalgar House Bradford custody suite when not required to provide cover/assistance at any of the other custody suites, however this may change during the term of the Contract.
CTU require the initial assessment of TACT detainees to be carried out by an FME.  Subsequent assessments, however, can be undertaken by HCPs. There may also be other exceptional occurrences where an FME is deemed necessary to undertake an assessment instead of a HCP. A Pay As You Go (PAYG) model for FME's is required instead of an embedded/on-call FME model included in the annual service cost.
The service will be supported by an online booking system for the request of healthcare services, triaging & prioritising the order of calls and allocation of assessments to the correct HCP.
The Contract commenced 25th September 2026 and will expire 30th September 2031, with the provision to extend for a further period, or successive periods, up to 30th September 2036.

records.buyer: Corporate Officer of the House of Commons
records.title: Built Environment Consultancy Services (BECS) Framework
records.description:
UK Parliament is responsible for the operation and maintenance of the Parliamentary Estate, which comprises a diverse portfolio of historic, listed and modern buildings and infrastructure. The Estate provides a working environment for both Houses of Parliament and supports the delivery of parliamentary business, as well as providing facilities for Members, staff and visitors.
Typical works focus on conservation of fabric, capital asset upgrade and replacement, mechanical, electrical and public health works, digital, telecoms, security and access systems and utilities. Further information about UK Parliament and the Parliamentary Estate can be found at https://www.parliament.uk/.
BECS covers the provision of a range of consultancy services, including Project Management (PM), Cost Management (CM), Multidisciplinary Design Services (MDS), Feasibility, Commercial and Registered Building Control services. The required services will support of major and minor construction works, building refurbishment, building security and infrastructure security.
The BECS framework is intended to support current and future portfolios of capital investment and capital maintenance projects for UK Parliament. The services expected under BECS will range from early-stage feasibility assessments, through to delivery and management of Works projects and programmes. The scale, complexity and nature of Works at Parliament require access to a suitably experienced and capable professional services supply chain.

records.title: Learning and Competency Management System
records.description:
Shropshire Fire and Rescue Service (SFRS) is undertaking Preliminary Market Engagement to develop its understanding of the market for the provision of a modern Learning and Competency Management System.
SFRS is exploring solutions that could support the management, delivery and oversight of learning, skills, qualifications, and competency across the Service. This includes learning management, competency and assessment management, reporting and management information, integration and interoperability, information security, accessibility, implementation, data migration, and ongoing support.
SFRS is also interested in understanding the availability of additional functionality relating to quality assurance, ePortfolio and evidence management, and individual performance and development reviews.
The purpose of this engagement is to understand the solutions and delivery models currently available, supplier capability, technological developments, implementation considerations, and indicative commercial and licensing models. The information obtained will be used to help SFRS refine its requirements, undertake options appraisal, and inform its procurement strategy.
SFRS is currently considering G-Cloud 15 (RM1557.15) as a potential route to market. No final decision has been made regarding the procurement route or the solution that may ultimately be required.
This Preliminary Market Engagement does not constitute the commencement of a procurement procedure or a commitment by SFRS to undertake a subsequent procurement.
Suppliers should submit their completed RFI through In-tend and all clarification correspondence should be managed through the portal.

records.title: Equipment - The Paddocks
records.description:
This capital procurement project represents a strategic investment in the health, fitness, and modern infrastructure of the council's leisure portfolio. It focuses specifically on the targeted acquisition of equipment assets across two distinct work streams
1. The Paddocks (Lot 1): A completely new fitness installation requiring standard premium cardio and fixed resistance equipment (Lot 1) 
2. The Paddocks (Lot 2): Deployment of fully automated, advanced digital strength and diagnostic equipment featuring real-time data streaming and NHS reporting integration. The infrastructure demands high-durability hardware capable of supporting automated user tracking, data-driven facility management, and direct synchronisation with exercise referral clinical metrics. (Lot 2) 
3. Runnymede Leisure Centre (Lot 1): Cardiovascular replacement consisting strictly of premium cardiovascular equipment upgrades. (Lot 1) 
4. The Paddocks (Lot 3): A dedicated suite of power-assisted, continuous motion exercise machines equipped with digital cloud connectivity software. This equipment is specifically engineered for inclusive rehabilitation, active aging, community health referral pathways, and users with limited mobility or long-term health conditions. (Lot 3)
The existing assets at Runnymede Leisure Centre have reached the end of their operational lifespan, resulting in increased maintenance overheads and a decline in user experience. Simultaneously, the development at The Paddocks requires a highly sophisticated setup to attract and retain members while supporting targeted health and physical progression initiatives.
Rather than relying on legacy hardware configurations or static, unmonitored equipment, the Authority is prioritising a forward-thinking, data-driven approach to gym management. By introducing automated biometric tracking and high-precision physical diagnostics alongside premium traditional fitness lines, the council aims to drive member engagement, reduce member attrition, and optimise overall facility performance.
Options Appraisal
1. Continued Maintenance of Legacy Hardware: Rejected. Continuing to repair out-of-warranty machinery or relocating aging equipment to new sites is financially non-viable. It fails to meet modern public expectations, incurs high ad-hoc maintenance costs, and does not provide the tracking capabilities required for contemporary data-driven health strategies.
2. Unified Multi-Vendor Bulk Purchase: Rejected. Attempting to bundle specialised digital diagnostic ecosystems and standard mechanical gym equipment into a single, generic lot restricts competitive bidding. It prevents the Authority from strictly specifying the unique software integrations required for real-time strength progression tracking and cloud-based user diagnostics.
3. Split-Lot Framework Procurement (Preferred Framework): The procurement is divided into three distinct, specialised Lots. This strategy allows the Authority to independently evaluate best-in-class manufacturers for traditional cardiovascular and mechanical resistance machinery (Lot 1) while establishing exact technical criteria to secure a highly specialised, closed-loop digital strength circuit and automated onboarding ecosystem that links in with NHS (Lot 2).
4.  Acquire a state-of-the-art power-assisted, digitally connected physical therapy and active health circuit designed for inclusive access, rehabilitation, and active aging (Lot 3)

records.title: From Local Shocks to Systemic Impacts: A Multi-hazard, Systems-based View of Physical Climate Risk
records.description:
Please provide a detailed description of the notice you are adding: 
The final date and time for the submission of bids is Wednesday, 14th October 2026 at 11:00 
DO NOT apply directly to the buyer. 
All tender information MUST be submitted through the Jaggaer eSourcing Portal. 
Brief Description of Requirement
It is broadly recognised that physical climate risk and related nature dependencies can pose risks to economic and financial stability. Governments and regulators in the UK and internationally have recognised this and continue to take action to address underlying vulnerabilities and support wider systemic resilience. Notwithstanding the clear need for accelerated global action, there remains significant uncertainties in appraising the future economic and financial implications of physical risk meaning market practices, government policy and regulation, may not be optimised (within the bounds of wider limitations and mandates) to align with climate-resilient pathways. 
Climate scenario analysis is a key tool to inform approaches to climate risk management. But due to the complexity and heterogeneity of climate risk, academic and industry evidence has highlighted that current mainstream scenarios – whilst highly sophisticated – may not capture all potential physical risk due to limited data availability and modelling constraints. Furthermore, whilst reference scenarios continue to be enhanced, some potential hazard exposures and highly complex systems dynamics may not be well suited to quantification through empirically calibrated, top-down damage functions, which provide estimates for economic damages in climate scenarios.  
There is, therefore, a need to investigate the potential for complementary methodologies to support more holistic approaches to physical risk appraisal and management. This is the focus of this research project.  
Specifically, research will focus on how local physical climate shocks (e.g. storms, flooding, droughts, heat stress) can - through cascading, compounding, and contagion effects - become systemic risks. There will be a particular focus on furthering understanding of UK vulnerabilities to climate shocks in other countries, with the objective of supporting improvements to industry practices and providing insights for government policy, regulation, and prudential supervision. 
This research project will be delivered in coordination with the Financial Conduct Authority’s Climate Scenarios Sandbox , with potential for insights generated through the sandbox to provide practical evidence regarding the utility of research outputs. The project will also be delivered in partnership with the recently established UK Taskforce on Climate and Nature Security  and will, where possible, be aligned with ongoing work on high-impact climate possibilities at the Climate Financial Risk Forum.

records.title: Coal Mining Risk Assessment
records.description:
Severn Trent Water Limited (STW) intends to establish a multi-supplier framework agreement for Coal Mining Risk Assessment.
The framework will support both planned and reactive work.
STW is seeking to understand market appetite and capability in advance of finalising the procurement strategy. The scope and structure of the framework may therefore be refined following this engagement.
STW intends to establish a framework agreement for the delivery of Coal Mining Risk Assessments.
The scope of services is expected to include but not limited to:
• Present a desk-based review of all available information on the potential coal mining hazards which are relevant to the site;
• Use that information to identify and assess the hazards to the proposed development from coal mining legacy, including any cumulative impact;
• Set out the necessary mitigation measures or works that will need to be adopted to enable safe development;
• Provide information to input into a Coal Authority permit application to disturb or enter coal mining interests and any subsequent licences and/or agreements that may be needed for construction
The framework will support both planned programmes and reactive requirements.
STW is undertaking this procurement to establish a multi-supplier framework capable of Coal Mining Risk Assessments.
STW is particularly interested in understanding how suppliers can support efficient, repeatable delivery and consistent performance outcomes.
The scope and structure of the framework may be refined following this notice and subsequent market engagement.

This Contract Award Notice relates to Procurement Reference DN797809 - East Cliff Stabilisation Works (FTS Unique Identifier: ocds-h6vhtk-05f6a1).
The procurement was originally advertised as a below-threshold competitive procurement based on the estimated contract value available at the time of publication. records.title: Omni-channel Communications Platform
records.description:
Manchester City Council  is undertaking a pre-market engagement exercise to explore Omni-Channel Communications platform capable of supporting the Council’s future telephony and contact centre requirements. The exercise will help MCC understand available solutions, delivery approaches, integration options and indicative commercial models before determining any future procurement approach.
The Council currently operates a hybrid telephony environment supporting approximately 4,300 users, comprising around 1,600 users on 8x8 and 2,700 users on Microsoft Teams Telephony. 8x8 provides the underlying telephony infrastructure and contact centre functionality required to support both Microsoft Teams users and users who remain directly on the 8x8 platform, predominantly within the Council’s contact centre services.
The current solution also includes handset provision and PCI Pal for call masking and secure payment functionality, supporting the Council’s wider operational, telephony and contact centre requirements.
This engagement is intended to help the Council better understand current market capabilities, inform its procurement approach, and shape the specification for a future tender process. The demonstration sessions will provide insight into the functionality of proposed systems, the benefits delivered, and any planned enhancements or additional capabilities suppliers may offer.
The intended outcome of this exercise is to provide the Council with a better understanding of available solutions, implementation considerations, integration capabilities, indicative costs, and supplier experience within local government and organisations of comparable size and complexity.

records.buyer: The Council of the Borough of Kirklees
records.title: KMCAS-226 Provision of Scheme Management, Care & Support Extra Care Schemes
records.description:
The three Extra Care Schemes in Kirklees are part of a 20 year Private Finance Initiative (PFI) contract with a consortium of companies called JLW Excellent Homes for Life Ltd. 
The schemes provide 140 flats for older people: Two schemes, Meadow Green, incorporating Meadow Green Lodge and Woodland Court are in North Kirklees and one, Sandy Mount is in South Kirklees.  They comprise purpose built buildings containing between 41 and 53 one and two-bedroom flats, all of which are for rent.  
The Council is the owner and the landlord.  JLW Excellent Homes for Life Ltd through their key sub-contractor Pinnacle are responsible for the repair and maintenance of the building and also manage the tenancies of the flats on behalf of the Council.
The Council expects that the Service Provider will work with the PFI Contractor, Catering Contractor and all other stakeholders to achieve the following overall aims of the Extra Care Schemes:
• To provide a safe, comfortable, welcoming and inclusive environment for Tenants, their families and friends and other visitors to the Scheme.
• To promote the maximum level of independence achievable by the individual. 
• To have an enabling ethos providing ‘just the right support at just the right time’, either planned or unplanned and to avoid disabling Tenants and therefore increasing dependency on services. 
• To support Tenants to maintain their tenancies and remain in their own home which is designed to be a ‘home for life’.
• To support Tenants to regain and maintain their health and wellbeing and to reduce hospital admissions and facilitate speedy hospital discharge whenever possible.
• To give assurance that Tenants can quickly access additional care and support if and when needed due to emergency, illness, accident and so on.
• To support Tenants to be active, both physically and mentally by facilitating a range of Activities and encouraging participation.
• To signpost or link Tenants into appropriate services and community activities outside the Scheme.
In addition - The Extra Care Schemes also aim to be a community resource and some of the Communal Areas and Activities are open for hire or use by the public.
The estimated value of the Services to be awarded is approximately £6,578,138 (exclusive of Value Added Tax) 
VAT not applicable for this Service
Please refer to the Price Information in relation to the estimated values.  Tenderers must note that the amount of planned care hours varies constantly depending on Service User needs.  Tenderers must also note that Service Users can choose other options for the delivery of their planned care e.g. an off-site care provider or a direct payment.

The scope of works includes: • Completion of the technical design; • Completion of the works of a mix of accommodation types, ancillary staff facilities and car parking upgrade work; • Completion of the associated car parking, landscaping, and site works; and • Completion of the associated utilities, services, roads, and drainage infrastructure. This includes coordination of all design disciplines to ensure compliance with statutory and regulatory requirements.

records.title: Paper and Card Processing Services
records.description:
Kent County Council (KCC), as the Waste Disposal Authority, has a statutory responsibility to arrange for the disposal of paper and card collected at kerbside by the Waste Collection Authorities, and for paper and card deposited by residents at Household Waste Recycling Centres.
Existing contracts are due to expire on 30 November 2026. This procurement seeks to establish new countywide contractual arrangements commencing on 1 December 2026.
Through its contracts with third party waste transfer providers, KCC will deliver material to the provider’s processing facility. The appointed provider will be responsible for the reception, handling, storage, and processing of all paper and card received under the contract, ensuring full compliance with environmental, regulatory and quality standards.
KCC is currently achieving a landfill diversion rate of 99%, with all separately collected paper and card being recycled rather than disposed of. This performance is supported by an established network of transfer and processing arrangements, ensuring materials are directed to appropriate recycling facilities.
Output materials must meet relevant industry standards for recycled paper and board, including EN643 for recovered paper, and must be suitable for reprocessing into new paper products. Providers must also comply with all applicable quality protocols and end of waste criteria.
The provider must maintain a comprehensive reporting and audit trail for all materials processed, from receipt through to final destination, and supply accurate and timely data to KCC to support performance monitoring and statutory reporting requirements.
No paper and card managed under this contract may be disposed of at landfill. All material must be recycled or otherwise recovered in accordance with the waste hierarchy and KCC’s zero to landfill objective.
The estimated contract volume is approximately 30,000 tonnes per annum. This figure is indicative only and no minimum tonnage guarantee is provided.
This procurement will comprise a single lot.
The initial contract term will be five years, with the option to extend for up to two further years, subject to performance and mutual agreement.
