records.title: Tender for Residential and Nursing Care Home Partnership Framework in Herefordshire
records.description:
Herefordshire Council is seeking to establish a multi-provider Care Home Partnerships Framework for the provision of residential care, nursing care and other associated care home services for adults with eligible care and support needs (the 'Services').
This procurement establishes an Open Framework Scheme under section 49 of the Procurement Act 2023.  This Tender Notice relates to the opportunity to apply for admission to the first Herefordshire Care Home Partnerships Framework (the Framework) within the Open Framework Scheme.
The Framework will support the delivery of long-term partnership arrangements between the Council and care home providers. The Services under the Open Framework Scheme and the Framework are 'light touch' as defined by section 9 of the Procurement Act 2023 and are governed by the rules relating to light touch contracts under the Procurement Act 2023.
The Framework will be available to residential and nursing care providers operating eligible care home services and is intended to support approximately 700 to 750 Council-funded placements at any one time across the market, with an anticipated 500 to 550 placements being delivered through formal partnership arrangements.
The Council has a Partnership and Provider Support Programme which this Open Framework Scheme is part of. The programme is an initiative for all providers commissioned through the Community Wellbeing Directorate of Herefordshire Council and is designed to support genuine collaborative working between Herefordshire Council and providers, promoting high-quality services, improved resident outcomes and a sustainable local care market. Providers admitted to the Framework may participate as a Framework Provider, Partner Provider or Strategic Partner Provider. Eligibility for each level is determined by the applicable Framework requirements, including any required commitment of capacity at the tendered Partnership Rate. Different levels of participation attract different engagement, development and support opportunities.
The Open Framework will have a maximum duration of eight years and an estimated maximum value of approximately £484 million over the full term. The Council does not guarantee that the Open Framework Scheme will continue for the full term of 8 years and no guarantee is given as to the actual value of any framework agreement under the Open Framework Scheme, or any call-off contracts entered under any framework agreement.
The Open Framework Scheme will be re-opened to new providers at least once in the first three years following the award of the first Framework and at least once during each subsequent five-year period until the expiry of the scheme. Herefordshire Council reserves the right to re-open the Open Framework Scheme at additional intervals where it considers this necessary to support market development, increase provider participation, respond to changes in service demand, address emerging care needs, encourage innovation or maintain sufficient capacity across the sector.
Neither admission to the framework nor any ranking or partnership designation guarantees a minimum number or value of placements. Placements remain subject to assessed need, suitability, resident choice, capacity, the applicable call-off mechanism and the Council's statutory duties.
The Council has considered the use of lots and has structured the procurement into lots reflecting the categories of care required by Herefordshire residents. The service is divided into 2 Lots, under which there are Categories of Care for which providers are required for submit a tender for.  These are:
Lot 1 - Older Persons Residential and Nursing Care
Lot 2 - Working Age Adults
Each Lot contains specific Categories of Care which must be applied for separately. Providers will be evaluated for admission to each lot against the published conditions of participation and award criteria, including quality and price, using the weightings and methodology set out in the tender documents. Individual placements will subsequently be allocated in accordance with the published placement process, taking account of assessed need, suitability, availability, lawful resident choice, Provider Status and Provider Ranked Score.
Across both lots, placements will be subject to assessed need, suitability, availability and lawful resident choice. Eligible care homes will normally be considered in order of Provider Status, then Provider Ranked Score within each level. For Lot 2 (Working Age Adults), matching will reflect specialist support requirements and relevant family and community connections, with searches extended beyond Herefordshire where suitable local provision is unavailable. Any objectively justified departure from the normal placement order will be recorded.
The Council is seeking to award multiple contracts to eligible providers who meet the requirements for each of the Lots. Bidders are referred to the invitation to tender document for full details as it contains specific rules on how bidders may submit their response. Providers may be awarded multiple Lots. Subject to satisfying the conditions of participation and award criteria applicable to the relevant lot and Category of Care (as defined in the invitation to tender), there is no maximum number of providers that may be admitted to a particular Lot under the Framework.
Bidders are referred to the invitation to tender and procurement documentation for full details.

records.title: National Construction Framework
records.description:
Wirral Council (as the Contracting Authority) and Procure Partnerships Framework (Framework Manager) are conducting market research to gauge the level of market interest and inform the procurement strategy to let a four-year National Contractor Framework, as defined by The Procurement Act 2023. The Framework is expected to go live on 13th October 2027.
The Framework is intended to provide public sector Contracting Authorities across all English regions with access to suitably qualified Contractors capable of delivering construction, fit-out and mechanical & electrical (M&E) projects across a range of sectors and project values.
The Framework, which is being delivered and managed by Procure Partnerships Framework, is expected to support the delivery of works under Design and Build and Build Only arrangements, using Two Stage, Single Stage and Direct Award procurement routes, and embracing both NEC and JCT forms of contract. Call-off contracts may extend beyond the expiry of the Framework.
The Framework is expected to include three Lot types: Construction, Fit-out, and Mechanical & Electrical (M&E).
The Framework will be structured on a regional and sub-regional basis across England, with every Lot defined by NUTS codes. Small to medium works Construction Lots will be split into sub-regional areas, enabling delivery through locally experienced partners, including small and medium-sized enterprises, with knowledge of local markets and supply chains. Higher-value Lots will cover wider regional areas.
Potential Framework users may therefore include but are not limited to: Local authorities and combined authorities, NHS Trusts and NHS organisations, Universities and further education institutions, Housing associations, Schools, Academies and Colleges, Blue Light/Emergency Services, Health and Social Care Bodies, Libraries and Museums, Registered Charities and Government Departments.
Organisations eligible to use the Framework are listed at https://www.procurepartnerships.co.uk/eligible-users. Any other contracting authority (as defined by the Procurement Act 2023) in England will also be able to use the Framework.
The Framework will provide Contracting Authorities with the ability to process appointments using Direct Award, Two Stage and Single Stage competition mechanisms.
It is anticipated that up to 12 Suppliers will be appointed to each Lot.
Contracting Authorities will be able to make a Direct Award to any Supplier appointed to a Lot of the same Lot type and value band, provided the award is made in accordance with the core terms and the objective mechanism for supplier selection set out in the framework, pursuant to Section 45(4)(b) of the Procurement Act 2023.
Where fewer than four Suppliers express interest in a competition, the Contracting Authority may also invite Suppliers appointed to an adjacent Lot of the same Lot type and value band. Adjacent Lots will be defined in the procurement documents.
The Framework’s lotting structure is anticipated to include:
Construction - Delivery of new build and construction works across England, excluding the North West, which is covered separately under Wirral Council’s North West Contractor Framework for general construction Lots, also managed by Procure Partnerships Framework. Construction is expected to comprise 69 Lots across six value bands.
Construction value bands: £50k - £500k, £500k - £2m, £2m - £10m, £10m - £20m, £20m - £40m, £40m+.
£50k - £500k, £500k - £2m and £2m - £10m (15 Lots per value band): Northumberland, Tyne & Wear (UKC2); Tees Valley & Durham (UKC1); West & North Yorkshire (UKE2, UKE4); South Yorkshire & the Humber (UKE1, UKE3); East Midlands Corridor (UKF1, UKF2); Lincolnshire (UKF3); West Midlands (UKG); East Anglia (UKH1); Bedfordshire & Hertfordshire (UKH2); Essex (UKH3); London (UKI); Kent, Surrey & Sussex (UKJ2, UKJ4); Thames Valley & Hampshire (UKJ1, UKJ3); West of England, Gloucestershire, Wiltshire & Somerset (UKK1, UKK23); Devon, Cornwall & Dorset (UKK21, UKK22, UKK3, UKK4).
£10m - £20m (13 Lots): as above, except that the North East (UKC) and Yorkshire & the Humber (UKE) each form a single Lot.
£20m - £40m (8 Lots): North East (UKC); Yorkshire & the Humber (UKE); East Midlands (UKF); West Midlands (UKG); East of England (UKH); London (UKI); South East (UKJ); South West (UKK).
£40m+ (3 Lots): North (UKC, UKE); Midlands (UKF, UKG); South (UKH, UKI, UKJ, UKK).
Fit-out - Delivery of fit-out works, including internal refurbishment and alteration, across all English regions including the North West. Fit-out is expected to comprise 27 Lots: three value bands, each with a Lot for each of the nine English regions.
Fit-out value bands: £50k - £2m, £2m - £20m, £20m+.
Mechanical & Electrical (M&E) - Delivery of mechanical and electrical installation, replacement and upgrade works, including building services and decarbonisation-related M&E works, across all English regions including the North West. M&E is expected to comprise 27 Lots on the same basis as Fit-out.
M&E value bands: £50k - £2m, £2m - £20m, £20m+.
Fit-out and M&E Lots (all value bands): North East (UKC); North West (UKD); Yorkshire & the Humber (UKE); East Midlands (UKF); West Midlands (UKG); East of England (UKH); London (UKI); South East (UKJ); South West (UKK).
In total, the Framework is anticipated to comprise 123 Lots (Construction 69, Fit-out 27, M&E 27).

records.title: English Language Testing_ licensing of Private Hire and Pedicab drivers
records.description:
Preliminary Market Engagement Notice
English Language Testing Services for Taxi and Private Hire Driver Licensing
Background
Transport for London (TfL) is undertaking a Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) exercise to better understand the current market for English Language Testing (ELT) services used to support the licensing of Private Hire and Pedicab drivers in London.
TfL currently requires applicants for either a private hire or pedicab driver licence to demonstrate English language speaking and listening skills at an appropriate level. As part of future service planning, TfL wishes to engage with the market to gain a comprehensive understanding of available solutions, supplier capability, technological developments, commercial models and emerging best practice within this sector.
The current service arrangement is expected to continue until September 2027, and TfL is commencing this engagement exercise to inform its future strategy and potential sourcing approach beyond that date.
Purpose of this Engagement
This Preliminary Market Engagement is being conducted solely to gather market intelligence and supplier feedback. The information obtained will assist TfL in:
•	Understanding the range of English language testing solutions currently available within the market.
•	Exploring innovative approaches to language assessment.
•	Understanding different commercial and contractual models available to contracting authorities.
•	Identifying potential suppliers capable of delivering services at the scale and standards required by TfL.
•	Assessing market appetite, capacity and capability.
•	Informing future requirements, procurement strategy and delivery options.
Scope of Interest
TfL is interested in receiving information from organisations that can provide all or part of the following services:
•	English language speaking and listening assessments aligned to recognised standards such as the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR).
•	Secure online, in-person testing solutions .
•	Fraud detection and prevention measures.
•	Test administration, marking and quality assurance processes.
•	Results management and reporting functionality.
•	Appeals and customer support services.
•	Accessibility and reasonable adjustment arrangements.
•	Data protection, cyber security and information management capabilities.
•	Management information and performance reporting.
Proposed Engagement Approach
TfL anticipates conducting market engagement activities between November and Early December 2026. These activities may include:
•	Supplier questionnaires (Market Sounding Questionnaire).
•	Industry engagement sessions.
•	Supplier presentations or demonstrations.
•	Individual clarification discussions with suppliers.
Participation in any stage of this engagement process will be voluntary.
Important Notice
This notice relates solely to Preliminary Market Engagement activities and does not constitute a call for competition, procurement exercise, tender opportunity or commitment by TfL to procure any services.
Any future procurement opportunity arising from this market engagement would be subject to separate governance approvals and would be advertised independently in accordance with applicable procurement regulations.
Participation in this engagement exercise will not provide any supplier with an advantage in any future procurement process, nor will it create any obligation on TfL to proceed with procurement or contract award.
Expression of Interest
Suppliers interested in participating in this Preliminary Market Engagement exercise are invited to express their interest and provide details of their relevant experience, solutions and capabilities. Further information regarding the engagement process and timetable will be shared with interested organisations in due course.

records.title: National Civil Engineering & Infrastructure Framework
records.description:
Wirral Council (as the Contracting Authority) and Procure Partnerships Framework (Framework Manager) are conducting market research to gauge the level of market interest and inform the procurement strategy to let a four-year Civil Engineering & Infrastructure Framework, as defined by The Procurement Act 2023. The Framework is expected to go live in October 2027.
The Framework is intended to provide public sector Contracting Authorities across England with access to suitably qualified Contractors capable of delivering civil engineering and infrastructure projects across a range of disciplines and project values.
The Framework, which is being delivered and managed by Procure Partnerships Framework, is expected to support the delivery of works under Design and Build and Build Only arrangements, using Two Stage, Single Stage and Direct Award procurement routes, and embracing both NEC and JCT forms of contract.
The Framework is expected to include five Lot types: Enabling Works and Demolition; Highways and Transport; Water, Flood Defence and Coastal Infrastructure; Utilities, Energy and Electrical Infrastructure; and Regeneration, Brownfield and Urban Infrastructure.
The Framework will be structured on a regional and sub-regional basis across England, with every Lot defined by NUTS codes. Lots up to £30m will be split into sub-regional areas, enabling delivery through locally experienced partners, including small and medium-sized enterprises, with knowledge of local markets and supply chains. Higher-value Lots will cover wider areas (North, Midlands and South).
The Framework does not include Lots for the North West of England. The North West is covered separately by the North West Contractor Framework, operated by Procure Partnerships Framework and Wirral Council on a separate procurement trajectory.
Potential Framework users may include but are not limited to: Local authorities and combined authorities, NHS Trusts and NHS organisations, Universities and further education institutions, Housing associations, Schools, Academies and Colleges, Blue Light/Emergency Services, Health and Social Care Bodies, Libraries and Museums, Registered Charities and Government Departments.
Organisations eligible to use the Framework are listed at https://www.procurepartnerships.co.uk/eligible-users. Any other contracting authority (as defined by the Procurement Act 2023) in England will also be able to use the Framework.
The Framework will provide Contracting Authorities with the ability to process appointments using Direct Award, Two Stage and Single Stage competition mechanisms.
It is anticipated that up to 12 Suppliers will be appointed to each Lot.
Contracting Authorities will be able to make a Direct Award to any Supplier appointed to a Lot of the same Lot type and value band, provided the award is made in accordance with the core terms and the objective mechanism for supplier selection set out in the framework, pursuant to Section 45(4)(b) of the Procurement Act 2023.
Where fewer than four Suppliers express interest in a competition, the Contracting Authority may also invite Suppliers appointed to an adjacent Lot of the same Lot type and value band. Adjacent Lots will be defined in the procurement documents.
Call-off contracts may extend beyond the expiry of the Framework.

records.title: Tender for Residential and Nursing Care Home Partnership Framework in Herefordshire
records.description:
Herefordshire Council is seeking to establish a multi-provider Care Home Partnerships Framework for the provision of residential care, nursing care and other associated care home services for adults with eligible care and support needs (the 'Services').
This procurement establishes an Open Framework Scheme under section 49 of the Procurement Act 2023.  This Tender Notice relates to the opportunity to apply for admission to the first Herefordshire Care Home Partnerships Framework (the Framework) within the Open Framework Scheme.
The Framework will support the delivery of long-term partnership arrangements between the Council and care home providers. The Services under the Open Framework Scheme and the Framework are 'light touch' as defined by section 9 of the Procurement Act 2023 and are governed by the rules relating to light touch contracts under the Procurement Act 2023.
The Framework will be available to residential and nursing care providers operating eligible care home services and is intended to support approximately 700 to 750 Council-funded placements at any one time across the market, with an anticipated 500 to 550 placements being delivered through formal partnership arrangements.
The Council has a Partnership and Provider Support Programme which this Open Framework Scheme is part of. The programme is an initiative for all providers commissioned through the Community Wellbeing Directorate of Herefordshire Council and is designed to support genuine collaborative working between Herefordshire Council and providers, promoting high-quality services, improved resident outcomes and a sustainable local care market. Providers admitted to the Framework may participate as a Framework Provider, Partner Provider or Strategic Partner Provider. Eligibility for each level is determined by the applicable Framework requirements, including any required commitment of capacity at the tendered Partnership Rate. Different levels of participation attract different engagement, development and support opportunities.
The Open Framework will have a maximum duration of eight years and an estimated maximum value of approximately £484 million over the full term. The Council does not guarantee that the Open Framework Scheme will continue for the full term of 8 years and no guarantee is given as to the actual value of any framework agreement under the Open Framework Scheme, or any call-off contracts entered under any framework agreement.
The Open Framework Scheme will be re-opened to new providers at least once in the first three years following the award of the first Framework and at least once during each subsequent five-year period until the expiry of the scheme. Herefordshire Council reserves the right to re-open the Open Framework Scheme at additional intervals where it considers this necessary to support market development, increase provider participation, respond to changes in service demand, address emerging care needs, encourage innovation or maintain sufficient capacity across the sector.
Neither admission to the framework nor any ranking or partnership designation guarantees a minimum number or value of placements. Placements remain subject to assessed need, suitability, resident choice, capacity, the applicable call-off mechanism and the Council's statutory duties.
The Council has considered the use of lots and has structured the procurement into lots reflecting the categories of care required by Herefordshire residents. The service is divided into 2 Lots, under which there are Categories of Care for which providers are required for submit a tender for.  These are:
Lot 1 - Older Persons Residential and Nursing Care
Lot 2 - Working Age Adults
Each Lot contains specific Categories of Care which must be applied for separately. Providers will be evaluated for admission to each lot against the published conditions of participation and award criteria, including quality and price, using the weightings and methodology set out in the tender documents. Individual placements will subsequently be allocated in accordance with the published placement process, taking account of assessed need, suitability, availability, lawful resident choice, Provider Status and Provider Ranked Score.
Across both lots, placements will be subject to assessed need, suitability, availability and lawful resident choice. Eligible care homes will normally be considered in order of Provider Status, then Provider Ranked Score within each level. For Lot 2 (Working Age Adults), matching will reflect specialist support requirements and relevant family and community connections, with searches extended beyond Herefordshire where suitable local provision is unavailable. Any objectively justified departure from the normal placement order will be recorded.
The Council is seeking to award multiple contracts to eligible providers who meet the requirements for each of the Lots. Bidders are referred to the invitation to tender document for full details as it contains specific rules on how bidders may submit their response. Providers may be awarded multiple Lots. Subject to satisfying the conditions of participation and award criteria applicable to the relevant lot and Category of Care (as defined in the invitation to tender), there is no maximum number of providers that may be admitted to a particular Lot under the Framework.
Bidders are referred to the invitation to tender and procurement documentation for full details.

records.title: P0402 - Provision of a Risk Management System
records.description:
Hywel Dda University Health Board (HDUHB) is looking to award a contract to appoint one (1) suitably qualified provider to replace their current corporate risk management system. The system has historically been managed by all Health Boards within NHS Wales individually, with the contract due to expire in November 2027. The proposed procurement presents an opportunity to modernise and future-proof risk management arrangements whilst exploring opportunities for greater regional collaboration and consistency in governance and risk practices. 
HDUHB operate in a highly regulated healthcare environment and require strong governance, assurance and transparency across strategic corporate, operational/service delivery, information, data protection and major projects risks.
The system will provide a centralised platform for the identification, assessment, management, monitoring and reporting of organisational risks. It will support effective governance, assurance and compliance processes, providing a single source of information for risk management activities across clinical, operational, workforce, financial, digital, corporate and regulatory functions. The system will support decision-making at operational, corporate and strategic levels, enabling risks to be escalated, monitored and reported through appropriate governance structures.

records.title: National Early Inflammatory Autoimmune Diseases Audit
records.description:
PLEASE NOTE, THIS IS A NEW TENDER OPPORTUNITY RELATED TO A TERMINATED TENDER REF: 2026/S 000-092791
THE CORE REQUIREMENTS OF THE SPECIFICATION REMAIN AS ORIGINALLY PUBLISHED AND THE ONLY AMENDMENTS ARE TO THE FUNDING ENVELOPE.
The contract is expected to initially be delivered for NHS-funded care in England and Wales, and publicly funded care in Jersey for a period of three years, at a maximum total budget of up to £1,116,421.20 GBP including VAT and £930,376.00 GBP excluding VAT. Bids exceeding this limit will be rejected. There is potential to extend the contract for up to two additional years as well as the option to include other Devolved Nations and/or Crown Dependencies, aspirational measures and discretionary inflationary uplifts (all of which will be defined in the service specification).
The maximum budget ‘core’ value of £1,116,421.20 GBP including VAT and £930,376.00 GBP excluding VAT, excludes the potential two-year extension and aspirational intent as included in section 14.4 of Annex A - Service Specification
The contract may be extended for up to 24 months at a pro rata value of the core three- year funding, estimated at up to £620,251.00 excluding VAT.
This proposed extension value may also include pro rata funding of any additional aspirational measures invoked in the first three years of the contract. For example: If an aspirational annual requirement costing £500,000 per year is invoked in year three, then the extension funding (if the aspirational measure is continued) will be the above figures plus the additional £500,000 per year.
Further to this funding, the specification contains a list of aspirational measures which will be expected to be modified into the contract should the need and funding become available. The aspirational intent value, including the potential two- year extension and core 3 year value means an overall ceiling value for this contract of up to £8,055,953.00 excluding VAT and £9,667,144.00 including VAT. This aspirational intent has the potential to be invoked fully, partially, or not at all, and the Authority cannot guarantee that the successful supplier will be required to do any of the aspirational measures listed in section 14.4 of Annex A - Service Specification
The role of a national clinical audit is to stimulate healthcare quality improvement through the provision of high-quality information on the organisation, delivery and outcomes of healthcare, together with tools and support to enable healthcare providers and other audiences to make best use of this information. Outcomes are benchmarked against available national guidance and standards e.g. quality standards from the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE), and those from other established professional and patient sources. Successful national audits are those where the individuals who are engaging with and using the audit results are also in a position to improve the system, and where there is a shared understanding of what good care looks like.
National clinical audits are expected to:
a.Develop a robust, high-quality audit designed around key quality metrics likely to best support local and national healthcare quality improvement.
b.Detect, describe and help reduce unwarranted clinical variation by systematically benchmarking performance, identifying outliers, and supporting services to understand variation in outcomes, processes and experience.
c.Achieve, articulate and maintain close alignment with relevant NICE national guidance and quality standards throughout the audit, as appropriate.
d.Enable healthcare quality improvement through the provision of timely, high-quality data that compares providers of healthcare, and comprises an integrated mixture of named Trust or Health board, Integrated Care System (ICS), commissioner, multidisciplinary team (MDT), possibly consultant or clinical team level and other levels of reporting.
e.Engage patients, carers and the public in a meaningful way, achieving a strong patient voice which informs and contributes to the design, functioning, outputs and direction of the audit.
f.Consider the value and feasibility of linking data at an individual patient level to other relevant national datasets either from the outset or in the future and plan for these linkages from the inception of the contract.
g.Ensure robust methodological and statistical input at all stages of the audit.
h.Identify from the outset the full range of audiences for the reports and other audit outputs and plan and tailor them accordingly.
i.Provide audit results in a timely, accessible and meaningful manner to support healthcare quality improvement, minimising the reporting delay and providing continual access to each unit for their own data.
j.Utilise strong and effective project and programme management to deliver audit outputs on time and within budget.
k.Develop and maintain strong engagement with local clinicians, networks, commissioners, patients and their families and carers and charity and community support groups to drive improvements in services.
l.Deliver high-quality audit outputs, benchmarking and quality improvement as a priority.
At the time of writing the specification, requirements include (but please also refer to the potential future aspirational intent section):
1. Audit Purpose
The overall ambition of the audit is to continue to capture and report data on the performance of individual healthcare providers against the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Quality Standard QS33: Rheumatoid Arthritis in Adults, Quality standard QS214: Rare diseases, and other relevant national standards and guidance, (see Appendix 1).
2. Paediatric Inflammatory Arthritis Pathway
The supplier should work with the wider Dataset and Methodology Stakeholder Group to develop, maintain and report against a minimum viable paediatric inflammatory arthritis pathway.
The initial focus should be on establishing a clinically meaningful dataset and reporting framework sufficient to describe the patient pathway and support audit activity.
Initial measures should focus on a limited number of priority areas agreed with funders and stakeholders, for example referral, diagnosis and treatment timelines.
The updated GIRFT Paediatric Inflammatory Arthritis Pathway guidance, anticipated for publication in January 2027, should be considered a key reference for the future development of the dataset, measures and reporting framework. The supplier should work with the wider Dataset and Methodology Stakeholder Group to review and align the dataset, metrics and reporting outputs with the recommendations and standards set out within the GIRFT guidance, ensuring ongoing relevance and consistency with national best practice.
Any expansion beyond the core pathway, including additional metrics, PROMs/PREMs, transition measures and broader pathway development, should be considered future aspirational intent subject to feasibility, resources and further funding.
3. Data Collection and Audit Design
The supplier should continue to deliver a continuous prospective clinical audit and work with the Dataset and Methodology Group to ensure the audit dataset remains clinically relevant and proportionate.
The supplier is expected to collaborate with specialist disease-specific clinical groups to support interpretation of findings and improve case ascertainment and recruitment rates.
4. Organisational Survey and Quality Improvement
The supplier should review and maintain the organisational survey to ensure it remains proportionate and aligned with audit objectives. Priority should be given to maximising analysis and utilisation of existing data rather than increasing data collection burden in collaboration with the wider Dataset and Methodology Stakeholder Group.
The organisational survey should support the audit's quality improvement objectives by enabling a deeper understanding of service delivery, workforce capacity, variation in practice and barriers to high-quality care.
5. Benchmarking and Improvement
The audit is expected to support continuous improvement across all services.
While identifying high-performing and outlier services remains important, the audit should also support improvement among services performing at or around the national average, where the greatest overall gains may be achieved.
Benchmarking should encourage year-on-year improvement within individual services and provide meaningful insights that motivate all providers to improve, regardless of their current position relative to national performance.
6. Targeted improvement support
The supplier should provide targeted quality improvement support following each annual audit cycle. Activities should build on existing professional networks, collaboratives and stakeholder infrastructure wherever possible rather than creating wholly new arrangements.
Improvement support should be designed to benefit healthcare providers across the performance spectrum, including those performing at a middle level where the greatest overall gains may be achieved, while also supporting services experiencing significant challenges or demonstrating exceptional practice.
Learning generated through quality improvement activities should be shared with all participating healthcare providers to maximise the impact of the audit programme.
The anticipated outputs are:
1.Near real-time dynamic and interactive metric results.
2.Publication of an annual state of the nation report with the inclusion of an organisational survey.
3.Incorporation of validated Patient Reported Outcome Measures.
4.Quality improvement resources.
5.The identification and notification of outliers.
For further information on the current audit, currently delivered by the British Society for Rheumatology (BSR) please head to: https://www.rheumatology.org.uk/improving-care/audits/neiaa

records.title: Naval Architecture Services
records.description:
The appointed Naval Architect shall develop a concept technical specification to a level of maturity that then enables prospective shipbuilders to submit fixed-price 
tenders for the detailed design and construction of the vessel as part of a separate future procurement process. The vessel design shall seek to:
• Maximise manoeuvrability, seakeeping performance, crew comfort and safety.
• Minimise helideck motion during low-speed operations.
• Minimise operational throughout the vessel's lifecycle.
• Maximise reliability of machinery, equipment and operational systems.
• Minimise airborne emissions, discharges and other environmental impacts.
• Have a desired design life of 25 years of operational use by NLB
A key objective of the project is to produce a vessel design capable of accommodating alternative fuel technologies while optimising overall energy efficiency. The design shall seek to minimise fuel consumption, carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions and other environmental emissions and must consider these objectives throughout the design process. Provision shall also be made for the collection, treatment and disposal of all operational waste streams, including bilge water, sludge, sewage and garbage. The technical specification and associated plans shall be developed in close collaboration with NLB personnel. The successful supplier will therefore be expected to join the NLB vessel replacement integrated project team and coordinate the technical workstreams throughout all stages of design development. The successful supplier will therefore be integrated as part of the NLB team for the future procurement process for the design and construction of the vessel. Tenderers are reminded of NLB’s obligations under the Act applicable to a covered procurement to take all reasonable steps to identify and keep under review conflicts of interest and potential conflicts of interest and to ensure that a conflict does not put a supplier at an unfair advantage in relation to a covered procurement. This may include requiring a supplier to take reasonable steps to ensure it is not put at an unfair advantage. As the technical specification, plans and associated Schedules will form part of the shipyard tender documentation, their content must comply with the requirements of the UK Procurement Act 2023, including but not limited to the rules on technical specifications, and any other applicable public sector procurement legislation in force at the time of issue, including relevant Procurement Policy Notes (PPNs). The shipyard ultimately awarded the detailed design and build contract shall be responsible for the complete and fully developed vessel design in all respects. 
The purpose of this initial stage of the project is therefore to develop a robust preliminary design that satisfies NLB's operational requirements and provides confidence that the proposed solution is practical, achievable and capable of successful delivery at an affordable cost.

records.title: National Civil Engineering & Infrastructure Framework
records.description:
The Framework is intended to provide public sector Contracting Authorities across England with access to suitably qualified Contractors capable of delivering civil engineering and infrastructure projects across a range of disciplines and project values.
The Framework, which is being delivered and managed by Procure Partnerships Framework, is expected to support the delivery of works under Design and Build and Build Only arrangements, using Two Stage, Single Stage and Direct Award procurement routes, and embracing both NEC and JCT forms of contract.
The Framework is expected to include five Lot types: Enabling Works and Demolition; Highways and Transport; Water, Flood Defence and Coastal Infrastructure; Utilities, Energy and Electrical Infrastructure; and Regeneration, Brownfield and Urban Infrastructure.
The Framework will be structured on a regional and sub-regional basis across England, with every Lot defined by NUTS codes. Lots up to £30m will be split into sub-regional areas, enabling delivery through locally experienced partners, including small and medium-sized enterprises, with knowledge of local markets and supply chains. Higher-value Lots will cover wider areas (North, Midlands and South).
The Framework does not include Lots for the North West of England. The North West is covered separately by the North West Contractor Framework, operated by Procure Partnerships Framework and Wirral Council on a separate procurement trajectory.
Potential Framework users may include but are not limited to: Local authorities and combined authorities, NHS Trusts and NHS organisations, Universities and further education institutions, Housing associations, Schools, Academies and Colleges, Blue Light/Emergency Services, Health and Social Care Bodies, Libraries and Museums, Registered Charities and Government Departments.
Organisations eligible to use the Framework are listed at https://www.procurepartnerships.co.uk/eligible-users. Any other contracting authority (as defined by the Procurement Act 2023) in England will also be able to use the Framework.
The Framework will provide Contracting Authorities with the ability to process appointments using Direct Award, Two Stage and Single Stage competition mechanisms.
It is anticipated that up to 12 Suppliers will be appointed to each Lot.
Contracting Authorities will be able to make a Direct Award to any Supplier appointed to a Lot of the same Lot type and value band, provided the award is made in accordance with the core terms and the objective mechanism for supplier selection set out in the framework, pursuant to Section 45(4)(b) of the Procurement Act 2023.
Where fewer than four Suppliers express interest in a competition, the Contracting Authority may also invite Suppliers appointed to an adjacent Lot of the same Lot type and value band. Adjacent Lots will be defined in the procurement documents.
Call-off contracts may extend beyond the expiry of the Framework.
The Framework’s lotting structure is anticipated to include:
Lot type 1: Enabling Works and Demolition - Delivery of site enabling works and demolition across all English regions except the North West.
Lot type 1 value bands: £50k - £2m, £2m+.
Lot type 1, both value bands (14 Lots per value band): Northumberland, Tyne & Wear (UKC2); Tees Valley & Durham (UKC1); West & North Yorkshire (UKE2, UKE4); South Yorkshire & the Humber (UKE1, UKE3); East Midlands Corridor (UKF1, UKF2); Lincolnshire (UKF3); West Midlands (UKG); East Anglia (UKH1); Bedfordshire & Hertfordshire (UKH2); Essex (UKH3); Kent, Surrey, Sussex & South London (UKJ2, UKJ4, UKI34, UKI44, UKI45, UKI51, UKI61, UKI62, UKI63, UKI75); Thames Valley, Hampshire & North London (UKJ1, UKJ3, UKI31, UKI32, UKI33, UKI41, UKI42, UKI43, UKI52, UKI53, UKI54, UKI71, UKI72, UKI73, UKI74); West of England, Gloucestershire, Wiltshire & Somerset (UKK1, UKK23); Devon, Cornwall & Dorset (UKK21, UKK22, UKK3, UKK4).
Lot type 2: Highways and Transport - Delivery of highways and transport infrastructure works, including (but not limited to) Highways Maintenance & Minor Works, Major Highways, Bridges, Structures & Tunnels, and Local Transport, across all English regions except the North West.
Lot type 2 value bands: £50k - £2m, £2m - £10m, £10m - £30m, £30m - £50m, £50m+.
Lot type 3: Water, Flood Defence and Coastal Infrastructure - Delivery of water, flood defence and coastal infrastructure works, including (but not limited to) Drainage and Flood Defence, Coastal Protection, and Blue-Green Infrastructure, across all English regions except the North West.
Lot type 3 value bands: £50k - £2m, £2m - £10m, £10m - £30m, £30m - £50m, £50m+.
Lot type 4: Utilities, Energy and Electrical Infrastructure - Delivery of utilities, energy and electrical infrastructure works, including (but not limited to) Utility Diversions, EV Charging Infrastructure, and Low-Carbon Infrastructure Enabling Works, across all English regions except the North West.
Lot type 4 value bands: £50k - £2m, £2m - £10m, £10m - £30m, £30m - £50m, £50m+.
Lot type 5: Regeneration, Brownfield and Urban Infrastructure - Delivery of regeneration, brownfield and urban infrastructure works, including (but not limited to) Town Centre Improvements, Hard Landscaping, and Regeneration & Brownfield Infrastructure, across all English regions except the North West.
Lot type 5 value bands: £50k - £2m, £2m - £10m, £10m - £30m, £30m - £50m, £50m+.
Lot types 2 to 5, £50k - £2m, £2m - £10m and £10m - £30m (14 Lots per value band): Northumberland, Tyne & Wear (UKC2); Tees Valley & Durham (UKC1); West & North Yorkshire (UKE2, UKE4); South Yorkshire & the Humber (UKE1, UKE3); East Midlands Corridor (UKF1, UKF2); Lincolnshire (UKF3); West Midlands (UKG); East Anglia (UKH1); Bedfordshire & Hertfordshire (UKH2); Essex (UKH3); Kent, Surrey, Sussex & South London (UKJ2, UKJ4, UKI34, UKI44, UKI45, UKI51, UKI61, UKI62, UKI63, UKI75); Thames Valley, Hampshire & North London (UKJ1, UKJ3, UKI31, UKI32, UKI33, UKI41, UKI42, UKI43, UKI52, UKI53, UKI54, UKI71, UKI72, UKI73, UKI74); West of England, Gloucestershire, Wiltshire & Somerset (UKK1, UKK23); Devon, Cornwall & Dorset (UKK21, UKK22, UKK3, UKK4).
Lot types 2 to 5, £30m - £50m and £50m+ (3 Lots per value band): North (UKC, UKE); Midlands (UKF, UKG); South (UKH, UKI, UKJ, UKK).
London is split along the River Thames: North London forms part of the Thames Valley, Hampshire & North London area, and South London forms part of the Kent, Surrey, Sussex & South London area.

Procurement Description
This Tender Notice is in relation to the Department for Education Early Years (EY) Special Educational Needs and Disability (SEND) Continuous Professional Development (CPD) Provision of Phase 1 Materials and Training.
Department for Education are seeking to procure an online package of training with learning materials for early years practitioners on SEND and make this available and accessible for all early years practitioners from September 2026 for up to 12 months, with the possibility of extension on a quarterly basis for up to an additional 12 months if required
The training should:
Be specific to SEND in early years only, specifically ages 0-4.
Be available and applicable to all early years practitioners, regardless of qualification level or setting type (PVIs, school-based nurseries, childminders etc.) and meet government accessibility standards.
Be in an online, modular, self-paced format that users can revisit at their convenience with videos/webinars dispersed amongst the online learning.
Provide a minimum of 20 hours of content, to enable and support learning beyond the level currently covered in the DfE’s Early Years Child Development Training, module 8.
Cover, at a minimum, content around inclusive practice and methods for embedding this within a setting and information/guidance on engaging with parents of children with SEND.
A combination of existing and newly configured content is acceptable, provided mobilisation and outcomes requirements are met.

records.title: Supply Chain Technology Solutions
records.description:
London & Quadrant Housing Trust (L&Q) is undertaking preliminary market engagement to explore available Supply Chain Technology Solutions.
About L&Q
At L&Q we believe passionately that people's health, security and happiness depend on where they live. We house around 250,000 people in more than 105,000 homes, primarily across London, the South East and the North West of England.
Our vision is that everyone deserves a quality home that gives them the chance to live a better life – our mission is to combine our social purpose and commercial drive to create homes and neighbourhoods everyone can be proud of.
As a regulated charitable housing association, we reinvest all the money we make into new and existing homes, creating successful communities and providing services for our residents.
The Project
L&Q's Supply Chain currently operates without a single technology solution supporting it end to end.
The objective is to advance L&Q's Supply Chain Technology so it can enable improvements to business capability that enables faster, data-driven procurement decisions, improves supplier accountability, and delivers greater value for money, while accelerating tactical process, governance, and supply chain improvements to realise early benefits through enhanced visibility of spend, performance, and contract delivery, reducing risk, strengthening category management, and delivering measurable savings, social value, and ESG outcomes ahead of full solution adoption.
This early market engagement forms part of the project's initial phase and will help inform the development of requirements, assess potential delivery options, and setting out a high level process design. Following this phase, L&Q intends to agree the option in February 2027 and, if required, commence procurement activity from March 2027.

records.title: Traffic Signals Maintenance and Equipment
records.description:

This contract only covers the maintenance of permanent traffic signals; temporary traffic signals are supplied by traffic management companies as part of civils contracts and are not a Swindon Borough Council asset.

records.title: Telecoms Mast Management Services
records.description:
Royal Berkshire Fire Authority (RBFA) requires a specialist telecommunications consultancy to manage its portfolio of mobile telecommunications installations located across several fire station sites. The portfolio includes agreements with mobile network operators and infrastructure providers occupying operational assets, including training towers. 
The appointed consultant will provide day-to-day management of the telecommunications estate, including coordination of operator access requests, lease and licence management, rent reviews, lease renewals, compliance monitoring, and advice relating to the Electronic Communications Code (ECC).  The service also supports the Authority in protecting operational activities, ensuring health and safety compliance, and maximising commercial income from the estate. 
Based on information provided during the procurement process, RBFA currently receives approximately 90 operator access requests per annum across its portfolio. The Authority therefore requires a suitably experienced provider capable of managing operator activity, minimising operational disruption, and ensuring that all works are undertaken in accordance with relevant lease provisions and statutory requirements. 
A key commercial objective of the contract is to maximise cost recovery from operators where lease provisions permit, thereby reducing the overall cost of portfolio management to the Authority and supporting a cost-neutral or near cost-neutral operating model. 
The appointed provider will also support the Authority with ad hoc professional services, including lease renewals, new lettings, valuations, site surveys, compliance matters and specialist telecommunications property advice as required throughout the contract term.

records.title: FCDO Accra British High Commission Offices Redevelopment, Ghana
records.description:
Project Overview
1.1	The route to market is the Competitive Flexible Procedure. This will comprise of a Request to Participate stage with Conditions of Participation questions and an Invitation to Tender stage.
1.2	The scope of the project is to redevelop two existing sites (Afadja and Volta) to accommodate the British High Commission. The British High Commission (Ghana) estate is made up of two sites that sit side by side. It is located on Julius Nyerere Link Road in a reasonably affluent and central part of Accra, close to Parliament, the Presidency and some Ministries. The office estate in Accra is tired and in poor condition (in places), having suffered from a lack of strategic investment and maintenance. 
1.3	It is anticipated that the consturction will take place in phases. Work will start at the Volta site which will be vacant throughout construction (staff normally based at this site will be temporarily moved to the Afadja Site).  Once construction works at the Volta site are complete, all of the staff at the Afadja site will be transferred to the Volta site to enable the phase 2 works to be undertaken in the unoccupied Afadja building. 
1.4	In line with the overall estate strategy, the intention is to have the Volta HC Office staff move to the Afadja High Commission for the duration of the Volta construction period.
1.5	The existing sites comprises of:
•	An existing split-site office building. It is proposed that the Volta building be retained and refurbished. 
•	Existing plant structures to be demolished to make way for new extension. 
•	Existing external landscaping to be demolished in some areas to make way for new cloister and walkway.  
1.6	Part of the site development design includes:
•	Undertaking minor works to the existing Afadja site to make suitable to be used as a decant property whilst works to the Volta building are undertaken.  
•	Refurbish the existing building to a fit-for-purpose, open plan office standard. 
•	Replacement of existing mechanical and electrical installations. 
•	Seismic strengthening and associated structural works.
•	External works to create shared internal and external spaces.  
1.7	The Contractor, as well as any engaged sub-contractors, are required to perform all work in accordance with the relevant UK Standards. The construction must meet established UK standards throughout the build process.
2.	It is anticipated that the works will be undertaken under the NEC form of contract; ECC 4, Option A (Priced Contract with an Activity Schedule). 
3.	The project team is also considering the inclusion of an Early Contractor Involvement stage ahead of the construction stage. Both stages will be within the same contract.  
4.	Some areas of the building will be classified as higher security and will require a separate specialist contractor. These works will not form part of this requirement/contract. However, the parameter and interface between the higher classified areas and the works within this requirement will require security cleared personnel at Security Check (SC*) level to manage the works. Contractor’s will need to be able to provide such personnel before the works contract can begin. 
*SC is a process of security vetting. Further details can be found at https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/united-kingdom-security-vetting-clearance-levels/national-security-vetting-clearance-levels#security-check-sc.

records.title: Tier 2 Mains Renewal Delivery & Resilience Framework
records.description:
Introduction
Yorkshire Water is publishing tender market notice for a Tier 2 Mains Renewal Delivery & Resilience Framework to support the delivery of its AMP8/9 investment programme.
The framework is intended to provide strategic delivery capability for the renewal, rehabilitation, replacement and resilience enhancement of potable water distribution infrastructure across the Yorkshire Water operational area.
This notice is issued to:
•	Inform the market of Yorkshire Water's proposed procurement strategy.
________________________________________
2. Background
Yorkshire Water is developing a long-term approach to address ageing water distribution assets and improve network resilience in support of:
•	AMP performance commitments.
•	Leakage reduction targets.
•	Asset health improvement.
•	Customer service resilience.
•	Environmental performance and sustainability objectives.
•	Long-term network optimisation.
The framework is expected to support annual investment programmes comprising a mixture of:
•	Open-cut mains replacement.
•	Trenchless rehabilitation solutions.
•	Strategic renewal schemes.
•	Burst-prone asset replacement.
•	Resilience and reinforcement projects.
•	Associated design and survey activities.
•	Commissioning and network integration works.
________________________________________
3. Scope of the Proposed Framework
The primary objective is to deliver shorter, non-complex mains renewal schemes more affordably through direct Tier 2 engagement. Typical scope will be customer-focused, non-complex schemes of less than 1 km, generally on mains of 300 mm diameter or smaller, but this should not preclude longer runs where advantageous.  
The anticipated scope may include, but is not limited to:
Design Services
•	Feasibility studies.
•	Detailed engineering design.
•	Temporary works design.
•	Network modelling support.
•	Buildability reviews.
•	Value engineering.
Delivery Services
•	Water main renewal and replacement.
•	Pipe installation and commissioning.
•	Pipe bursting and sliplining.
•	Directional drilling and trenchless technologies.
•	Ancillary civils.
•	Highway reinstatement.
•	Traffic management.
•	Customer liaison services.
Resilience Enhancements
•	Network reconfiguration.
•	Strategic resilience interventions.
•	Pressure management assets.
•	Critical supply protection schemes.
•	Smart network deployment.
________________________________________
4. Indicative Framework Structure
Yorkshire Water is considering a proposed multi supplier framework structure which will include:
•	Design and Build.
•	NEC4 ECSC Task Orders.
•	Competitively Tendered standard rates.
•	Defined pricing adjustments.
•	Direct award and/or mini competition award model.
________________________________________
5. Estimated Value and Duration
At this stage the estimated total framework value is anticipated to be in the region of:
£10 million value framework split in different schemes. 
The framework term being considered is: 
Initial period: 5 years with Extension options: up to 3 years
Total potential duration: up to 8 years.
These figures are indicative only and subject to change.
________________________________________
6. Expected Supplier Capabilities
Clean Water main laying using all relevant techniques, including rehabilitation and replacement. No lining experience is required. Typical scope will be customer-focused, non-complex schemes of less than 1 km, generally on mains of 300 mm diameter or smaller. Requirement: Design and Build capability, with the ability to plan and deliver works safely, efficiently and with minimal disruption to customers and local communities
Yorkshire Water wishes to engage with organisations capable of demonstrating experience in one or more of the following:
•	Regional Tier 2 contractors
•	Water utility infrastructure delivery.
•	Mains renewal programmes.
•	Pipeline construction.
•	Design and engineering services.
•	Leakage reduction interventions.
•	Trenchless technology deployment.
•	Digital construction techniques.
•	Programme and portfolio management.
•	Supply chain innovation.
Suppliers should be able to demonstrate:
•	Strong health, safety and wellbeing performance.
•	Environmental management capability.
•	Social value delivery.
•	Carbon reduction initiatives.
•	Collaborative behaviours.
•	Experience operating under NEC contracts.

records.title: PROVISION OF SERVICES TO ACCEPT, PROCESS AND MARKET MIXED AND SOURCE SEPARATED WASTE FOR RECYCLING
records.description:
arc21 is procuring, in two Lots to reflect different waste configurations and collection systems and to provide for future changes and roll out of services, the provision of services relating to the receipt, transfer, processing, brokerage to end markets and management of any output wastes, from waste that is collected via kerbside dry recycling collections by arc21’s Relevant Member Councils, in accordance with the Waste Hierarchy. Lot 1 predominantly incorporates waste collected in the Antrim and Newtownabbey Borough Council, Ards and North Down Borough Council and Belfast City Council areas. Collection systems currently include kerbside sort with some separate food and textile streams, co-mingled without glass and separate glass. The combined estimated annual tonnage is 34,000 tonnes based on current collection systems but this is subject to change over the Term of the Contract due to factors such as policy changes e.g. EPR and DRS, obligations placed on businesses to recycle and councils seeking to increase their recycling rates. Over the Term of the Contract, it is envisaged, but not guaranteed, that changes may be made to the council collection regimes. This may mean further segregation of waste which may be achieved by greater source segregation either through kerbside sort or the implementation of other collection systems such as twin bins for dry recyclables and/or the further rollout of separate food waste collections and enhanced recycling services to businesses. Additionally, there may be further segregation at council recycling centres aimed at collecting dry recyclables from households and/or businesses. Furthermore, it is anticipated there may be a requirement to receive, sort and market other materials such as plastic film and/or increase textile collection, either on a pilot basis or as a full roll-out. The draft contract sets out a process for implementing such changes including providing for possible changes to the terms of the contract in consequence. Changes to the reporting requirements may occur during the Contract Term. Decisions on any changes will not be taken until DIWASS and Digital Waste Tracking are fully implemented and will be based primarily on functionality and the Authority’s ability to access information. If streamlining is possible a reduction in the costs associated with the administration may be sought using the variation process included in the Form of Contract. 
Lot 2 predominantly incorporates waste collected in the Lisburn and Castlereagh City Council, Mid and East Antrim Borough Council and Newry, Mourne and Down District Council areas. The waste is collected co-mingled and there is a requirement for glass to be able to be accepted mixed with the other dry recyclables. The combined estimated tonnage is 27,000 tonnes based on the current collection system operated in Newry, Mourne and Down District Council, the transition from kerbside sort to co-mingled including the addition of glass for Mid and East Antrim Borough Council and the current comingled system without glass for Lisburn and Castlereagh City Council. In the event Lisburn and Castlereagh City Council fully transition to co-mingled with glass it is estimated there will be additional tonnage of circa 3,500 tonnes. Over the Term of the Contract, it is envisaged, but not guaranteed, that changes may be made to the council collection regimes as a result of policy change and/or requirements of the council. There may be a requirement for further segregation of waste which may be achieved by greater source segregation through the implementation of a twin bin system for dry recyclables and/or enhanced recycling services to businesses. Additionally, there may be further segregation at council recycling centres aimed at collecting dry recyclables from households and/or businesses. Furthermore, it is anticipated there may be a requirement to separate glass, to receive, sort and market plastic film and/or increase textile collections, either on a pilot basis or as a full roll-out. The draft contract sets out a process for implementing such changes including providing for possible changes to the terms of the contract in consequence. Changes to the reporting requirements may occur during the Contract Term. Decisions on any changes will not be taken until DIWASS and Digital Waste Tracking are fully implemented and will be based primarily on functionality and the Authority’s ability to access information. If streamlining is possible a reduction in the costs associated with the administration may be sought using the variation process included in the Form of Contract. 
The Contract values for Lots 1 and 2 include consideration of the gate fee and material values over the Term of the Contract and anticipate possible service changes, additional material stream costs and income. The Authority shall have the option to extend the duration of the Agreement for any period up to 36 months in aggregate beyond the Initial Term and the Contract values include for these extensions if utilised fully. Following the Service Commencement Date, Relevant Member Councils may change their waste collection arrangements, including adding or removing recyclable materials, which may in turn alter the list of Target Materials. Such changes are anticipated during the Contract Term due to evolving policy and legislative requirements and/or future requirements by the Relevant Member Councils. The appointed Contractor(s) will also be responsible for delivering social benefits, collating and reporting data and reporting performance relevant to the Contract. The Authority reserves the right to allow other councils of the Authority to use the alternate Lot, on occasion and/or for specific material treatment requirements that may emerge during the Term of the Contract.

1.3	It is anticipated that the consturction will take place in phases. Work will start at the Volta site which will be vacant throughout construction (staff normally based at this site will be temporarily moved to the Afadja Site).  Once construction works at the Volta site are complete, all of the staff at the Afadja site will be transferred to the Volta site to enable the phase 2 works to be undertaken in the unoccupied Afadja building. 
1.4	In line with the overall estate strategy, the intention is to have the Volta HC Office staff move to the Afadja High Commission for the duration of the Volta construction period.
1.5	The existing sites comprises of:
•	An existing split-site office building. It is proposed that the Volta building be retained and refurbished. 
•	Existing plant structures to be demolished to make way for new extension. 
•	Existing external landscaping to be demolished in some areas to make way for new cloister and walkway.  
1.6	Part of the site development design includes:
•	Undertaking minor works to the existing Afadja site to make suitable to be used as a decant property whilst works to the Volta building are undertaken.  
•	Refurbish the existing building to a fit-for-purpose, open plan office standard. 
•	Replacement of existing mechanical and electrical installations. 
•	Seismic strengthening and associated structural works.
•	External works to create shared internal and external spaces.  
1.7	The Contractor, as well as any engaged sub-contractors, are required to perform all work in accordance with the relevant UK Standards. The construction must meet established UK standards throughout the build process.
2.	It is anticipated that the works will be undertaken under the NEC form of contract; ECC 4, Option A (Priced Contract with an Activity Schedule). 
3.	The project team is also considering the inclusion of an Early Contractor Involvement stage ahead of the construction stage. Both stages will be within the same contract.  
4.	Some areas of the building will be classified as higher security and will require a separate specialist contractor. These works will not form part of this requirement/contract. However, the parameter and interface between the higher classified areas and the works within this requirement will require security cleared personnel at Security Check (SC*) level to manage the works. records.description:
The Ministry of Defence (the Authority) under the Materiel Distribution Land (MDL) programme is developing a requirement project for Heavy Equipment Transporter (HET) platform. Initially circa 70 to 90 vehicles with an integrated support solution service for an initial period of ten years, with potential options to increase the acquisition volume and extend beyond the initial support period. Aspirational Full Operating Capability (FOC) is June 2029.
This requirement aims to introduce a new, technologically advanced system for the delivery of heavy and out-of-gauge equipment, with a minimum threshold of eighty-five (85) metric tonnes, featuring improved low mobility lift capabilities. This system will significantly improve and sustain the operational movement of heavy, mission-critical equipment well into the future.
The primary role is to transport heavy armoured equipment, including armoured fighting vehicles (AFVs) and main battle tank (MBT), but it must also be capable of moving lighter equipment into the theatre of operations. Additionally, this equipment will be used during peacetime for training delivery both in the UK and overseas.
A PIN has previously been released for this requirement reference 2025/S 000-002913.

records.title: Traffic Signals Maintenance and Equipment
records.description:
Swindon Borough Council invites you to contribute to Preliminary Market Engagement in relation to delivering the services referred to below.
The Council is seeking to appoint a supplier to maintain the traffic signal equipment within the Borough of Swindon.
This will cover all re-active maintenance “faults” that occur on the traffic signal asset. These being either by failure of equipment or by damage from a 3rd party. It will also include hosted fault management software for reporting faults to the contractor, viewing cleared faults, calculating KPIs and reviewing the historic fault database for each site.
The contract will also include prices and a mechanism for pro-active maintenance “refurbishment work”. This is the process of updating and replacing sites when they have reached the end of their life. It will also include prices and a mechanism for ordering future LED signal head upgrades and prices for new signal equipment at new installations.
This contract only covers the maintenance of permanent traffic signals; temporary traffic signals are supplied by traffic management companies as part of civils contracts and are not a Swindon Borough Council asset.
The overall aim of the planned procurement exercise is to run an Open Tender procedure for works under the remit of the Procurement Act 2023.
The Council intends on establishing a contract with a single contractor to deliver these services over an initial contract period of 36 months with an option to extend by up to 24 months.
The estimated annual contract value is600,000.
The estimated contract value for the initial contract period of 3 years is £1,800,000.
The estimated total contract price over 5 years is £3,000,000.
The purpose of this Preliminary Market Engagement is to gain market insight into the following aspects of the project: -
•	Market Interest
•	Capacity
•	Mobilisation
•	Insurances
•	Pricing
This Preliminary Market Engagement exercise will close at 16:00 on 18th December 2026; following this all responses will be reviewed by Swindon Borough Council.

records.title: Glasshouse Fields Estate – External Fire Safety Improvement Scheme
records.description:
NHT are working with Martin Arnold Limited, acting as NHT’s consultants, who have designed the works to allow for the external facades of all properties associated with this project to be brought up to standards required by the Building Safety Act and Building Regulations. 
The primary reason for the works is to address the defects identified by the FRAEW report.
These defects are:
•Fire stopping around vent and duct penetrations within the masonry, rendered EWI and curtain wall façades. 
•Provide cavity barriers to the top of the walls at the parapet level of the masonry and rendered façades. 
•Remediate the curtain walls on compartment wall lines to remove combustible insulation and reinstate cavity barriers behind the panels.
In order to address the defects, all external facades will need to be stripped back in localised areas, a new sheathing board fitted, new fire cavity barriers fitted, new insulation fitted and the external leaf of the façade reinstated, including all enabling and other associated works in achieving this. This statement is intended as a simply description of the works, please refer to the specification for a full description of the works

records.title: High Needs Supported Accommodation Service for Young People Aged From 16 Years - Strategic Partner
records.description:
Bury Council is seeking a single strategic partner to provide a complete turnkey solution for a High Needs Supported Accommodation Service for looked after and care experienced young people aged from 16 years.
The successful provider will:
- fund, design and build a minimum of five properties on a Council-owned site leased to it by the Council: four self-contained single-occupancy homes for young people and one staff and support hub;
- register the service with Ofsted as supported accommodation and keep it registered;
- staff and operate the service 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, with its own employed staff;
- repair, maintain and renew the properties for the contract term;
- work with the Council as a strategic partner on an open-book basis.
Tenderers should note that the following are fixed requirements of this procurement and will not be subject to negotiation:
- Service: A High Needs Supported Accommodation Service for looked-after and care-experienced young people aged 16 and 17, operated in accordance with the Supported Accommodation (England) Regulations 2023 and registered with Ofsted.
- Accommodation: A minimum of four self-contained homes for young people together with one staff and support hub.
- Site: The accommodation will be developed on a Council-owned site which will be leased to the successful Provider.
- Capital Funding: The successful Provider shall be responsible for all design, development, construction, financing and associated capital costs required to deliver the accommodation. Capital, development, financing and borrowing costs shall not be recoverable through the weekly placement fee.
- Contract Term: Ten (10) years with an option for the Council to extend for a further period of up to five (5) years.
- Programme: The accommodation is anticipated to be ready for occupation approximately 18 months after Contract Award and agreement of the development site.
- TUPE: TUPE is not expected to apply as this is a new service.
Matters Subject to Further Development
The Council has taken reasonable steps to define its requirements at the point of publication. However, due to the nature of the development and service, certain matters cannot be fully determined at this stage and may be refined during the procurement, development, mobilisation and implementation phases.
These include:
- The specific Council owned site to be utilised.
- Ground conditions, abnormal development costs and utility connection requirements, which may only become known following detailed surveys and investigations.
- The outcome and timing of the planning process and any associated approvals.
- Final lease documentation, which will be based on Heads of Terms issued with the procurement documents and remain subject to the Council's internal approval processes.
- The timing of Ofsted registration and any associated regulatory approvals.
- Detailed mobilisation arrangements, including any phased opening of accommodation.
- Final contract management arrangements, reporting requirements and performance measures.
- Service demand, occupancy levels and placement volumes throughout the Contract Term.
- Changes in legislation, statutory guidance, regulatory requirements or inspection frameworks applicable to supported accommodation services.
Tenderers should therefore ensure that their proposals demonstrate sufficient flexibility to respond to reasonable operational and regulatory changes throughout the Contract Term.
Service Flexibility
The successful Provider shall be required to deliver a service capable of adapting to:
- changes in demand and occupancy levels;
- safeguarding requirements;
- statutory, regulatory and inspection requirements;
- reporting and performance management requirements; and
- partnership-working arrangements with the Council and other relevant agencies.
Any changes shall be implemented in accordance with the terms of the Contract and the provisions of the Procurement Act 2023.
Estimated Contract Value
The estimated Contract Value has been calculated on the basis of four homes operating at the maximum weekly price throughout the maximum potential Contract Term of fifteen years.
The estimate is not a guarantee of occupancy levels, placement volumes, expenditure or income.
Option to Add Additional Homes
The Council reserves the right to require the successful Provider to develop and operate additional self-contained homes during the Contract Term should service demand justify such expansion.
Any additional homes shall be delivered on substantially the same terms and conditions as the initial requirement.
At the maximum Contract Price, each additional home would increase the annual Contract Value by up to £156,000 per annum.
The estimated value of any such option has been taken into account when establishing the overall scope of this procurement.
Sites
The Council will lease a Council owned site to the successful Provider for the development. The site has not yet been confirmed. Details of the sites under consideration will be provided within the procurement documents.
Should a proposed site become unavailable, unsuitable, uneconomic, fail to secure the necessary approvals, or otherwise be incapable of delivering the required accommodation and service outcomes, the Council reserves the right to substitute an alternative Council owned site. Any resulting changes shall be managed in accordance with the Partnership Agreement and associated contractual provisions.
If no suitable site can be identified or agreed, the Council reserves the right to discontinue the project and terminate the Partnership Agreement in accordance with its terms.
Tenderers should note that the specific development site may change prior to Contract Award. However, following development of the accommodation, the Council does not anticipate any material change to the accommodation requirement other than through the option to add additional homes described above.
Future Service Development
The Council expects the service to evolve in line with emerging best practice, learning, legislation and regulatory requirements.
Accordingly, the Council may, during the Contract Term, introduce enhancements to service delivery, including:
trauma-informed approaches;
psychologically informed environments (PIE);
revised support interventions;
enhanced partnership-working arrangements;
improved outcomes frameworks; and
revised reporting and performance management requirements.
Any such enhancements shall be implemented in accordance with the Contract variation provisions and shall not alter the overall nature of the Contract.
The successful Provider shall be expected to demonstrate flexibility and resilience in adapting service delivery to ensure services remain effective, compliant and responsive to the needs of young people.
Award Approval
Award of the Contract will be subject to Cabinet approval and confirmation that the preferred Tender provides an affordable, sustainable, deliverable and value for money solution.
The Council's objective is to secure improved outcomes for looked after and care experienced young people through the provision of high-quality supported accommodation that represents long-term value for money when compared with current arrangements.
Tenders will be evaluated solely in accordance with the published procurement documents, award criteria and the maximum permitted price.
The Council reserves the right not to award a Contract where:
no Tender meets the Council's minimum requirements;
all Tenders exceed the maximum permitted price;
the Council is unable to obtain the necessary approvals;
the procurement no longer represents an affordable or deliverable solution; or
the procurement is discontinued in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023.
The Council reserves the right to abandon or discontinue the procurement process at any stage and shall not be liable for any costs incurred by Tenderers in participating in the procurement.
