records.title: Places for People ERP System
records.description:
Places for People (PfP) employs in excess of 13,000 colleagues operating across the UK. The organisation intends to continue acquiring and integrating other organisations to expand its scale and enhance the services it provides to people and communities. As a result, PfP anticipates sustained growth over the next 10 years, increasing both workforce size and operational complexity.
This growth trajectory introduces increasing demands around:
Organisational integration
Process standardisation
Data consistency and governance
Scalable support for HR, finance, payroll, procurement, and asset management
Rapid onboarding of newly acquired organisations and colleagues
In this context, a modern, integrated ERP solution is fundamental to enabling PfP to operate efficiently at scale. The future ERP platform must support mergers and acquisitions, enable consistent and flexible processes, and provide reliable, organisation-wide management information.
PfP's long-term strategy includes rationalising its technology landscape through the alignment of business capabilities to enterprise-grade solutions.
PfP is undertaking a competitive procurement process to assess ERP solutions. The outcome of this process is intended to support the organisation's transformation by modernising core enterprise capabilities and ensuring they remain scalable, resilient, and aligned to future growth.

records.buyer: Mayor's Office For Policing And Crime
records.title: London's Violence Reduction Unit - Pan London Tertiary Service
records.description:
About the VRU
The London Violence Reduction Unit (VRU), hosted within the Mayor's Office for Policing and Crime (MOPAC), pioneers a partnership-based public health approach to tackling violence rooted in prevention and early intervention. Since 2019, the VRU has invested in over 550,000 targeted interventions for young people across London.
Project Background
The VRU takes a public health approach to violence reduction, recognising that prevention requires action at different stages. Primary prevention seeks to change the conditions that make violence more likely, strengthening protective factors before violence occurs. Secondary prevention responds when risk or violence is emerging, aiming to interrupt risk and prevent escalation. Tertiary prevention focuses on reducing the harm caused by violence, supporting recovery and reducing the likelihood of further violence. These approaches are complementary, forming part of a wider response to violence and exploitation.
Children and young people affected by violence and exploitation can experience complex and interconnected needs, alongside significant barriers to accessing support. These may include safeguarding concerns, trauma, mental health needs, housing instability, disrupted relationships and difficulties accessing education, employment and other opportunities. Tertiary provision is therefore essential to provide tailored, coordinated support that addresses immediate safeguarding concerns, helps young people recover and improve their circumstances, and reduces the risk of further harm.
The Violence and Exploitation Support Service (VESS) launched in June 2024 to provide specialist support to young people across London who have been affected by violence and exploitation. Management of the VESS contract transferred from the Mayor’s Office for Police and Crime (MOPAC) to the VRU in October 2025, with the contract due to expire in June 2027.
VESS has made an important contribution to the VRU’s wider approach to tertiary provision, reinforcing the value of trusted relationships between practitioners and young people, flexible and personalised support, and a multidisciplinary approach connecting young people to specialist services, including mental health, housing, education, employment and safeguarding. This experience, alongside the VRU’s established expertise in violence reduction and wider evidence base, provides a strong foundation for the development of the new Tertiary Service.
As VESS is due to end in June 2027, the VRU is commissioning a new Tertiary Service to provide specialist support to young people experiencing the highest levels of harm, vulnerability, violence and exploitation.
Description of the service
The London Violence Reduction Unit (VRU) will appoint a provider to deliver a pan-London Tertiary Service for young people aged 11–25 who are experiencing the highest levels of harm, vulnerability, violence and exploitation.
The VRU Tertiary Service forms part of the VRU’s wider public health approach to violence reduction. It is intended to provide specialist support to young people who are already affected by, or at significant risk of, serious violence and exploitation, where intensive and coordinated, intervention is required to address their needs and reduce the risk of further harm.
The Service will deliver intensive, relationship-based one-to-one support that responds to immediate safeguarding concerns and the wider factors contributing to violence, exploitation and vulnerability. Practitioners will build trusted relationships with young people who may have experienced significant trauma, have difficulty engaging with services or have developed distrust towards professionals.
Support will be tailored to each young person’s circumstances, needs, risks and aspirations. This includes responding to immediate concerns while addressing longer-term factors affecting safety, stability and wellbeing. The Provider will coordinate support across multiple areas of need and help young people access relevant specialist interventions and wider services.
The Provider will work collaboratively with statutory, voluntary and community sector partners to support identification and referral, coordinate interventions, address barriers to accessing support and strengthen pathways between the VRU’s wider tertiary provision and other relevant services.
The Service will operate within a consistent pan-London framework, supported by strong local integration and partnerships. The Provider will understand local systems and community contexts in which young people experience violence and exploitation, while ensuring that young people can access a consistent standard of support across London.
The service is expected to:
- Identify, engage and support young people aged 11-25 who are experiencing the highest levels of violence, exploitation, harm and vulnerability.
- Deliver intensive, relationship-based support through named practitioners who build trusted, consistent and sustained relationships with young people.
- Improve young people's safety, wellbeing, stability and resilience by addressing immediate safeguarding concerns and underlying drivers of harm.
- Provide tailored, needs-led interventions that respond to each young person's individual circumstances, strengths, risks, and aspirations.
- Support young people to access, navigate, and engage with relevant statutory, voluntary, and community services through advocacy and system navigation.
- Improve access to specialist support, including housing, education, training and employment, family support, mental health services, and other interventions relevant to need.
- Strengthen multi-agency partnerships, information sharing, and coordinated responses across local systems.
- Promote culturally competent, gender-responsive, and trauma-informed approaches that reflect young people's identities, experiences, and needs.
- Embed lived experience, cultural competence, reflective practice and trauma-informed principles throughout service delivery.
- Strengthen local safeguarding and violence reduction responses through the sharing of intelligence, learning, emerging risks and contextual safeguarding insights.
- Operate as a connected pan-London service that shares effective practice, learning and intelligence across borough boundaries.
- Support wider system improvement by informing more effective local and pan-London responses to violence and exploitation through learning from service delivery.
Target Audience
The Service is intended for London-based young people aged 11 to 25 who are most impacted by violence and exploitation.
Support young people who demonstrate indicators of:
- Established harm: Violence or exploitation is currently occurring or has occurred repeatedly.
- Entrenched circumstances: The young person is experiencing persistent violence or exploitation that has not been effectively addressed through existing services or previous interventions.
- Multiple and interconnected risks: Violence or exploitation is linked to factors such as housing instability, family circumstances, harmful peer influences, trauma, substance use, education, or involvement with the justice system.
- Escalating or significant contextual risk: The young person is exposed to harm through relationships, peer networks, locations, institutions, online spaces or wider environments that require specialist intervention and coordinated support. This risk may be increasing in frequency, severity or impact.
Examples of young people who may be appropriate for the Service include, but are not limited to:
- Young people with missing episodes linked to violence, exploitation or criminal activity.
- Young people who are being exploited into, or are actively involved with, harmful peer groups, gangs or organised criminal networks.
- Young people whose risks have persisted or escalated despite previous interventions or support arrangements.
- Young people demonstrating escalating patterns of offending, exploitation, vulnerability or harm.
- Young people experiencing violence and exploitation alongside housing insecurity, homelessness, family breakdown, trauma, poor mental health, neurodiversity, substance use or disengagement from education, training or employment.
Scope of Delivery
The Provider will deliver a pan-London Tertiary Service for young people aged 11–25 who are experiencing the highest levels of harm, vulnerability, violence and exploitation.
The Provider delivering the Service must demonstrate the following:
- Credible and effective youth work
- Advocacy and systems navigation
- Safeguarding and transitional safeguarding
- Multi-agency partnership working and local systems integration
- Specialist intervention and needs-led support
- Reflective practice, learning and service development
The Provider will demonstrate experience of working with young people affected by violence and exploitation who present with high levels of risk, harm and vulnerability. 
The Provider will deliver a clear organisational approach to engaging and supporting this cohort. They must evidence how their approach enables them to build trust, sustain long term engagement, and achieve positive outcomes in relation to safety, wellbeing, stability and reduced vulnerability to violence and exploitation. 
Practitioners must demonstrate credibility, authenticity, professional curiosity and appropriate boundaries, supported by training, supervision and ongoing workforce development. 
The service is expected to work closely with local authorities, criminal justice system, education providers, health services, community VCS organisations, and other VRU tertiary programmes.

records.description:
The Community Wellbeing Service for Older People, Physical Disability and Dementia aims to help people take a proactive approach to their health and wellbeing, increase independence, and prevent, reduce or delay the need for statutory services. This is achieved via support which includes, but is not limited to: peer groups, physical activities, providing information (e.g. about support in the local community and how to manage money and benefits), supporting people to live safely in their own home, and maintaining and adapting an individual’s home to their needs with low level trusted assessor equipment.

The proposed Community Wellbeing Service for Older People, Physical Disability and Dementia will replace the existing Wellbeing Services in the Community contracts, which are commissioned separately for older people, people with dementia, and people with physical disabilities through a range of Voluntary Community Sector Enterprise (VCSE) partners. 
The proposed contracts will provide services for 
•Older People (55+)
•People with dementia and their families

records.title: C0193 - AI Programme - Learning & Evaluation
records.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is developing quickly and is already affecting how communities, public services and civil society organisations operate. It brings opportunities to improve services, reduce administrative pressure and develop new approaches to community needs. It also presents risks relating to exclusion, bias, environmental sustainability and the concentration of power. The Fund wants communities and civil society organisations to play an active role in shaping how AI is developed and used. The Fund has approved AI-related funding designed to build community agency, support responsible adoption and generate practical learning for the Fund and the wider sector. The Fund’s AI-related funding portfolio currently includes three strands: • AI capacity-building uplifts in England and Scotland; • Community-Powered AI grants; and • the Pulse Network. The three strands, detailed in section 2 below, differ in their scale, purpose and delivery model. The AI Capacity Building Uplifts are being wholly funded and delivered by the National Lottery Community Fund. The Community-Powered AI and Pulse Network strands are being delivered through a collaboration between The National Lottery Community Fund, UK Community Foundations (UKCF) and CAST. UKCF is the lead partner for the Community-Powered AI and Pulse Network strands. CAST leads relevant technical workstreams and brings specialist expertise in AI, digital innovation and data ethics to both strands. The Fund provides funding, programme governance, and will hold the contract with the Evaluation Partner, helping to ensure the work delivers useful learning and benefits for communities. Given the fast-changing nature of AI, the Community-Powered AI and Pulse Network strands will take a developmental approach. As learning emerges and the external context evolves, there may be minor adjustments to delivery approaches, activities or support offers, while remaining focused on the programme's overall aims and intended outcomes. The Fund seeks to appoint a Learning and Evaluation Partner from approximately January 2027 to June 2029. The purpose of the evaluation is to generate evidence about the delivery and emerging outcomes of the Fund’s AI capacity-building uplifts and Community-Powered AI grants. The findings will help the Fund and its partners improve delivery, make informed decisions about future investment, and share transferable learning with funders, civil society organisations and others interested in supporting responsible and community-centred approaches to AI. The Learning and Evaluation Partner will also draw on relevant evidence from the Pulse Network, helping the Fund understand connections across its portfolio of AI strands without duplicating the Network’s own learning and sense-making functions. The primary audiences for the work will be: • teams within the Fund responsible for programme delivery, funding strategy and future AI-related investment; • CAST and UKCF as programme partners; • organisations receiving AI capacity-building uplifts and Community-Powered AI grants, to support adaptation and learning. A wider secondary audience will include funders, civil society organisations in the voluntary, community and social enterprise (VCSE) sector, and others interested in supporting responsible and community-centred approaches to AI.

records.title: Shaft and Silo Process Cell including Shaft Retrieval Crane
records.description:
Description
Nuclear Restoration Services Ltd (NRS) is undertaking preliminary market engagement, in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023, in relation to the potential future procurement of the Shaft and Silo Programme Process Cell including Shaft Retrieval Crane, in support of the decommissioning of the legacy Shaft and Silo ILW storage facilities at the Dounreay Site, Caithness, Scotland.
This Preliminary Market Engagement Notice is issued for information and engagement purposes only. It does not commence a procurement procedure and does not represent any commitment by NRS to award a contract.
Background and Site Context
The Dounreay Site represents one of the most complex decommissioning environments in the UK nuclear estate, combining legacy experimental facilities, constrained site conditions, and long term high hazard activities within a live, regulated nuclear site.
The Shaft & Silo programme is expected to span multiple years and is principally to design, build and carry out the operation of the facilities for retrieval, treatment and packaging of the Shaft and Wet Silo waste contents.
Indicative Scope
The Dounreay Site requires the provision of a Process Cell including Shaft Retrieval Crane; an integral part of the new Shaft & Silo Retrieval Facilities. The Process Cell consists of a series of interdependent plant items that primarily effect sorting and size reduction of the waste retrieved from the Shaft & Wet Silos, prior to consignment and grouting in 200l drums ready for characterisation. Waste from the Wet Silos is transferred to the Shaft Facility via the Waste Transfer System. 
DSRL will be engaging the market to undertake the detailed design, build, installation and commissioning of the Shaft and Silo Process Cell including Shaft Retrieval Crane.
Note: The construction of all buildings within which this scope covers are excluded from and outside the requirements of this procurement.
The scope and delivery approach remain under development and may change.

This Preliminary Market Engagement Notice is issued for information and engagement purposes only. It does not commence a procurement procedure and does not represent any commitment by NRS to award a contract.
Background and Site Context
The Dounreay Site represents one of the most complex decommissioning environments in the UK nuclear estate, combining legacy experimental facilities, constrained site conditions, and long term high hazard activities within a live, regulated nuclear site.
The Shaft & Silo programme is expected to span multiple years and is principally to design, build and carry out the operation of the facilities for retrieval, treatment and packaging of the Shaft and Wet Silo waste contents.
Indicative Scope
The Dounreay Site requires the provision of design, development, manufacture, testing and supply of specialist remotely operated equipment required to retrieve and process legacy Intermediate Level Waste from the Dounreay Shaft and Silo. The scope includes the Silo Retrieval Arm (SWORD) for manipulation and size reduction of waste within the Silo, Shaft intervention equipment (SWIFT) for in-situ intervention and size reduction activities, and remote manipulators for handling and processing retrieved waste within the Process Cell.
DSRL will be engaging the market to undertake the Design, Manufacture and Supply of Silo Retrieval Arm, Process Manipulators and Shaft Intervention Platform.
Note: The construction of all buildings within which this scope covers are excluded from and outside the requirements of this procurement.
The scope and delivery approach remain under development and may change.

records.title: AACC reviews waiting list clearance
records.description:
The All Age Complex and Continuing Care division transferred to CLCH in July 2026 under a Delegation Agreement with West & North London ICB. The Trust will be utilising time-limited, non-recurrent funding to support the backlog of reviews in order to improve service to patients and help stabilise the operational team.

The objectives are to:
• Provide a fully managed service to CLCH across the CHC pathway
• Provide safe, timely and high-quality clinical reviews/assessments;
• Complete robust reviews / assessments supported by clear evidence and professional rationale;
• Involve the individual and, where appropriate, their family, representative, care provider and relevant professionals;
• Identify changes in need, risk or care provision promptly and escalate them to CLCH;
• Maintain effective case tracking, management information and audit trails; and
• Enable CLCH to flex capacity to meet the demand of the service

The Supplier will complete c1400 FNC reviews and initially hand back any associated reassessment activity for CLCH to complete, however the contract allows the supplier to support CLCH with additional assessment capacity if demand requires. The Supplier will complete a robust FNC review by reviewing current needs, identifying material changes, gathering and triangulating evidence, engaging relevant parties, completing the required documentation and submitting a clear recommendation and rationale to CLCH. Every Review / Assessment completed by the supplier will undergo internal quality assurance.

The Supplier will provide a responsive Fast Track triage (c277) service in line with the agreed pathway. Activity will include a clinical triage, validation of documentation, liaison with representatives and providers, review of existing Fast Track arrangements, identification of changed needs, escalation of urgent risks and completion of the relevant records. If a Triage highlights a change in need, The Supplier will pass this back to CLCH to complete the full assessment however the contract allows the supplier to support CLCH with additional assessment capacity if demand requires. Should a change in need not have occurred The Supplier will update CLCH to remain on FT pathway.

The contract will be for a 6-month period with the option to extend for a further 6-month period, but there is not anticipated to be additional funding for this extension period it will simply be time for the chosen provider to complete the number of required assessments within the financial envelope if not done by forecast of end of March. This however, provides flexibility should additional funding be identified or an overrun of planned activity.

records.title: THEP Schools Collective M&E Tender
records.description:
Tower Hamlets Education Partnership (THEP) is coordinating a collective procurement exercise involving nine (9) participating schools within the London Borough of Tower Hamlets, managed by Cohesion Consulting Ltd (CCL). 
The participating Schools have come together to procure Mechanical and Electrical (M&E), Facilities Management (FM) and Premises Services jointly, seeking to achieve economies of scale, improved value for money and consistent service standards, while each school retains its own autonomy. 
The Schools are seeking experienced and reliable contractor(s) to deliver high-quality, safe, compliant and responsive Mechanical and Electrical (M&E), FM and Premises across their sites, commencing on 1st September 2027. The participating Schools are transitioning out of existing PFI arrangements, with the handover and transition process expected to commence on 1st April 2027. Contractors are expected to support the transition to ensure effective continuity of services and compliance. 
This procurement covers three services areas: 
•	M&E Services: Planned preventative maintenance (PPM), reactive and emergency maintenance, statutory compliance and associated mechanical and electrical building services. 
•	Facilities Management (FM) Services: Facilities management and associated support services, as specified within the procurement documents. 
•	Premises Services: On-site premises management and operational support, include site management functions where required. 
Not all participating Schools will require all three service areas. Each School’s individual requirements will be identified within the procurement documents, and may comprise one, two or all three service areas. 
A limited number of additional schools within the London Borough of Tower Hamlets, identified as potential participants within the procurement documents, may join the collective during the PSQ stage, prior to the issue of the Invitation to Tender (ITT). 
Where additional Schools are confirmed, the updated list of participating Schools, their required services and relevant procurement information will be made available to all bidders through the In-Tend portal. 
The final list of participating Schools and their service requirements will be confirmed prior to the issue of the ITT. 
Bidders must submit a fully compliant tender covering every participating School and all service areas required by each School, as identified within the procurement documents. Partial tenders, including submissions covering only selected Schools or selected service areas, will not be accepted.
Each Contract will be for an initial three-year period from its respective Service Commencement Date, with the option to extend for up to two further years (1+1), subject to satisfactory performance and the terms of the Contract. The Contracts will include termly and annual reviews and a break clause to support both parties should the relationship not prosper. 
The Schools' preference is to appoint a single Contractor across the collective, recognising the opportunities for shared resources, operational efficiencies, consistent standards and improved value for money. However, each School will enter into its own M&E, FM and/or Premises Services contract, incorporating the relevant standard Specification and an individual Financial Model. The Schools reserve the right to award contracts individually, including to different Contractors, in accordance with the published evaluation and award methodology.
The Schools are seeking a proactive service partner capable of delivering the safe, reliable and efficient building maintenance, facilities management and premises support. Contractors will be expected to demonstrate effective statutory compliance, effective planned preventative maintenance, a responsive reactive and emergency service, competent staffing, robust performance monitoring, effective contract management and continuous service improvement. The successful Contractor(s) will be expected to support uninterrupted School operations and provide a comfortable, sustainable learning environment for staff and students.
Contractors will be expected to demonstrate how they can achieve efficiencies across the collective whilst recognising the individual operational and service requirements of each School.
The procurement will be undertaken using a two-stage Competitive Flexible Procedure under the Procurement Act 2023, commencing with a Procurement Specific Questionnaire (PSQ), followed by an Invitation to Tender (ITT) stage for shortlisted bidders.
The ITT evaluation will comprise Written Quality (50%), Financial Evaluation (30%) and Presentation (20%). Written Quality will be evaluated collectively, with Financial and Presentation scores determined separately for each participating School, in accordance with the published evaluation methodology. 
TUPE requirements will apply where relevant, and bidders must demonstrate their ability to accommodate the employment and pension obligations associated with any transferring staff, including LGPS requirements and Admission Body Status (ABS), where applicable. 
The estimated aggregate contract value across the participating and potential additional Schools, covering the applicable M&E, FM and Premises Services, including the full five-year period and VAT, is approximately £8,428,280. This figure is indicative only, as the Schools are transitioning out of existing PFI arrangements and detailed service costs are not yet fully established. The actual contract value may therefore vary significantly from this estimate. 
The participating Schools reserve the right individually, subject to the Procurement Act 2023 and the procurement documents, to make no award where an acceptable and deliverable solution is not demonstrated.
To declare your interest in the tender and download contract documents (available free of charge), please register on  https://in-tendhost.co.uk/cohesionconsulting/aspx/Home. Once registered, please declare interest in the opportunity to access and download the full document set. 
All procurement communications, clarifications and submissions must be made through the In-Tend portal in accordance with the published procurement instructions.

records.title: Hidden Critical Elements Condition Assessment Solutions
records.description: Network Rail is undertaking preliminary market engagement to explore specialist solutions for assessing the condition of Hidden Critical Elements (HCEs) within existing railway structures. The requirement is focused on methods capable of establishing and evidencing the condition and deterioration of concealed structural elements, rather than solely locating them. Solutions may be non intrusive or hybrid and should provide interpretable results covering condition, coverage, confidence and limitations, supported by appropriate validation against known condition or targeted intrusive examination. The engagement will explore technical capability, safe deployment within the operational railway, access and possession requirements, site duration, scalability, supplier capacity, unit costs and whole life affordability. It will also help Network Rail refine its requirements, validation approach and future procurement strategy. Any subsequent trial or procurement will be subject to appropriate technical, safety, assurance, commercial and governance approvals, and participation in this engagement does not constitute a commitment by Network Rail to procure a solution.

DVSA is looking to procure the services of a supplier to deliver Level 3 Diploma/Qualification in Light and Heavy Vehicle Maintenance and Repair for approximately 48 delegates in total over the initial contract period.
DVSA Vehicle Examiners need to possess advanced technical knowledge gained through extensive hands-on experience and formal qualifications, typically at Level 3 in Vehicle Maintenance and Repair. This includes expertise in diagnosing and repairing complex systems such as engines, transmissions, electrical components, and emissions controls. They are trained to apply structured fault-finding methods, use diagnostic equipment, and interpret regulatory standards to assess vehicle compliance. Their understanding of legal and safety requirements enables them to produce accurate technical reports and confidently present evidence in court, supporting enforcement actions with professional, evidence-based assessments.
All complete courses must be delivered within a defined two-year period to align with DVSA’s overall training process and staff probation timelines.
Course modules will be delivered on a block‑release basis. The supplier must provide multiple UK training locations, preferably in the north and south, that are conveniently located near transport links to minimise delegate travel. 
Sessions shall be delivered through a blended learning model that utilises virtual training and/or e‑learning where physical attendance is not essential.
Where face-to-face training is required, it will take place at the supplier’s premises.

Expected tender notice publication: January 2027

Procurement contact / portal: DCMS procurement portal
Description of the requirement
The Notice is an update of the proposed Industry Engagement referenced in the previous UK2 Noticed issued for this programme (Ref: 20261020-000005) 
The Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) is undertaking preliminary market engagement in connection with the proposed procurement of a Principal/Main Contractor to supply works in respect of the Queen Elizabeth II Memorial programme.
The proposed appointment will involve the management, coordination and delivery of a complex, multidisciplinary programme of construction, enabling works, public realm improvements and specialist installations within St James's Park, London.
The anticipated scope includes:
Enabling works, including site establishment, surveys, site clearance, protection of existing assets, temporary works and associated utilities and infrastructure;
Demolition and removal of the existing bridge, including associated temporary works, protection of adjacent assets, disposal of materials and coordination with the wider construction programme;
Construction of the foundations and associated substructures for the new bridge, including groundworks, excavation, reinforced concrete works, drainage and associated civil engineering interfaces;
Installation of the new bridge, including site preparation, lifting and installation operations, temporary works and coordination with the separately appointed Bridge Contractor responsible for fabrication of the bridge structure, glass balustrades and incorporated paving, with the detailed allocation of installation responsibilities to be confirmed through the procurement and contractual arrangements;
Demolition and reconstruction of existing public toilet facilities, including associated building services and integration with the surrounding public realm;
Hard landscaping, including paving, pathways, groundworks, levels, drainage, external finishes and associated civil engineering works;
Soft landscaping, including sourcing and procurement of plants, trees and other planting materials, ground preparation, planting and landscape establishment;
Heritage works, including the careful dismantling, movement, relocation and reinstatement of Grade II listed structures, subject to relevant statutory consents and heritage protection requirements;
Memorial installations, including coordination and liaison with the appointed artist and relevant specialists to facilitate the installation of memorial statues, sculptures and associated elements;
Specialist contractor interfaces, including coordination with the separately procured Bridge Contractor responsible for the stainless steel bridge structure, glass balustrades, incorporated paving and associated works;
Construction management and integration, including logistics, site access, sequencing, temporary works, health and safety, quality assurance, programme coordination and stakeholder management; and
Completion and handover, including testing, commissioning where applicable, reinstatement, defects management and handover to DCMS and relevant operational stakeholders.
The works will take place within a sensitive historic park environment, requiring careful management of public access, heritage assets, existing landscape features, construction logistics and stakeholder interfaces.
Indicative Timescales
The current indicative programme anticipates award of the Stage 1 Pre-Construction Services Agreement (PCSA) in August 2027 and the Stage 2 main construction works contract in May 2028.
These dates are estimates and remain subject to procurement outcomes, programme development and the necessary DCMS approvals.
The anticipated duration and completion date of the Stage 2 construction works have not yet been determined. These will be developed during Stage 1, or as part of the formation of the Stage 2 contract, taking account of the appointed contractor's proposed construction methodology, interfaces with the specialist Bridge Contractor, wider programme dependencies and seasonal landscaping requirements.
Proposed Procurement and Delivery Approach
DCMS is considering a two-stage appointment for the Principal/Main Contractor, comprising an initial Pre-Construction Services Agreement (PCSA) for Early Contractor Involvement, construction planning, buildability review, supply-chain engagement and development of the construction price, followed by a separate commitment to the main construction works.
The proposed scope includes enabling works, demolition and reconstruction of public toilet facilities, hard and soft landscaping, relocation and reinstatement of Grade II listed structures, coordination of memorial installations with the appointed artist, and integration of the separately appointed specialist Bridge Contractor.
DCMS is considering a competitive flexible procedure under the Procurement Act 2023, incorporating an initial assessment of supplier capability and a subsequent tender stage.
The proposed arrangements include coordination with the Bridge Contractor during pre-construction and its intended subsequent novation to the Principal/Main Contractor, subject to agreed contractual arrangements and approvals.
The proposed approach remains subject to market engagement and DCMS governance approvals.

The Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) is undertaking preliminary market engagement in connection with the proposed procurement of a Bridge Contractor to supply works in respect of the Queen Elizabeth II Memorial programme.
The proposed appointment will involve the specialist design validation, prototype development, fabrication, construction and installation of a bespoke pedestrian bridge forming part of a nationally significant memorial project in central London.
The Bridge Contractor will be required to work closely and collaboratively with Foster + Partners, the appointed lead designer, and the wider design team to support technical design development and validation, prototype testing, fabrication detailing and the successful delivery of the bridge in accordance with the agreed design intent. 
The proposed scope comprises the complete integrated bridge package, including:
structural stainless steel fabrication and associated components;
specialist glass balustrades, including their supporting and fixing arrangements;
incorporated paving, finishes and associated interfaces;
structural and fabrication design validation;
prototype manufacture, testing and technical refinement;
detailed 3D and fabrication modelling;
fabrication, assembly, transportation, lifting and installation; and
associated temporary works, quality assurance and specialist supply-chain coordination.
The works will be delivered within a sensitive public realm environment and will require particular attention to architectural quality, specialist craftsmanship, technical assurance, construction logistics, programme coordination and stakeholder interfaces.
DCMS is seeking feedback from contractors capable of taking responsibility for the complete integrated bridge package, either through their own specialist capabilities or through appropriately managed specialist subcontractors.
Indicative timescales
The current indicative programme anticipates award of the Stage 1 Pre-Construction Services Agreement (PCSA) in May 2027 and the Stage 2 main fabrication and installation contract in February 2028.
These dates are estimates and remain subject to procurement outcomes, programme development and DCMS approvals. The anticipated duration and completion date of the Stage 2 works will be determined during Stage 1 or as part of the formation of the Stage 2 contract.
Proposed Procurement and Delivery Approach
DCMS is considering a two-stage appointment for the specialist Bridge Contractor, with an initial Pre-Construction Services Agreement (PCSA) to support prototype development, testing, technical design validation and refinement, followed by a separate commitment to the principal fabrication and installation works.
DCMS is considering a competitive flexible procedure under the Procurement Act 2023, with an open initial tender stage to encourage participation from the specialist market.
The Bridge Contractor is expected to be appointed initially by DCMS, with the intention of subsequent novation of that contract to the Principal/Main Contractor, subject to agreed contractual arrangements and approvals.
The proposed approach remains subject to market engagement, further consideration and DCMS governance approvals.

records.title: Provision of Consultancy Services for the Development of a Hillingdon Circus Junction Movement and Public Realm Strategy
records.description:
Hillingdon Circus is strategically located at the junction of Long Lane and the A40 Western Avenue, with Hillingdon Underground Station to the north and the Master Brewer development site occupying the land to the east of Long Lane, between the A40 and Freezeland Way.
The Circus functions as an important multimodal gateway, connecting strategic movement along the A40 with Underground, bus and coach services, alongside local walking and cycling routes. Long Lane forms an important north-south corridor, linking Ickenham and areas to the north of the A40 with Hillingdon, Uxbridge Road and neighbourhoods to the south, while also connecting local shops, schools and community facilities.
However, this strong strategic connectivity is accompanied by highway-dominated infrastructure and complex traffic movements that create significant local severance. Wide carriageways, slip roads, level changes and junction arrangements weaken connections between the station, local centre, and surrounding residential areas. Pedestrian movement is often indirect and constrained by complex crossings, level changes and highway infrastructure, while parts of the public realm suffer from poor legibility, limited greenery and anti-social behaviour, particularly around underpasses and poorly overlooked spaces.
The purpose of this study is to understand how Hillingdon Circus currently functions and to test the feasibility of three distinct options for creating a safer, greener and better-connected place, while maintaining its important transport role. The project's aim is to explore how to improve public realm and what suitable transport intervention would be best placed to:
· Support Hillingdon Circus's role as a strategic transport interchange,
· Strengthen Local town centre and creation of welcoming gateway,
· Supporting wider regeneration and growth opportunities by improving connection between local high street and new residential development.
Proposals should seek to create a high-quality and inclusive environment for pedestrians, strengthen connections to surrounding destinations, and support the needs of local communities, commuters, and visitors.
Each of the three design options should demonstrate how it responds to the following design objectives:
1. Strengthen active travel connectivity: Improve walking, cycling and wheeling connections through Hillingdon Circus and into the wider network, supporting access to the station, schools, shops, neighbourhoods, open green spaces and development sites, while encouraging healthier everyday travel.
2. Improve multimodal transport and interchange: Improve the accessibility and quality of interchange between Underground, bus, regional coach services including the Oxford Tube, walking, cycling and wheeling, while maintaining effective transport movement.
3. Reduce vehicular dominance and car dependency: Review opportunities to rationalise highway space to support active travel, planting and public realm, while maintaining necessary movement functions.
4. Improve environmental quality and green infrastructure: Reduce the effects of noise, air pollution and urban heat-island effect while increasing tree cover, biodiversity, shade and landscape quality.
5. Integrate water-sensitive design: Improve resilience to localised flooding through SuDS, rain gardens, planting and integrated landscape measures.
6. Improve safety and sense of place: Reduce anti-social behaviour and improve safety, particularly at night, in line with the women's safety audit, while strengthening the identity and arrival experience of Hillingdon Circus.
7. Create an inclusive and accessible place: Ensure streets, crossings and public spaces are direct, easy to navigate and accessible to children, older people, wheelchair users and people with reduced mobility.

records.title: CP2632-25 Open Light Touch Framework for the Provision of Short Breaks for Disabled Children and Young People in Devon
records.description:
Devon County Council has established an Open Framework for the Provision of Short Breaks for Disabled Children and Young People in Devon and is now opening its second Entry Point.
Short breaks are play and leisure opportunities which support disabled children to go to new places, spend time with friends, take part in fun and enjoyable activities, develop their independence, and try new things. These activities could be in the family home, in the community or other residential setting. A short break gives parents, carers, and families a chance to have time out and rest from caring responsibilities. Short breaks can last from a couple of hours to an evening, overnight, or weekend and can be offered during daytimes, evenings, weekends, and school holidays. Recognising that every child, young person, and family is unique, Devon County Council will secure a diverse range of high-quality short breaks provision ensuring that support is proportionate, accessible, and responsive.
This Framework enables Devon County Council to call-off and award individual packages and block contracts for placements to approved Framework Suppliers.
The Open Light Touch Framework is anticipated to continue for a period of five (5) years unless terminated in accordance with the terms of the Framework. There is the option to extend up to a further three (3) years at the discretion of the Authority.  It is anticipated that there will be two (2) Entry Points in the first year and then one (1) Entry Point every other year for the duration of the Open Framework. However, the Authority reserves the right to have more Entry Points at its discretion.
The Framework comprises the following Lots:
Lot 1: Targeted support and short breaks for children from birth up to 13 years
Lot 2: Targeted support and short breaks for older adolescents (ages 14 to 17 years)
Lot 3: Specialist provision and short breaks for children from birth up to 17 years
Suppliers may bid for one or more lots.
Any questions in relation to this tender must be raised via the messaging section of the tendering portal www.supplyingthesouthwest.org.uk.

records.title: Corporate Information Audiovisual Asset Management System
records.description:
High Level Requirements
The Science Museum Group comprises of a group of UK institutions:
- Science Museum, London
- Science & Industry Museum, Manchester
- National Science & Media Museum, Bradford
- National Railway Museum, York
- Locomotion, Shildon
- Science and Innovation Park, Wroughton
The requirement is for an internal (non-public facing) Asset Management System that colleagues across the group can use to search, manage and access audiovisual materials that have been created or commissioned by the Science Museum Group (Corporate Records).
These materials fall into three major categories, each which has its own use cases and workflows.
- Video Production. At the end of a video project, whether it is a video for one of our YouTube channels or video content for our galleries and exhibitions, the deliverables (H.264, Apple ProRes 444), the edit project (ZIP, TAR) and camera rushes will be stored for long-term reference. The expectation is that the original files will be accessed very infrequently and, in most cases, can be managed via low bitrate “access copies”.
- Oral Histories. This is a collection of interviews on a specific topic, normally audio only, but could include video. The management of such content requires consideration for time-based metadata (topics covered) as well as versioning as we may often have to produce a redacted version of an interview to remove Personally Identifiable Information.
- Complex Digital Objects. This can cover multiple scenarios, but the key one would be the storage and management of multi-file multimedia deliverables such as Macromedia Director or Unity Projects that are used throughout the museums. These are large archive packages, such as ZIP or TAR, or disc images like ISO, IMG or VDHX.
Alongside these content types would be general document storage – Microsoft office files, Adobe Acrobat – and potentially design documents – high resolution stills photography, Adobe Photoshop and Illustrator working files.
The chosen system must demonstrate support for:
- Audiovisual materials encoded using a variety of codecs, including camera files, with technical metadata extraction and “access copy” creation.
- Metadata support for hierarchical structured collections, time-based logging and building relationships between assets and titles.
- Ability to integrate with third-party tools and export assets with all associated metadata to a defined metadata standard.
- Ability to share a selection of materials with a third party for a limited time with limited permissions.
- Storage management based around 3:2:1:1:0 methodology, including the ability to schedule fixity checking across the content held.
- Support for multiple storage technologies including cloud and LTO tape.

records.description:
An integrated review of Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council’s museum service, covering Mill Green Museum & Watermill and Welwyn Roman Baths.
Mill Green brings together a working historic watermill, museum exhibitions and the borough’s archaeology, social history, art and photography collections. Welwyn Roman Baths presents the surviving bathhouse remains of the Roman villa at Dicket Mead. Together, the sites and collections tell the stories of Welwyn Garden City, Hatfield and the surrounding villages.
The review will bring together service review, community consultation, education and learning, and the service’s future role and legacy.
The intended outcomes are:
•	Identify how the service can become more relevant and accessible.
•	Identify opportunities to reach people who do not currently engage with the museum service.
•	Develop an ambitious but achievable future direction for the service.
•	Establish how the service can contribute to place, community and heritage legacy in the context of Local Government Reorganisation.

records.title: ECITB and Mersey Dee Clean Energy Scholarship Tenders 2027 (Providers)
records.description:
Engineering Construction Industry Training Board (ECITB) is pleased to announce the commencement of pre-market engagement for our forthcoming 2027 ECITB and Mersey Dee Clean Energy Scholarships procurement, which will commence in September 2027.
Scholarships are the ECITB’s flagship new entrant programmes, designed to address skills shortages in the UK engineering construction industry by providing employer-led, full-time technical training that leads directly into employment or accelerated apprenticeships. This scholarship will be delivered in conjunction with the Mersey Dee Alliance.
The programme aims to:
•	Create a sustainable pipeline of skilled entrants into the engineering construction industry, in this instance with a focus on the clean energy sectors in the northwest of England and north Wales
•	Deliver training in disciplines where regional demand has been identified through labour market intelligence.
•	Connect learners directly with employers throughout their training, rather than simply delivering college-based education.
•	Ensure learners receive a thorough grounding in industry best practise and safe behaviours before being presented to employers.
•	Support the industry's workforce needs across England, Scotland and Wales
•	Maximise available public and ECITB funding to create a sustainable and cost-effective delivery model.
Regions and Disciplines
Tenders are planned to be launched in January 2027 covering the following Regions and Disciplines:
-Regions: Mersey - Dee & North Wales region around River Dee
-Disciplines: Mechanical, Pipefitting, Fab/Weld, Electrical and General Engineering (foundation)
*These may be subject to change at ECITB’s and supporting partners discretion
About the ECITB
The Engineering Construction Industry Training Board (ECITB) is the statutory skills organisation for the Engineering Construction Industry (ECI) in Great Britain.
An Arm’s Length Body of government, the ECITB works with employers and governments to attract, develop and qualify the engineering construction workforce in a wide range of craft, technical and professional disciplines.
Employer-led, the ECITB is accountable to parliament and funded by a levy that it is required to collect from the industry.
The levy is used to support employers to train and upskill their workforce to industry standards, develop qualifications and courses that meet employer needs and regulate a network of approved training providers.
The ECITB is also an Awarding Organisation accredited by the Office of the Qualifications and Examinations Regulation (Ofqual), Qualifications Wales and Qualifications Scotland Accreditation.
The ECITB plays a vital role, along with the education sector, government and employers, in ensuring Britain has workers with the skills to meet the needs of the engineering construction industry.
We invest more than £28 million every year to enhance skills across the engineering construction industry, support growth through workforce training, and tackle labour shortages and skills gaps. This includes technical, management and professional training as well as support for apprenticeships and graduates entering industry.
About the Mersey Dee Alliance
The Mersey Dee Alliance (MDA) is a cross-border partnership supporting economic growth across North East Wales, West Cheshire and Wirral. It brings together public sector, education and business partners to support key industries, strengthen skills and employment opportunities, and attract investment.
With a strong concentration of engineering, manufacturing and energy industries, the region provides an important setting for collaboration on the skills needed to support future growth and the transition to a low-carbon economy.

records.title: C0138 - UK Fund Monitoring Evaluation & Learning
records.description: 09/The UK Portfolio is seeking a single supplier or consortium of suppliers to conduct an impact evaluation of the UK Fund and provide a range of learning services to UK Fund grantholders. The UK Fund is a funding programme that cover two distinct thematic areas: - Connected Communities - CYP and Youth Voice The first awards were granted in February 2024, focusing on Connected Communities, and in 2025 the funding expanded to Children and Young People (CYP) and Youth Voice. The key themes that run across the different thematic areas include voice, relationship building, agency, community systems and lived experience. UK Fund has adopted a funding approach that spans across and between countries, rather than being geographically restricted, and focuses on supporting well-established programmes that demonstrate proven impact, enabling them to scale and expand further. The funding also prioritises equity - targeting only communities facing poverty, disadvantage, and discrimination. Another distinguishing factor about the UK Fund is its emphasis on long-term systems change, requiring projects to include a mix of service delivery and systemic transformation in their plans. The evaluation and learning contract will adopt a collaborative, co-design approach that engages all grantholders, ensuring that all activities align with their learning needs. The supplier is also encouraged to involve the communities with whom the projects work, enabling them to shape and contribute to the learning and evaluation processes. This is particularly important given the programme’s emphasis on voice, agency, and power. Please note work commenced on the contract on the 09/11/2026 at risk. records.description:
Wakefield Council is considering options for the future delivery of its Regulation 44 Independent Visits (Children’s Homes) Service for Council-run Children's Homes.
Regulation 44 of the Children's Homes (England) Regulations 2015 requires all children's homes to receive monthly monitoring visits conducted by an Independent Person and the production of a written report following each visit. Wakefield Council currently operates a number of children's homes and is exploring the market's ability to provide this statutory service on its behalf.
Wakefield Council currently operates 12 children's homes (with 1 additional home planned) requiring monthly Regulation 44 visits. The number of homes may increase or decrease during the lifetime of any future contract and providers will therefore need to demonstrate flexibility in meeting changing requirements.

records.title: I-4988: ECH - 6 Schemes (2027)
records.description: Oxfordshire County Council has statutory duties under the Care Act 2014 in relation to the assessment of adults' care and support needs and the provision or arrangement of care and support for eligible individuals. The Council also has a broader responsibility to promote the effective operation of the local care and support market, helping to ensure that sufficient, diverse and sustainable services are available to meet the needs of Oxfordshire residents, including those who fund their own care and support. Extra Care Housing (ECH) forms an important part of the Council's approach to supporting people to live independently within their own homes and communities. ECH combines self-contained accommodation with access to on-site care and support, providing an alternative to more traditional models of home care and residential care. Oxfordshire County Council invites tenders for CQC-regulated care and support across six Extra Care Housing schemes comprising 229 homes. The successful tenderer shall deliver person-centred planned care, including medication and daily living support, and a 24-hour on-site Core Service providing emergency responses, wellbeing checks and assistance with communal meals and activities. Provision includes care within four Interim Care Pathway Flats supporting hospital discharge, admission prevention and respite. Services shall promote independence, dignity and choice, respond flexibly to changing needs and involve collaboration with housing and health partners. The contract commences on 1 April 2027 for three years.

records.title: Installation of new dust LEV in Coxon F028
records.description:
As part of a previous Lab Refurbishment programme, a dust extraction system was installed in Coxon’s F028 laboratory in 2025. When commissioning connected equipment to the installed dust extract system, a loss of LFP powder was realised into the extract duct, which coincided with an over pressurisation of the duct from a connected vac pump causing LFP powder to exit at several joints contaminating the laboratory environment.
At this time, CPI had separately engaged a 3rd party consultant, Mechon Limited, for a wider review of extract systems across CPI’s estate. Following the loss of containment, Mechon were engaged to expedite the review the affected Laboratories as a matter of priority.  
This review has resulted in a detailed specification of work and design package being produced. The provided Mechon Design and Specification is to be ultimately referenced and is required to correct the loss of containment and return F028 and F029 laboratories to service. Later works, not covered by this contract, will encompass non-critical long-term redesign of the system.

records.title: St Matthew's Primary School _ Luton
records.description:
St Matthew’s Primary School is seeking an experienced, innovative, and customer-focused catering partner to deliver high-quality school meal services for our pupils and staff.
Located in the heart of Luton’s historic Old Town, St Matthew’s is a large and vibrant primary school with a diverse school community. We are committed to providing nutritious, enjoyable, and well-presented meals that support the health, wellbeing, and educational success of our pupils.
We are inviting expressions of interest from catering providers who can demonstrate:
•	A strong track record of delivering successful school catering services.
•	Commitment to providing fresh, nutritious, and balanced meals that meet or exceed School Food Standards.
•	Innovative menu development that reflects the diversity of our school community and promotes healthy eating.
•	Excellent customer service and engagement with pupils, staff, parents, and school leadership.
•	Effective management of kitchen operations, staffing, food safety, and compliance requirements.
•	Initiatives to increase meal uptake, particularly for Universal and Free School Meals.
•	A commitment to sustainability, waste reduction, and responsible sourcing.
The successful contractor will work in partnership with the school to create a positive dining experience, encourage healthy lifestyle choices, and support the wider educational objectives of the school.
Suppliers interested in this opportunity will be expected to demonstrate financial stability, relevant experience within the education sector, robust safeguarding practices, and the capability to deliver a high-quality catering service throughout the contract term.
St Matthew’s Primary School looks forward to engaging with suppliers who share our vision of delivering exceptional food and service to our school community.

records.title: Barwell Infant School _ Leicester
records.description:
Barwell Infant School is seeking a catering partner who can deliver fresh, nutritious, and appealing meals that children genuinely want to eat. We believe that food is a fundamental part of the school day—supporting wellbeing, fuelling learning, and helping pupils develop healthy habits that last far beyond their time with us.
The ideal partner will act with honesty, integrity, and a clear commitment to putting pupils at the centre of every decision. From menu design to service style, we expect a caterer who consistently asks, “What is best for the children?” and demonstrates this through their actions, communication, and daily practice.
Lunchtimes at Barwell Infant School must be enjoyable, vibrant, and inclusive. We want a dining experience that feels warm and welcoming, where pupils are encouraged to try new foods, feel confident in their choices, and look forward to their meal each day. The right partner will bring creativity, professionalism, and a genuine passion for feeding young people well.
A key indicator of operational success will be increased meal uptake. Growth in participation will reflect not only the quality of the food, but the strength of the service, the engagement with pupils and families, and the overall dining experience delivered.
Barwell Infant School is committed to forming a collaborative, long term partnership with a caterer who shares our values and our ambition to provide an exceptional meal service for every child.

records.description:
Connect to Work is a new, voluntary supported employment initiative funded by the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP). It is the first major element of the Get Britain Working Strategy and will take a collaborative, locally led approach designed to help people with health conditions, disabilities, or other barriers, find and maintain paid work.
Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Combined Authority (CPCA) have appointed Cambridgeshire County Council as Prime Provider to manage the delivery across Cambridgeshire and Peterborough. Therefore, we are now seeking experienced providers to deliver the supported employment models as detailed below.
Connect to Work combines two supported employment delivery models:
• IPS – Individual Placement and Support
IPS is an intervention which integrates employment support alongside primary and secondary health services and other support services. For more information please see the links in the specification and ITT.
• SEQF – Supported Employment Quality Framework, intensive supported
employment for people with learning disabilities, autism, and complex
barriers. SEQF is a more intensive intervention, where in delivery terms the Participant will receive more contact and support from their Employment Specialist.
For more information please see the links in the specification and the ITT
As well as experienced providers of IPS and SEQF, we also encourage smaller voluntary and community organisations who want to learn and develop their own supported employment delivery to apply. We will provide full support and training to facilitate development of supported employment models to fidelity requirements

records.title: P5718 Arboriculture Services Contract
records.description:
The London Borough of Tower Hamlets intends to modify its existing Arboricultural Services contract (P5718) with Gristwood and Toms Limited to ensure the continued delivery of essential tree management services across the Borough's highways, parks, housing estates and open spaces.
The contract provides for the inspection, maintenance and management of the Council's tree stock, including emergency tree works, cyclical pruning and pollarding programmes, tree planting and establishment works, watering programmes, and statutory pest management activities. These services are critical to ensuring the Council continues to meet its statutory and common-law duties relating to tree safety, whilst supporting its objectives to maintain, protect and enhance the Borough's diverse tree population for the benefit of residents and visitors.
The proposed modification extends the contract term by nine months, from 1 December 2026 to 31 August 2027, to maintain service continuity while the replacement Arboricultural Services contract is concluded and mobilised. No changes are proposed to the scope of services, performance requirements, pricing structure or overall nature of the contract. Services will continue to be delivered by an Arboricultural Association Approved Contractor in accordance with all applicable legislation, industry standards and local operational requirements.

records.title: Building Safety Higher Risk Buildings Works - Framework Agreement
records.description:
Portsmouth City Council ('the council')- invited tenders from suitably qualified suppliers for inclusion onto a multi contractor framework that will be used to provide building safety projects for
several higher risk residential buildings and a mix of medium to low rise residential buildings within the Portsmouth area.
The framework will consist of 5 contractors.
This will include a 'Primary Tier' of 4 contractors and a 'Secondary Tier' of 1 contractor to provide contingency. 
The Council is aiming to have established the framework by January 2027. Once in place the framework will run for a duration of 4 years extendable by up to a further 2 years in increments
to be agreed to a maximum term of 6 years.
The value of the framework is estimated to be in the range £60m - £120m over the maximum 6 years based upon Portsmouth City Council's Building Safety Programme for high, mid and low rise works from 2025 to 2030.
The framework, although primarily for delivery of projects that cover high rise buildings with higher construction value works, will also cover approximately 30% of the Council's low - medium
rise blocks in order to package up phases of work by consideration of geography and/or efficiencies, with the remaining 70% let via other arrangements.
Whilst the project and pipeline of works are designed to provide a representation of the likely value of works procured through the framework, the actual values of call offs may vary, hence there is
no minimum or maximum values for call-off contracts, and no commitment can be made in this respect.
Although the call-off contract values may differ, the core work will be of a similar nature, i.e. of high complexity, requiring a high level of engagement from the contractor and requiring significant
resident engagement.
The framework has been established via evaluation of tenders submitted for the Mill Gate House project. The Council intends to allocate proposed pipelines of work. Each pipeline
contains building safety remediation works to 3nr. higher risk buildings. The value of each pipeline varies from £7-9M, however, may be subject to change upon development of designs.
These pipelines will streamline the procurement of contractors and allow the councils higher risk building safety remediation programme to be accelerated. The highest scoring contractor on the framework would be allocated the first pipeline of
works, and the remaining pipelines will be allocated
to 2nd, 3rd and 4th highest scoring contractors.
The award of future call-off contracts within the packages /pipelines will be subject to the Contractors performance meeting minimum KPIs.
MILLGATE PROJECT
To facilitate setting up the Framework, the contractors provided price and quality submission for the MillGate Building Safety
Remediation Project, which will be the first contract
let via the framework to the highest scoring
contractor (CBG Construction Ltd). 
This will be a two-stage procurement utilising JCT PCSA and Design and Building contracts.
Mill Gate House is a 21-storey residential block of flats located within St George's Square, Portsmouth. The building comprises 76 individual flats with a spilt between general needs social
housing and sheltered accommodation. The anticipated project value is circa £5-6 million, and works are programmed to commence on site April 2027 and last approximately one year,
FRAMEWORK SCOPE
Contractors will be expected to undertake a range of multi-disciplinary project work, taking on the role of Principal Designer and Principal Contractor (for purposes of CDM 2015 and Building Regulations 2010) to deliver building safety works though single,
two stage, and traditional procurement routes. The Contractor will be required to oversee and manage the design and construction of the works, using a range of either directly employed staff or subcontracted consultants and contractors.
The works let via the framework will typically be complex and specialist and will require a highly experienced and competent contractors to design and manage to ensure full compliance with the relevant legislation. This will involve designing and
managing works through the Building Safety Regulator (BSR) application process.
The works will also require a high degree of resident engagement and liaison to effectively manage. Works will typically be to occupied buildings and may involve either managing disruptive works whilst the residents remain in situ or assisting with the management of resident decants to temporary accommodation.

records.title: Turnkey Delivery of Onboard CCTV Remote Download & Cloud VMS
records.description:
West Midlands Trains (WM Trains) is seeking to appoint a Lead System Integrator (LSI) under a single turnkey contract to design, supply, install, and maintain an Onboard CCTV Remote Download and Cloud Video Management System (VMS).
The fundamental objective of this procurement is to deploy a cloud-managed edge architecture that entirely eliminates manual hard drive (HDD) extractions and physical depot call-outs for video retrieval, establishing a unified functional baseline across a diverse rolling stock estate.
1. Fleet Scope & Integration Strategy
The deployment covers an estimated 202 passenger multiple units (703 individual vehicles) operating across the London Northwestern Railway (LNR) and West Midlands Railway (WMR) networks, encompassing Classes 150, 172, 196, 350, and 730.
The existing CCTV estate is a multi-vendor environment comprising both legacy hybrid/analogue systems and modern IP-based Network Video Recorders (NVRs). Crucially, onboard camera replacement is strictly out of scope. The requested solution must act as an intelligent hardware/software overlay, utilising edge gateways and software federation to interface directly with the existing onboard recording equipment without displacing current camera heads.
2. Core Technical Capabilities
The overarching solution must deliver:
Automated Least-Cost Routing (LCR): Intelligent connection management prioritising depot/station Wi-Fi for routine, high-volume evidential bulk offloading, while reserving 4G/5G cellular connectivity for real-time live streaming and urgent incident triage.
Low-Latency Live Streaming: Remote visibility into onboard saloon and forward-facing camera feeds with an end-to-end latency of under 1.0 second during active security or operational incidents.
Unified Cloud VMS: A single, secure "pane of glass" interface providing dynamic timeline searching and queuing across all fleet classes. The platform must support Enterprise Single Sign-On (SSO) via standard protocols (e.g., SAML 2.0, OIDC) for seamless integration with WM Trains’ corporate identity provider, alongside secure, role-based access methods for external multi-agency stakeholders.
Automated Health Telemetry: Proactive, remote monitoring of NVR recording states, storage health, and camera availability to replace "discovery-by-failure" maintenance models.
External Stakeholder Handover: A fully digital, audited export workflow providing tamper-evident, SHA-256 hashed video packages directly to external agencies, including the British Transport Police (BTP), via secure API or digital evidence locker.
3. Turnkey Delivery & Governance Responsibilities
The appointed Lead System Integrator will hold end-to-end responsibility for the delivery and lifecycle of the solution, including:
Sourcing, supplying, and configuring all edge-gateway hardware and off-board connectivity (e.g., cellular data plans and private APNs).
Authoring the complete engineering modification substantiation packs (including CSM-RA safety justifications) in the specific formats required by varying train manufacturers (OEMs) and Rolling Stock Owners (RoSCOs).
Conducting physical vehicle installation, cabling, and fleet modification utilising RISQS-accredited personnel, scheduled dynamically around operational passenger service demands and depot stabling windows.
Providing ongoing hardware warranty, field maintenance, emergency depot spares SLAs, and SaaS platform support over the duration of the contract term (including a rolling obsolescence management plan).

records.buyer: West Mercia Police and Crime Commissioner
records.title: Photovoltaic Solar Arrays (Roof Top) at the Hindlip Estate (Phase 1 - OCC Southwell House)
records.description:
The West Mercia Police Contracts and Procurement Team, acting on behalf of the Police and Crime Commissioner for West Mercia ("the Authority"), conducted a regulated below threshold procurement under the Procurement Act 2023 for the design, supply, installation and commissioning of a rooftop Photovoltaic (PV) Solar Array installation at OCC Southwell House, Hindlip Hall Estate (Reference: EST26-2724).
The Authority's intention was to appoint a contractor for Phase 1 at OCC Southwell House, with the potential for future photovoltaic (PV) solar installation projects across the wider estate to be instructed under the resulting contractual arrangement, subject to future business need, funding availability and internal approvals.
The procurement was undertaken via the Bluelight eTendering Portal (In-Tend) and comprised the following stages:
Stage 1 - Expression of Interest (EOI)
Stage 2 - Conditions of Participation (CoP)
Stage 3 - Invitation to Tender (ITT)
Suppliers expressing an interest in Stage 1 were invited to participate in the Conditions of Participation stage. Suppliers meeting the Authority's Conditions of Participation requirements were subsequently invited to submit a tender response at Stage 3.
Tender submissions were evaluated in accordance with the criteria, weightings and methodology set out within the procurement documentation.
The evaluation comprised:
Quality Assessment - 60%
Commercial Assessment (Price) - 40%
Suitability Assessment - Pass / Fail
Following completion of evaluation and moderation, the Authority identified the Most Advantageous Tender in accordance with the published procurement methodology and now intends to enter into a contract with the successful supplier, subject to completion of the statutory standstill period and any remaining governance requirements under the Procurement Act 2023.

records.title: The Development and Delivery of Armagh City, Banbridge and Craigavon Borough Council Local Economic Partnership AI/Robotics: Empowering Business Through Awareness Programme 2027-28
records.description: The LEP is funded by the DfE Regional Balance Fund and is tasked with addressing structural economic barriers and designing local interventions. The Action Plan focuses on three priority themes 1. Land Availability and Development 2. Business Workspace Development 3. Supporting Business Growth The AI and Robotics Adoption Programme is a key strand of Theme 3 Supporting Business Growth and is open to micro small and social enterprises up to 50 employees across the Armagh City, Banbridge and Craigavon Borough Council area with a minimum 12-month trading history. The programme will be delivered in two stages. Stage 1 will provide AI and Robotics Awareness Roadshows and Workshops for up to 200 participants, helping businesses understand the practical applications and benefits of AI and robotics. Stage 2 will recruit up to 50 eligible businesses to undertake an AI and Robotics Readiness Assessment and Diagnostic Review. Businesses with an identified need will receive up to 15 hours of tailored mentoring to explore AI and robotics adoption, culminating in a bespoke Action Plan with recommendations to enhance productivity, efficiency, customer engagement and competitiveness.
