records.title: Corporate Information Audiovisual Asset Management System
records.description:
High Level Requirements
The Science Museum Group comprises of a group of UK institutions:
- Science Museum, London
- Science & Industry Museum, Manchester
- National Science & Media Museum, Bradford
- National Railway Museum, York
- Locomotion, Shildon
- Science and Innovation Park, Wroughton
The requirement is for an internal (non-public facing) Asset Management System that colleagues across the group can use to search, manage and access audiovisual materials that have been created or commissioned by the Science Museum Group (Corporate Records).
These materials fall into three major categories, each which has its own use cases and workflows.
- Video Production. At the end of a video project, whether it is a video for one of our YouTube channels or video content for our galleries and exhibitions, the deliverables (H.264, Apple ProRes 444), the edit project (ZIP, TAR) and camera rushes will be stored for long-term reference. The expectation is that the original files will be accessed very infrequently and, in most cases, can be managed via low bitrate “access copies”.
- Oral Histories. This is a collection of interviews on a specific topic, normally audio only, but could include video. The management of such content requires consideration for time-based metadata (topics covered) as well as versioning as we may often have to produce a redacted version of an interview to remove Personally Identifiable Information.
- Complex Digital Objects. This can cover multiple scenarios, but the key one would be the storage and management of multi-file multimedia deliverables such as Macromedia Director or Unity Projects that are used throughout the museums. These are large archive packages, such as ZIP or TAR, or disc images like ISO, IMG or VDHX.
Alongside these content types would be general document storage – Microsoft office files, Adobe Acrobat – and potentially design documents – high resolution stills photography, Adobe Photoshop and Illustrator working files.
The chosen system must demonstrate support for:
- Audiovisual materials encoded using a variety of codecs, including camera files, with technical metadata extraction and “access copy” creation.
- Metadata support for hierarchical structured collections, time-based logging and building relationships between assets and titles.
- Ability to integrate with third-party tools and export assets with all associated metadata to a defined metadata standard.
- Ability to share a selection of materials with a third party for a limited time with limited permissions.
- Storage management based around 3:2:1:1:0 methodology, including the ability to schedule fixity checking across the content held.
- Support for multiple storage technologies including cloud and LTO tape.

records.title: Bus Fleet Diesel and Electric Vehicles
records.description:
Correction to figures included in notice - ocds-h6vhtk-05ec46
In April 2023, Liverpool City Region Combined Authority (LCRCA) published an Assessment on Bus Franchising in the Liverpool City Region, which set out a proposed bus Franchising Scheme in accordance with the Transport Act 2000. In October 2023, the Liverpool City Region Mayor made the decision to introduce a Franchising Scheme covering the Liverpool City Region. Franchising is a legal model where buses are under the control of a public sector authority (LCRCA) who set the routes, frequency, fares and overall standard of buses in the region. The existing commercially led market will be replaced and private bus operators will no longer be able to run most services independently. Instead, bus services will be operated under franchise contracts and bus operators will bid to run the services through a competitive procurement process managed by the Combined Authority. LCRCA intend to introduce the second Tranche of franchised bus services from September 2027, covering Liverpool, Sefton and Knowsley. This follows the first Tranche of franchised bus services introduced in September 2026 covering St Helens and the Wirral. For Category 1 franchise contracts, LCRCA will provide the successful operator with a fleet of vehicles which the operator will then operate, manage and maintain the fleet throughout the franchise term. In preparation for the commencement of the Tranche 2 bus franchising programme in September 2027, LCRCA wish to procure a fleet of new vehicles including diesel and electric vehicles. A number of double-decker, single-decker and midi-sized buses are required to be delivered in May 2027 ahead of the commencement date of franchised services.

records.title: THEP Schools Collective Cleaning Tender
records.description:
Tender in-tend description text
Tower Hamlets Education Partnership (THEP) is coordinating a collective procurement exercise involving  ten (10) participating schools within the London Borough of Tower Hamlets, managed by Cohesion Consulting Ltd (CCL). 
The participating Schools have come together to procure cleaning services jointly, seeking to achieve economies of scale, improved value for money and consistent service standards, whilst each school retains its individual autonomy. 
The Schools are seeking experienced and reliable cleaning contractor(s) to deliver high-quality, consistent and responsive cleaning services across their premises, with the majority commencing on 1 September 2027. However, individual Schools may require earlier commencement dates, which will be confirmed within the procurement documents. 
The Schools' preference is to appoint a single Contractor across the collective, recognising the opportunities for shared resources, operational efficiencies, consistent standards and improved value for money. However, each School will enter into its own cleaning services contract, incorporating a standard Cleaning Specification and an individual Financial Model. The Schools reserve the right to award contracts individually, including to different Contractors, in accordance with the published evaluation and award methodology.
A further number of additional schools within the London Borough of Tower Hamlets, identified as potential participants within the procurement documents, may join the collective during the PSQ stage. Where additional Schools are confirmed, the updated list of participating Schools and relevant procurement information will be made available to all interested bidders through the In-Tend portal. The final list of participating Schools will be confirmed before the PSQ submission deadline.
Bidders must submit a fully compliant tender covering every participating School. Partial tenders will not be accepted.
Each Contract will be for an initial three-year period from its respective Service Commencement Date, with the option to extend for up to two further years (1+1), subject to satisfactory performance and the terms of the Contract. The Contracts will include termly and annual performance reviews and a break clause to support both parties should the relationship not prosper.
The Schools are seeking a proactive cleaning partner capable of delivering consistently high cleaning standards, reliable staffing and supervision, robust performance monitoring, effective contract management and continuous service improvement. Contractors will be expected to demonstrate how they can achieve efficiencies across the collective whilst recognising the individual operational requirements of each School.
The procurement will be undertaken using a two-stage Competitive Flexible Procedure under the Procurement Act 2023, commencing with a Procurement Specific Questionnaire (PSQ), followed by an Invitation to Tender (ITT) stage for shortlisted bidders.
The ITT evaluation will comprise Written Quality (50%), Financial Evaluation (25%) and Presentation (25%). Written Quality will be evaluated collectively, with Financial and Presentation scores determined separately for each participating School.
TUPE requirements will apply where relevant, and bidders must demonstrate their ability to accommodate the employment and pension obligations associated with the individual Schools, including Local Government Pension Scheme (LGPS) requirements and Admission Body Status (ABS), where applicable. 
The estimated aggregate contract value across the participating Schools, including the full five-year period and VAT and the additional potential schools, is £4,646,327. This figure is indicative only, as the majority of Schools are transitioning out of existing PFI arrangements and detailed service costs are not yet fully established. The actual contract value may therefore vary significantly from this estimate. 
The participating Schools have asked that the procurement consultancy fees for this exercise are paid by the successful Contractor(s). The successful Contractor appointed to each School will pay the consultancy fees for that School by crediting the full amount against its first invoice to the School. The fees for each School will be set out in the procurement documents, and bidders must include them in their Financial Model for that School. All fees are exclusive of VAT.
The Schools individually reserve the right, subject to the Procurement Act 2023 and the procurement documents, to make no award in respect of any or all Schools where an acceptable and deliverable solution is not demonstrated.

records.title: Best Start Family Hubs
records.description:
The national Best Start Family Hubs and Healthy Babies programme sets a refreshed direction for family and health support from April 2026 to March 2029. It builds on the learning from Sure Start, Family Hubs and Start for Life, with a clear expectation that local areas bring together health, education, early years, parenting and community support so that families can access help earlier, more easily and in places they already know and trust.
The programme places strong emphasis on early identification, prevention and reducing inequalities, particularly during pregnancy and the early years when the foundations for lifelong health, learning and development are laid. Best Start Family Hubs should provide a welcoming and inclusive front door for families, supported by a wider network of linked local services and outreach locations, so that families can receive the right support at the right time and are not left to navigate services on their own.
The updated national guidance describes Best Start Family Hubs as a key part of the Government's wider Best Start in Life strategy, supporting the ambition for more children to achieve a good level of development by age five. The model remains universal and open to families from conception to age 19, or up to 25 for young people with special educational needs and disabilities, while prioritising support for families with babies and young children.
Locally, Worcestershire already has an established Family Hubs offer across the county. This procurement will support the expansion and strengthening of the current model so that it aligns with the additional national expectations for Best Start Family Hubs and Healthy Babies, including improved access, outreach, partnership working and support for families during pregnancy and the early years.

records.title: 715890497 Precision Technic Defence Ltd Enabling Contract (EC) UK5
records.description:
Description of Procurement
The Ministry of Defence (MOD) (the “Authority”) intends to award an Enabling Contract to Precision Technic Defence Ltd (PTD) to sustain the current in-service Support Weapon Enhanced Sighting System (SWESS) capabilities through to the approved Out of Service Date (OSD) of March 2033.
The capabilities comprise:
•	SWESS Light Inline Sight Capability (OEM and Design Authority: Pixels on Target LLC), incorporating the VooDoo-S Thermal Sight and associated equipment.
•	SWESS Light Night Sight Capability (OEM and Design Authority: Envision Technologies LLC), incorporating the VooDoo-M Thermal Sight and associated equipment.
(together, the “SWESS Capabilities”).
The SWESS Capabilities support operation on the L7A2, L129A2 and L404A1 weapon systems and form part of the current in-service sighting solution used by Defence. The capabilities are Modified Off-The-Shelf (MOTS) military products that have been adapted and integrated to meet MOD operational requirements.
The Authority requires continued support and provision of the existing, modified and operationally assured SWESS Capabilities until their planned OSD. The existing contractual arrangement for the SWESS Light Inline Sight Capability has reached its available financial headroom, while the existing arrangement for the SWESS Light Night Sight Capability is approaching its available financial headroom. A replacement contractual route is therefore required to sustain both capabilities through to OSD.
The proposed contract will provide a single contractual mechanism for the support, maintenance and repair of the SWESS Capabilities, together with the technical services, Post Design Services, training, spares and accessories necessary to sustain them. It will also allow for the provision of additional SWESS units and associated ancillaries where required to support fleet management, replacement of attrition items, growth towards Total Fleet Requirement and operational demand. The scope is limited to sustaining and providing additional units of the current assured MOTS capabilities throughout their remaining service life.
Estimated Contract Value
£60,000,000 (estimated maximum value)
The advertised contract value is the maximum estimated value of all potential orders that may be placed under the contract during its term. It does not represent a guaranteed level of expenditure. The Authority reserves the right not to place any orders under the contract and is not obliged to spend the full advertised value, or any value, during the lifetime of the contract.
Contract Duration
From contract award until 31 March 2033.
The contract will expire no later than the approved OSD of March 2033 and is intended solely to sustain the current assured MOTS capabilities throughout their remaining service life, including the provision of additional units and associated ancillaries where required. The Authority does not intend to use the contract to procure a replacement capability. Before the SWESS Capabilities reach OSD, the Authority will reassess its future requirements and determine the appropriate procurement strategy, including competition where appropriate.

records.title: Provision of Consultancy Services for the Development of a Hillingdon Circus Junction Movement and Public Realm Strategy
records.description:
Hillingdon Circus is strategically located at the junction of Long Lane and the A40 Western Avenue, with Hillingdon Underground Station to the north and the Master Brewer development site occupying the land to the east of Long Lane, between the A40 and Freezeland Way.
The Circus functions as an important multimodal gateway, connecting strategic movement along the A40 with Underground, bus and coach services, alongside local walking and cycling routes. Long Lane forms an important north-south corridor, linking Ickenham and areas to the north of the A40 with Hillingdon, Uxbridge Road and neighbourhoods to the south, while also connecting local shops, schools and community facilities.
However, this strong strategic connectivity is accompanied by highway-dominated infrastructure and complex traffic movements that create significant local severance. Wide carriageways, slip roads, level changes and junction arrangements weaken connections between the station, local centre, and surrounding residential areas. Pedestrian movement is often indirect and constrained by complex crossings, level changes and highway infrastructure, while parts of the public realm suffer from poor legibility, limited greenery and anti-social behaviour, particularly around underpasses and poorly overlooked spaces.
The purpose of this study is to understand how Hillingdon Circus currently functions and to test the feasibility of three distinct options for creating a safer, greener and better-connected place, while maintaining its important transport role. The project's aim is to explore how to improve public realm and what suitable transport intervention would be best placed to:
· Support Hillingdon Circus's role as a strategic transport interchange,
· Strengthen Local town centre and creation of welcoming gateway,
· Supporting wider regeneration and growth opportunities by improving connection between local high street and new residential development.
Proposals should seek to create a high-quality and inclusive environment for pedestrians, strengthen connections to surrounding destinations, and support the needs of local communities, commuters, and visitors.
Each of the three design options should demonstrate how it responds to the following design objectives:
1. Strengthen active travel connectivity: Improve walking, cycling and wheeling connections through Hillingdon Circus and into the wider network, supporting access to the station, schools, shops, neighbourhoods, open green spaces and development sites, while encouraging healthier everyday travel.
2. Improve multimodal transport and interchange: Improve the accessibility and quality of interchange between Underground, bus, regional coach services including the Oxford Tube, walking, cycling and wheeling, while maintaining effective transport movement.
3. Reduce vehicular dominance and car dependency: Review opportunities to rationalise highway space to support active travel, planting and public realm, while maintaining necessary movement functions.
4. Improve environmental quality and green infrastructure: Reduce the effects of noise, air pollution and urban heat-island effect while increasing tree cover, biodiversity, shade and landscape quality.
5. Integrate water-sensitive design: Improve resilience to localised flooding through SuDS, rain gardens, planting and integrated landscape measures.
6. Improve safety and sense of place: Reduce anti-social behaviour and improve safety, particularly at night, in line with the women's safety audit, while strengthening the identity and arrival experience of Hillingdon Circus.
7. Create an inclusive and accessible place: Ensure streets, crossings and public spaces are direct, easy to navigate and accessible to children, older people, wheelchair users and people with reduced mobility.

The Authority wishes to develop a light-touch regime framework for independent special schools and non-maintained schools, providing a consistent and proportionate approach for use by local authorities across the Eastern Region, in conjunction with Commission East.
Norfolk County Council, working in partnership with Improvement East and regional colleagues, wishes to invite Independent Special School providers to a market engagement event on 26 November 2026 at 10:00am.
The purpose of the event is to share Norfolk's and the wider Eastern Region's strategic priorities and commissioning intentions for specialist education provision, including improving sufficiency and sustainability, supporting high-quality provision closer to children's local communities, and strengthening collaborative, relational commissioning with providers.
The event will provide an opportunity for providers to hear about future developments and emerging needs across the region and to gather provider feedback to inform inform future commissioning and procurement planning.
This event forms part of our early market engagement activity and does not constitute the commencement of any formal procurement process.
Further details, including agenda and joining arrangements, will be circulated to registered attendees.
Providers wishing to attend or receive future communications regarding this engagement should register their interest by contacting:
Ian Jansens (cs.commissioning@norfolk.gov.uk) or Gemma Coxen ( Commission East event organiser) commission.east@norfolk.gov.uk.

records.title: HDD Horizontal Directional Drilling Framework
records.description:
NGN invites tenders from suitably qualified and experienced suppliers for the provision of Horizontal Directional Drilling (HDD) services to support the delivery of NGN's operational programmes across its gas distribution network. 
NGN's estimated annual expenditure under the Framework Agreement is approximately £1.2 million. This value is provided for indicative planning purposes only and does not constitute any guarantee, commitment or representation regarding the volume, nature, frequency or value of work that may be awarded during the term of the Framework Agreement.
1.Purpose of the Framework 
The purpose of the framework is to ensure NGN has access to competent, capable and responsive suppliers able to deliver directional drilling services safely, compliantly and efficiently in support of core operational activities, including: 
Gas Mains Replacement 
Reinforcement works 
Gas Mains Connections 
Diversions 
 The framework will provide operational resilience, flexibility of capacity and value for money across all NGN operational areas. 
2. Core Service Deliverables 
The Supplier shall provide horizontal directional drilling services as instructed by NGN from time to time, including: 
Safe, compliant execution of horizontal directional drilling works to facilitate the installation of polyethylene (PE) gas mains 
Installation of PE pipework with nominal outside diameters of:  
Up to 125mm O.D. 
180mm O.D. 
250mm O.D. 
315mm O.D. 
355mm O.D. 
Provision, operation and maintenance of all drilling plant, equipment, tooling and resources required to deliver the works 
Supply of competent, trained and accredited personnel appropriate to the works undertaken  
Delivery of works in accordance with NGN specifications, industry standards and all applicable statutory and regulatory requirements 
3. Call‑Off and Work Instruction Deliverables 
For each call‑off or works instruction, the Supplier shall: 
Accept and resource works in accordance with the instructed programme and priorities 
Attend site as instructed and coordinate activities with NGN operational representatives and other contractors where required 
Deliver the works within the agreed timescales and constraints set out at call‑off stage 
Comply with any site‑specific requirements confirmed by NGN at call‑off stage 
4. Health, Safety and Environmental Deliverables 
The Supplier shall: 
Comply at all times with NGN Health & Safety policies and procedures 
Ensure all personnel are competent, trained and appropriately accredited for the works undertaken 
Provide method statements and risk assessments as required by NGN 
Manage environmental impacts associated with drilling activities in accordance with legal and NGN requirements 
Immediately report accidents, incidents, near misses and unsafe conditions in line with NGN procedures 
5. Management and Supervision Deliverables 
The Supplier shall provide: 
Effective site supervision for all drilling activities 
A competent point of contact for operational coordination and issue resolution 
Adequate management oversight to ensure quality, safety and compliance 
Cooperation with NGN audits, inspections and assurance activities 
6. Reporting and Records Deliverables 
The Supplier shall maintain and provide, as required: 
Accurate records of works completed under each call‑off 
Evidence of compliance with safety, quality and technical requirements 
Progress updates and completion confirmations as instructed by NGN 
Any documentation reasonably required to support performance monitoring and assurance 
7. Performance and Service Level Deliverables 
The Supplier shall meet the performance standards set out in the Framework Agreement, including: 
Compliance with agreed KPIs and SLAs 
Timely delivery of works 
Quality of workmanship 
Responsiveness to NGN instructions and operational priorities 
Performance will be monitored through NGN's contract management processes, including regular review meetings where required. 
8. Interfaces and Exclusions 
Unless expressly stated in the relevant call‑off: 
The Supplier's obligations are limited to the delivery of directional drilling services 
Activities such as traffic management, reinstatement, permits or third‑party services are excluded and will be instructed separately by NGN where required 
Surveys are excluded from the standard directional drilling rates. Where expressly instructed and authorised within the relevant Call-Off and Purchase Order, surveys shall be paid using the applicable Schedule 2 rate 
9. Continuous Improvement 
The Supplier shall support continuous improvement by: 
Engaging in performance reviews with NGN 
Identifying opportunities to improve safety, efficiency or service delivery 
Implementing agreed improvement actions within reasonable timescales 
10. Performance Management, KPIs and Service Level Agreements 
10.1 General 
The Supplier shall deliver the Services in accordance with the performance requirements set out in this Section. Performance will be monitored by NGN throughout the Framework Term to ensure services are delivered safely, compliantly, and in line with operational requirements. 
Failure to meet the KPIs or SLAs may result in escalation, the implementation of a Performance Improvement Plan, or other remedies available to NGN under the Framework Agreement. 
10.2 Service Level Agreements (SLAs) 
SLA 10.2.1 - Mobilisation and Attendance 
The Supplier shall attend site in accordance with the priority of the works instruction: 
Emergency / urgent works: attendance within [4] hours of instruction 
Planned works: attendance in line with the agreed programme 
Target: 95% compliance per reporting period. 
SLA 10.2.2 - Programme Adherence 
Directional drilling works shall be completed in accordance with the agreed call‑off programme and timescales. 
Target: 95% of works completed within agreed timescales. 
SLA 10.2.3 - Health & Safety Compliance 
The Supplier shall comply fully with NGN Health & Safety requirements, approved RAMS, and statutory obligations. 
Targets: 
Zero fatalities 
Zero prohibition notices 
100% compliance with approved RAMS and NGN safety procedures 
SLA 10.2.4 - Quality of Works 
Works shall be completed right‑first‑time with no defects or rework attributable to the Supplier. 
Target: 98% of works completed without defect or rework. 
SLA 10.2.5 - Incident Reporting 
All accidents, incidents and near misses shall be reported in accordance with NGN procedures. 
Target: 
Immediate verbal notification 
Written report submitted within 24 hours 
SLA 10.2.6 - Site Behaviour and Coordination 
The Supplier shall cooperate fully with NGN operational teams and other contractors and conduct all site activities professionally. 
Target: No substantiated complaints attributable to the Supplier. 
10.3 Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) 
KPI 10.3.1 - Responsiveness 
Timely response to NGN instructions, communications and operational queries. 
Target: 95% of communications responded to within one working day. 
KPI 10.3.2 - Resource Availability 
Ability to provide adequate labour, plant and equipment to meet NGN call‑off requirements. 
Target: 95% of call‑offs accepted and resourced as instructed. 
KPI 10.3.3 - Reporting and Records 
Accuracy and timeliness of required records, reports and evidencing of completed works. 
Target: 100% of required reports submitted on time and complete. 
KPI 10.3.4 - Customer and Stakeholder Impact 
Minimisation of adverse impact on customers, highways and third parties. 
Target: No avoidable customer complaints attributable to the Supplier. 
KPI 10.3.5 - Environmental Compliance 
Compliance with environmental controls and requirements associated with drilling activities. 
Targets: 
Zero environmental enforcement notices 
Demonstrable compliance with NGN environmental procedures 
10.4 Management Information 
The Supplier shall provide management information to support performance monitoring, including: 
Summary of works delivered 
Performance against each KPI and SLA 
Incidents, near misses and corrective actions 
Resource availability and capacity issues 
Management information shall be provided monthly, or more frequently where reasonably required by NGN. 
10.5 Performance Review and Escalation 
Performance against KPIs and SLAs will be reviewed as part of NGN's contract management arrangements. Where performance falls below required standards, NGN may: 
Require a Performance Improvement Plan 
Escalate performance concerns through governance routes 
Restrict future call‑offs 
Apply other contractual remedies, including suspension or removal from the framework, where persistent underperformance occurs

records.title: CP2771-26 - Coroners Service Body Transportation
records.description:
The Authority is seeking Bids to establish a Closed Framework for the provision of a county-wide Coroner Body Removal and Transportation Service on behalf of HM Coroner for Devon. The Framework will be structured into geographical lots to ensure comprehensive service coverage across the county.
The service supports the statutory responsibilities of HM Coroner in investigating deaths that are sudden, unexplained, violent, unnatural or where the cause of death is unknown. The Supplier will be responsible for the dignified, professional and timely collection and transportation of deceased persons from locations throughout Devon to Designated Mortuary facilities or approved body storage facilities.
A Framework will be formed with successful Bidders being promoted onto the relevant Lot(s). Following Framework award, the Authority will enter into a Call-Off Contract with each successful Supplier promoted to that Lot. Individual Service Requests will then be allocated in accordance with the Service Allocation Procedure set out in the Framework Agreement, without further competition. 
The estimated total value of the Framework over the initial four (4) year term is approximately £2,300,000 excluding VAT. Should the Framework be extended for a further two (2) years the total estimated value for the whole six (6) years is approximately £3,500,000 excluding VAT. However, the Authority gives no guarantee as to the actual value of the Call-off Contracts under the Framework.

records.title: Target Hardening (Sanctuary Scheme)
records.description:
A Sanctuary Scheme is a multi-agency, survivor-centred initiative which aims to enable households who are experiencing Domestic Abuse to remain safely in their own homes by installing a 'Sanctuary' in the home and through the provision of support to the household. This is sometimes referred to as "target hardening".
The Target Hardening Property Scheme for Worcestershire is being commissioned in conjunction with all six District Councils (Bromsgrove, Malvern Hills, Redditch, Worcester City, Wychavon & Wyre Forest) in Worcestershire. The intention is to create a single, high quality, responsive commissioned service across the County to provide Target Hardening to various levels within existing accommodation to enable survivors of Domestic Abuse to remain in their own homes.
Sanctuary Schemes are referred to in the Domestic Abuse Act 2021, which places a strong emphasis on supporting survivors of domestic abuse and their children within safe accommodation.

records.title: Tender for Residential and Nursing Care Home Partnership Framework in Herefordshire
records.description:
Herefordshire Council is seeking to establish a multi-provider Care Home Partnerships Framework for the provision of residential care, nursing care and other associated care home services for adults with eligible care and support needs (the 'Services').
This procurement establishes an Open Framework Scheme under section 49 of the Procurement Act 2023.  This Tender Notice relates to the opportunity to apply for admission to the first Herefordshire Care Home Partnerships Framework (the Framework) within the Open Framework Scheme.
The Framework will support the delivery of long-term partnership arrangements between the Council and care home providers. The Services under the Open Framework Scheme and the Framework are 'light touch' as defined by section 9 of the Procurement Act 2023 and are governed by the rules relating to light touch contracts under the Procurement Act 2023.
The Framework will be available to residential and nursing care providers operating eligible care home services and is intended to support approximately 700 to 750 Council-funded placements at any one time across the market, with an anticipated 500 to 550 placements being delivered through formal partnership arrangements.
The Council has a Partnership and Provider Support Programme which this Open Framework Scheme is part of. The programme is an initiative for all providers commissioned through the Community Wellbeing Directorate of Herefordshire Council and is designed to support genuine collaborative working between Herefordshire Council and providers, promoting high-quality services, improved resident outcomes and a sustainable local care market. Providers admitted to the Framework may participate as a Framework Provider, Partner Provider or Strategic Partner Provider. Eligibility for each level is determined by the applicable Framework requirements, including any required commitment of capacity at the tendered Partnership Rate. Different levels of participation attract different engagement, development and support opportunities.
The Open Framework will have a maximum duration of eight years and an estimated maximum value of approximately £484 million over the full term. The Council does not guarantee that the Open Framework Scheme will continue for the full term of 8 years and no guarantee is given as to the actual value of any framework agreement under the Open Framework Scheme, or any call-off contracts entered under any framework agreement.
The Open Framework Scheme will be re-opened to new providers at least once in the first three years following the award of the first Framework and at least once during each subsequent five-year period until the expiry of the scheme. Herefordshire Council reserves the right to re-open the Open Framework Scheme at additional intervals where it considers this necessary to support market development, increase provider participation, respond to changes in service demand, address emerging care needs, encourage innovation or maintain sufficient capacity across the sector.
Neither admission to the framework nor any ranking or partnership designation guarantees a minimum number or value of placements. Placements remain subject to assessed need, suitability, resident choice, capacity, the applicable call-off mechanism and the Council's statutory duties.
The Council has considered the use of lots and has structured the procurement into lots reflecting the categories of care required by Herefordshire residents. The service is divided into 2 Lots, under which there are Categories of Care for which providers are required for submit a tender for.  These are:
Lot 1 - Older Persons Residential and Nursing Care
Lot 2 - Working Age Adults
Each Lot contains specific Categories of Care which must be applied for separately. Providers will be evaluated for admission to each lot against the published conditions of participation and award criteria, including quality and price, using the weightings and methodology set out in the tender documents. Individual placements will subsequently be allocated in accordance with the published placement process, taking account of assessed need, suitability, availability, lawful resident choice, Provider Status and Provider Ranked Score.
Across both lots, placements will be subject to assessed need, suitability, availability and lawful resident choice. Eligible care homes will normally be considered in order of Provider Status, then Provider Ranked Score within each level. For Lot 2 (Working Age Adults), matching will reflect specialist support requirements and relevant family and community connections, with searches extended beyond Herefordshire where suitable local provision is unavailable. Any objectively justified departure from the normal placement order will be recorded.
The Council is seeking to award multiple contracts to eligible providers who meet the requirements for each of the Lots. Bidders are referred to the invitation to tender document for full details as it contains specific rules on how bidders may submit their response. Providers may be awarded multiple Lots. Subject to satisfying the conditions of participation and award criteria applicable to the relevant lot and Category of Care (as defined in the invitation to tender), there is no maximum number of providers that may be admitted to a particular Lot under the Framework.
Bidders are referred to the invitation to tender and procurement documentation for full details.

records.description:
NHS Wales Shared Services Partnership (NWSSP), on behalf of Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board (CTM UHB), intend to award for the design, manufacture, supply, delivery, installation, testing and commissioning of a replacement stainless-steel racking system within the Sterile Services Store at Royal Glamorgan Hospital, Llantrisant.
The requirement is for a fixed 316-grade stainless steel racking solution that increases storage capacity, improves operational efficiency and safe manual handling practices, and supports the secure storage of sterile instrument trays within a healthcare environment. The successful contractor will be responsible for undertaking site surveys, detailed design, manufacture, installation, testing, load certification and commissioning of the system, together with the provision of all associated compliance documentation, staff training, warranty support and post-installation review.
The requirement was previously advertised through an open competitive procurement process under reference CTM-ITT-62567. No tender responses were received prior to the submission deadline. Following the conclusion of the competition, the Health Board has elected to proceed with a direct award in order to secure delivery of the requirement and maintain the planned implementation programme.
This notice is being published for transparency purposes to provide visibility of the Health Board's intention to award the contract and the procurement route being utilised. It ensures the proposed award is openly communicated and provides transparency around the contracting decision.

records.title: DHSC: Health Survey for England 2028-31
records.description:
The Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) is preparing to procure the future delivery of the Health Survey for England (HSE) for the 2028–2031 survey years. HSE is the principal national survey used to measure and monitor the health of adults and children living in private households in England. It provides nationally representative information on health status, health-related behaviours, long-term conditions, disease prevalence and health inequalities, combining interview data with physical and biological measurements. Its findings support national and local policymaking, inform the planning of health services and enable monitoring of trends over time.
The proposed requirement covers end-to-end survey delivery, including survey development, sampling, participant recruitment, mixed-mode data collection, physical and biological measurements, laboratory services, data processing, statistical analysis, reporting, publication support and data archiving.
The successful supplier will be expected to support the continued delivery and modernisation of HSE, including a phased transition towards an online-first mixed-mode approach, while maintaining data quality, representativeness, inclusivity and continuity with the established HSE time series.
The contract will cover two principal and related workstreams:
Workstream 1: Core HSE delivery –Delivery HSE for each of the 2028, 2029, 2030 and 2031 survey years.
Workstream 2: Core HSE Modernisation Programme - In parallel with Core HSE Delivery, an agreed programme of research, development, testing and evaluation to support the future development of HSE 
The contract is expected to commence on 5th May 2027 and support delivery of the 2028, 2029, 2030 and 2031 survey years, with an end date of 31 July 2033 to allow completion of all associated processing, analysis, reporting, publication support, data deposit, archiving, transition and exit activities.
The proposed contract may include options to extend delivery to an additional survey year (2032) and to commission additional services or activities related to the core requirement. Any options would be exercised at DHSC’s discretion, subject to need, funding and the terms of the contract. Full details of the requirement and any contractual options will be set out in the tender documents.
Preliminary market engagement was carried out in October 2026 to share the draft specifications, proposed procurement approach, selected draft contract documents and timetable, and to invite feedback from potential bidders. We have now considered the questions and comments received and are sharing our responses in a Q&A document to provide further clarity ahead of the tender, which is scheduled for publication during the week commencing 14th December. The specifications are being updated to incorporate relevant feedback and will be made available when the tender is published.

records.title: SCE0078 - Breastfeeding Peer Support Service for Mothers in Hospital
records.description:
This is a Provider Selection Regime (PSR) intended approach notice. The awarding of this contract is subject to the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023. For the avoidance of doubt, the provisions of the provisions of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 do not apply to award.
Leicester City Council (The Authority) is intending to follow the Most Suitable Provider Process to award a contract for the provision of Breastfeeding Peer Support Service for Mothers in Hospital (SCE0078).
This service is a hospital-based, nurse-led service delivered within University Hospitals of Leicester (UHL) to support new mothers and parents who are breastfeeding or wish to breastfeed. The service forms a key part of Leicester's Warm Chain of Breastfeeding Support, providing families with timely, compassionate, and evidence-based infant feeding support from pregnancy through to the postnatal period. 
The service aims to improve breastfeeding initiation, continuation, and overall infant feeding outcomes by providing accessible support during a critical stage of the breastfeeding journey. Trained Breastfeeding Peer Supporters work alongside clinical teams within UHL to engage with families before discharge, offering practical assistance, emotional encouragement, and tailored information to meet individual needs. The service originated through the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) funded Best Start for Life Workforce Pilot, which focused on improving outcomes during the first 1,001 critical days of a child's life. Recognising the significant health benefits associated with breastfeeding for both infants and parents, the project was established to strengthen local breastfeeding support pathways and reduce health inequalities across Leicester. 
The relevant CPV code for this contract is: Community Health Service - 85323000-9. The award decision makers for this procurement process are: 
Rob Howard - Divisional Director for Public Health
Mohammed Irfan - Head of Finance
Siobhan Paterson, Social Care, Education and Public Health Procurement Category Manager
Procurement Strategic Panel
Please note that the dates provided in this notice are indicative and may be subject to change. This contract is VAT exempt. This is not a below-threshold open competition procurement as stated within the Procedure Type. This is an intention notice to follow the Most Suitable Provider process under Provider Selection Regime 2023.

records.description:
This is a Provider Selection Regime (PSR) Urgent Award notice. The awarding of this contract is subject to the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023. For the avoidance of doubt, the provisions of the Procurement Act 2023 and the Procurement Regulations 2024 do not apply to this award. The publication of this notice states that a contract has already been awarded.  
The award of this contract is for the urgent provision of a Referral Management Service (RMS) to facilitate appropriate ADHD and Autism assessment referrals to most appropriate pathways.
The service aims to provide a consistent screening/triage function, applying thresholds (clinical and functional) that determine the most appropriate support including accessing a formal diagnostic assessment.
Over the last 12 months, the ICB has undergone significant organisational changes and, at the direction of NHS England, has made substantial staffing reductions. These changes have unfortunately impacted on the ICB's capacity to procure and mobilise an RMS which was required to be mobilised within 26/27 to urgently help improve quality and reduce costs.  
The RMS is a pilot with an initial contract term of 12 months, and an option to extend 12 months. The optional 12 months would allow the ICB an appropriate timeframe to analyse and assess the impact of the pilot. Subject to the pilot's success, the additional 12 months will also allow the ICB sufficient time to consider the future service model and to undertake any necessary procurement activity under the Healthcare Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations (PSR) 2023.

records.title: Homes Off the Streets Programme - Clearing House & Tenancy Sustainment Teams
records.description:
Transport for London (TfL) is procuring on behalf of the Greater London Authority (GLA), and invites suitably qualified suppliers to participate in, an Open Procedure for the delivery of services under the Mayor's Homes Off the Streets (HOTS) programme. This recommissioning process presents a vital opportunity to reshape the future of rough sleeping services to achieve the Mayor's Rough Sleeping Plan of Action, (https://www.london.gov.uk/programmes-strategies/housing-and-land/mayors-priorities-londons-housing-and-land/homelessness/services-people-experiencing-homelessness-including-sleeping-rough/mayors-rough-sleeping-plan-action) with the ambitious goal of ending rough sleeping in London by 2030. We are seeking to transform service delivery models to preventing returns to rough sleeping, and ensure targeted sustainable routes off the streets.
There are seven lots in total. This procurement covers the delivery of a pan-London Clearing House service and six Tenancy Sustainment Team (TST) services, including five geographic sub-regional TST lots that form part of the Clearing House partnership, and one pan-London Private Rented Sector (PRS) TST which is a standalone service.
These services support residents with a history of rough sleeping to access, sustain, and thrive in long‑term stable housing.
1. Clearing House (Lot 1)
A single pan‑London contract delivering:
• Coordination of referrals, property nominations and allocations
• Partnership working with housing associations and support providers
• Management of the 3,700+ home Clearing House partnership
• Providing the Clearing House system used by stakeholders to make referrals and advertise homes
2. Tenancy Sustainment Teams (TST) (Lots 2-6)
The TSTs will provide floating long-term support to tenants in Clearing House accommodation. Working in partnership with the Clearing House and landlords, the service will deliver client assessments and on-going tenant support around:
• Tenancy sustainment
• Access to employment, training and education
• Personal wellbeing, community integration and independence
TST lots are structured to mirror the London housing sub-regions, as follows:
• Lot 2 - North Central
• Lot 3 - North East
• Lot 4 - South East
• Lot 5 - South West
• Lot 6 - North West
3. Private Rented Sector (PRS) Tenancy Sustainment Team (TST) (Lot 7)
PRS TST will provide short-term floating support to clients at the point that they first move into private rented sector accommodation. They will manage referrals and assessments and provide support around:
• Setting up a tenancy, including utilities and bills
• Understanding tenancy rights and responsibilities
• Tenancy sustainment
• Personal wellbeing, community integration and independence
Bidders may apply for multiple lots; however the total annual value of awards will be limited to a maximum of 50% of the bidder's annual turnover.
All lots include a core element and General Optional services to support increased caseloads. Lot 7 additionally includes a Specific Optional services element to deliver a PRS Tenancy Rescue service offer, consisting of crisis intervention for tenants at imminent risk of losing PRS accommodation.
Contract start date is estimated to be 1st April 2027. Contract duration will be of three (3) years and options to extend the contract for a further period of up to three (3) years, exercisable in one or more periods. The maximum duration of the contract (including all extensions) will be no more than six (6) years.

records.title: 2026-072 Future Price Control Frameworks
records.description:
Ofgem is seeking support from a supplier to inform its Future Frameworks project, which is considering what the next generation of network price controls could look like beyond 2031. While RIIO has evolved significantly since its introduction in 2013, the energy sector is entering a period of unprecedented change driven by electrification, increasing network investment requirements, strategic system planning, changing patterns of energy demand, advances in flexibility markets and rapid technological development, including artificial intelligence.
The requirement forms part of Ofgem’s wider Reimagining Network Regulation programme and builds on work previously undertaken through the Future Systems and Network Regulation (FSNR) review. The purpose of this contract is to obtain independent expert analysis on how changes in the external environment and developments in Ofgem’s own regulatory capabilities may inform the design of future regulatory frameworks. In particular, the work will explore how enhanced data, digital, Intelligent Oversight and AI-enabled capabilities could create opportunities for alternative approaches to setting allowances, incentives, performance measures and accountability arrangements for gas and electricity network companies.
Building on and advancing the work undertaken in FSNR, the supplier is expected to assess the relative strengths, weaknesses, risks and opportunities of different future framework options. The supplier should recommend a list of potential options for further consideration against the RIIO model, such as enhanced planning-based approaches, more adaptive and responsive ex ante regulatory arrangements and models with a greater focus on monitoring. The work will help Ofgem understand which options warrant further consideration, what enabling capabilities would be required to deliver alternative models, and what elements of new approaches could be tested during RIIO-3 and ED3 to inform future policy decisions. 
This contract is intended to provide strategic insight rather than develop a detailed post-2031 price control design. The outputs from the supplier will support Ofgem’s long-term thinking on how network regulation can continue to deliver affordable bills, resilient networks, high-quality service and effective delivery of Net Zero objectives in an increasingly digital and data-enabled environment.
The work should consider two linked developments: 
	* Changes in the external sector context, including the continuing scale and pace of electricity transmission build, NESO led strategic planning, demand uncertainty, flexibility, gas demand uncertainty, and the implications of future gas disconnections or decommissioning. 
	* Changes in Ofgem’s own regulatory capability, particularly through Data Transformation, Intelligent Oversight and AI-enabled regulation, which may provide faster, deeper and more granular insight into company performance, delivery risks and efficient costs. 
The central question for the work is: 
	*What opportunities do improved intelligence, data and AI capabilities create for alternative approaches to setting cost allowances, outputs, performance thresholds, standards and incentives for gas and electricity network companies from 2031 onwards?

records.title: 2026-085 IAM Training
records.description:
Recent reviews of the UK utility sectors, including the Independent Water Commission’s (Cunliffe) Report, have highlighted the importance of robust asset management, engineering assurance and asset health oversight in supporting the resilience of critical infrastructure. In response, Ofgem is enhancing its approach to asset assurance across the gas and electricity sectors through the establishment of the Asset Health Inspectorate (AHI).
The AHI will undertake a programme of audits and inspections to assess the effectiveness of asset management systems, governance arrangements and maintenance practices operated by regulated network companies. This includes reviewing asset management processes, maintenance records and 
the condition of assets in the field, as well as investigating significant network incidents where appropriate.
To support this work, Ofgem is developing specialist engineering and asset management capability across its workforce. The Institute of Asset Management (IAM) Certificate qualification has been identified as a key foundation-level training programme to equip staff with a practical understanding of asset management principles, asset lifecycle management, risk-based decision making and recognised industry good practice. 
Ofgem is therefore procuring the services of a supplier as a suitably qualified training provider to deliver IAM Certificate training to Ofgem staff and support delegates in preparing for the associated IAM Certificate examination.

records.title: Provision of Payment Gateway Services

amendments.description:
DVLA has modified the existing Payment Gateway Services Contract by extending the contract term for an initial period of twelve (12) months, for the period of 1 June 2027 to 31 May 2028, with the option to extend for a further period of up to six (6) months, for the period of 1 June 2028 to 30 November 2028, if required. 
The modification is necessary to ensure the continued provision of critical payment gateway services whilst the replacement procurement is completed and the successor service is mobilised, implemented, integrated, tested and transitioned into live operation
amendments.rationale:
Need for modification brought about by circumstances which a diligent contracting authority/entity could not foresee: ****AMENDMENT TO PREVIOUS NOTICE ****** - We were unable to make the necessary amendments to the previously published notice through the portal. (Notice Number: 2026/S 000-108786  notice reference number: 2026-500337 )
This update is solely to correct an administrative error in how the contract value was recorded in the previously published notice. The actual contract value remains unchanged, and all other information is as previously published
Justification for Modification 
During the planning and development of the replacement Payment Gateway Services procurement, Ministerial decisions relating to the implementation of the Electronic Vehicle Excise Duty (eVED) regime introduced additional requirements and dependencies that could not have been fully anticipated when the contract was awarded. As a result, further time has been required to define requirements, complete technical, governance and commercial activities, and progress the replacement procurement. 
The extension is necessary to maintain continuity of critical payment services whilst procurement, implementation, integration, testing and transition activities are completed. The modification is a permitted modification under Regulation 72(1)(c) of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015, does not alter the overall nature of the contract, and is limited to the period necessary to complete these activities. 
Legal Basis 
This modification is made in accordance with Regulation 72(1)(c) of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015, as: 
The need for modification has arisen from circumstances which a diligent contracting authority could not have foreseen, including evolving requirements and Ministerial decisions relating to the implementation of the Electronic Vehicle Excise Duty (eVED) service. 
The modification does not alter the overall nature of the contract. 
The extension is necessary to ensure continuity of service and facilitate the procurement, implementation, integration and transition of the replacement solution. 
The value of the 12month extension was £608,526; as required for reliance on Regulation 72(1)(c) PCR, this is less than 50% of the value of the original contract, this being £3,100,000. 
Extension Period 
Initial extension: 12 months (1 June 2027 to 31 May 2028) 
Optional additional extension: up to 6 months (1 June 2028 to 30 November 2028) 
Total potential extension: 18 months (1 June 2027 – 30 November 2028) 
Expected Outcome 
The extension will ensure uninterrupted Payment Gateway Services are maintained while the replacement contract is procured and the successor service is implemented, integrated, tested and transitioned into live operation. It will also provide sufficient time to accommodate ongoing business requirements arising from Ministerial decisions regarding eVED, and the future incorporation of Open Banking services, ensuring the replacement solution is appropriately designed, procured and implemented. 
The optional extension period of up to 6 months will provide additional contingency, if required, to support completion of procurement, implementation, integration and transition activities while maintaining continuity of critical payment services and minimising disruption to DVLA customers.

records.title: Millgate Shopping Centre Re-Development
records.description:
Mill Gate transformation is a catalyst
project that will reposition the shopping centre and its
surroundings as a more connected, attractive and commercially
resilient town-centre destination. Building on the aspirations of
the Mill Gate Regeneration Framework, the proposals focus on
opening up the existing mall environment, creating new public

development-ready plots for future phases of regeneration.

Rock and surrounding town-centre destinations whilst
supporting future mixed-use regeneration.

maintenance of pedestrian access and ongoing operation of
businesses, markets and servicing functions throughout the
construction period.

records.title: NHS Leasing Facilities Framework 2027
records.description:
University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust (the Trust) intends to establish a successor to the NHS Leasing Facilities Framework, for use by the Trust and other eligible public bodies. The Framework will be managed on the Trust's behalf by MUFG Corporate Markets Treasury Limited (MUFG CMTL).
The Framework will provide access to leasing and usage-based funding for equipment, including medical, testing and estates equipment, ICT, furniture, modular buildings, plant and machinery, green technology, and vehicles. It is expected to retain the two existing leasing lots and introduce a new Pay-Per-Use lot.
Eligible users are expected to include contracting authorities under the Procurement Act 2023 and the Public Contracts (Scotland) Regulations 2015, and registered providers of social housing and registered social landlords. This includes NHS bodies, central government, local authorities, emergency services and educational establishments across the UK.
The Trust is carrying out preliminary market engagement to test the proposed lot structure, the Pay-Per-Use model and the commercial approach before the tender is issued. Feedback will help shape the final framework structure and tender documents.
Lots (proposed)
1.Lot 1: Residual Based Lease Facilities

3.Lot 3: Pay-Per-Use Facilities

records.title: Level 2 Sexual Health Service  for Sexually Transmitted  Infection (STI) management
records.description:
Norfolk County Council Public Health has commissioned a community-based Level 2 Sexual Health Service within the South Norfolk/Breckland locality.
The proposed service will build upon existing Primary Care-based sexual health provision and expand the scope of delivery to include the assessment, testing and treatment of symptomatic but uncomplicated sexually transmitted infections (STIs). The service is intended to improve access to local sexual health services, particularly within rural and geographically dispersed communities, whilst supporting integration with existing Norfolk sexual health pathways and referral arrangements.
The service has been developed in response to identified local need and will focus specifically on the South Norfolk/Breckland population. 
The proposed contract term is four (4) years with an indicative annual contract value of approximately £103,500, representing an estimated total contract value of £414,000 over the full contract term. The contract will operate on an activity-based payment model and therefore the values in this notice are estimate.
This procurement has been undertaken under Direct Award Process B of the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023.  There are no specific Provider Selection Regime Find a Tender notices and therefore Norfolk County Council is adapting the Public Contract Regulations 2015 award notice.
The Authority notes that alternative sexual health provision already exists elsewhere within Norfolk and therefore this contract is specifically focused on addressing the needs of the South Norfolk/Breckland locality.

records.title: Torpoint Ferry Refit and Service Life Extension Programme 2028 – 2030
records.description:
Cornwall Council, on behalf of the Joint Authority owners and Tamar Crossings, is seeking to procure a three-year programme of planned refits and service life extension works for the three Torpoint Ferries, with one vessel undergoing refit annually between 2028 and 2030.
Each ferry will undergo a refit lasting approximately six weeks at a suitable shipyard, located within a maximum transit time of 24 hours from Torpoint, calculated at a speed of advance of four knots.
The works will include dry docking, statutory inspections and Maritime and Coastguard Agency and Lloyd’s Register recertification, structural, mechanical and electrical refurbishment, replacement of key components, and associated towing, testing and commissioning.
Essential service life extension works will also include replacement of ageing generators and vehicle loading ramps, together with the installation of a compliant sewage and wastewater system.

records.title: Market Warming Event - Devon Wide Oral Health Workforce Training Service
records.description:
Devon, Plymouth and Torbay Councils are working collaboratively to commission and procure a new Devon wide oral health training service. This is an exciting opportunity to have a Devon wide service delivering oral health training across the whole of Devon, supported by oral health leads from each Local Authority.
As part of our commissioning process, we are holding a second virtual market warming event to discuss the proposed new service with potential providers. We will use the feedback from the session to help shape and refine the Specification.
Please hold this date/time for the market warming event: Thursday 3rd December 2026 between 09.30 - 11:00am.
• The session will be held online via Teams and will be recorded.
• Devon, Plymouth, and Torbay Councils will present the new service and the aims of the service elements.
• Torbay Council’s procurement support will provide a short overview of the use of Pro-Contract.
• There will be a short, facilitated discussion around the elements of the new service.
• Time will be given for providers to ask questions.
Please note: Any interested providers who wish to attend the market warming event on the 3rd December 2026 should express their interest here , on ProContract, but also please email alex.jones@devon.gov.uk and lawrence.brown@torbay.gov.uk to express interest in attending the event. This will then secure attendees places and provide us with the details to email the Teams meeting invite.
Before the event on the 03rd December, we will share an agenda for the session and a document outlining the new service, so providers can have sight of this and come prepared with questions and feedback. A Teams meeting invitation link will also be sent to each interested provider who has emailed us confirming their interest in attending.
Any questions about the event should be submitted via ProContract’s Messaging facility. All questions submitted via ProContract’s Messaging facility will be answered and the questions and responses will be shared with all potential providers.
We look forward to seeing you all at the virtual market warming event (via Teams) on 03rd December 2026.
Please note that this event is not part of a competitive process. Publication or response does not commit Torbay County Council or respondents to a future procurement, nor provide any process exemptions or preferential treatment to any parties expressing an interest. The Authority will not be liable for costs incurred by any interested party in participating in this exercise

records.title: Overseas Facilities Management Category Strategy
records.description:
The National Armaments Director Group, Commercial and Industry, is developing an Overseas Facilities Management Category Strategy for the Permanent Joint Operating Bases and the Germany and Wider Europe estate.
This market engagement is to consider appropriate commercial solutions for all MOD assets and FM services overseas; the scope of any subsequent procurement(s) remains undecided.  The current established overseas prime FM contracts includes Permanent Joint Operating Bases (PJOB) in Cyprus, Gibraltar, the South Atlantic Islands, the Falkland Islands and Ascension Island, and Training Estate in Germany and Wider Europe.
Under the current established overseas prime FM contract arrangements, are delivered through a mixture of Total Facilities Management (TFM), Hard Facilities Management (HFM) and Soft Facilities Management (SFM) models. These arrangements support the operation, maintenance and compliance of the built estate and provide workplace and life-supporting services required by Defence personnel and organisations.
The Authority is at an early stage in developing its future requirements and commercial strategy. No decision has been taken on the future scope, packaging of services or geographic areas, contracting model or procurement approach.
This preliminary market engagement with Tier 1 Suppliers is intended to help the Authority understand the capability, capacity and appetite of the market and to obtain industry insight to inform the development of the Overseas Facilities Management Category Strategy and any potential future requirements.

records.title: Preliminary Market Engagement: Survey and Recording of Consent for Data Linkage
records.description:
Public Health Wales (PHW) is undertaking a study, commissioned by Welsh Government, to quantify the energy costs of people with long-term health conditions and disabilities across Wales, specifically those that result in unavoidably high energy use due to long-term health conditions, disability or care needs (hereafter long-term health conditions, LTCs). 
The study will have two stages:
•	Stage one, conducted in-house, will involve PHW mapping LTCs which require high energy use and the type of energy need (e.g. heating, cooling, powering equipment) based on existing evidence. It will also map the support available for such households. 
•	Stage two will involve procurement and draw on the LTCs identified in stage one. A data-linkage study will quantify energy costs and provide more granular data on households with high energy use related to LTCs. This may include, but is not limited to, the increased energy cost or (where not available) energy consumption in households with LTCs and associated with each LTC (compared to those without LTCs), the number of individuals with each LTC, and their geographical distribution in Wales.
To enable the delivery of stage two and specifically the quantification of increased energy cost or consumption in households with LTCs, PHW plan to procure an energy data consultancy to obtain household-level smart meter energy cost data or, where billing information is not available, energy consumption data.

records.title: Collections Store Refurbishments - Logistics Hub - Principal Contractor
records.description:
The Collection Store Refurbishment (CSR) Project forms part of both the wider NHM Unlocked Programme and NHM 150th Anniversary Campaign Programme, which supports: 
-The internal moves of 11 million specimens 
-The moves of 28 million specimens to our new facility at Thames Valley Science Park
-The 150th Anniversary Campaign to open previously closed galleries to the public
-The sale of our South London Collections facility
The NHM Unlocked Programme represents the largest ever move of natural history specimens worldwide. The wider CSR project has been tasked with refurbishing collections stores and rehousing five collections across five locations across the South Kensington Estate in suitable collections conditions.
The business case for the NHM Unlocked Programme is predicated on limited space and historic, ageing buildings; meaning that globally important specimens are being kept in conditions that hamper access and sometimes fail to meet minimum environmental standards. Moreover, the insights locked up in the collection remain largely untapped. From tackling climate change and meeting the mineral needs of a net zero world, to restoring biodiversity and achieving food security, the collection offers insights into the planetary emergency and how we might realise a brighter future where both people and planet thrive. The CSR Project supports this endeavour. 
Initially we will be tendering for works on the Osteology Store, this will convert a collections store in the basement of the Grade I Listed Waterhouse Building into a temporary “Logistics Hub” and future end state store for heavy and large specimens coming from our South London Store. 
As a separate tender there will be a further opportunity to express an interest in tendering for the Main Works package which covers refurbishment works to the other four areas around the South Kensington Estate, including subsequent areas of the Waterhouse Basement (two locations), Darwin Centre Phase 1 and in the Palaeontology Building. 
This tender relates to the initial works package located in the Osteology Store. The works comprise:
-refurbishment and alteration of Rooms B.03, B.07, B.07B-H, B.07J and BC05, 
-demolition of non-original partitions and raised floors, offices and removal of associated finishes and furnishings (excluding items retained on the eastern wall). 
-Internal works include the construction of a new security lobby with dry-lined partitions and a powered door, 
-repairs to damaged fabric and flooring, and measures to prevent pest ingress.
-Window and door works including repairs and redecoration to historic partitions and doors, installation of secondary glazing to three north-facing windows, adaptations for building services, and a new powered external door,
-Building services works include the removal and rebalancing of existing ventilation systems, strip-out of redundant electrical and data services, and the Stage 4 design and installation of new HVAC, electrical, fire alarm, security, BMS and controls systems. 
-All works will be undertaken in accordance with the fire strategy, maintaining the integrity of existing 120-minute compartment walls, and will include temporary protection of historic features, cleaning and making good on completion.
This phase of the project will initially prioritise the early conversion of the existing basement Osteology Store to a 'Logistics Hub', supporting the sequencing of moves and works in other areas and to reduce programme risk. It is critical that the Logistics Hub is made available early to enable the decant of the Old General Herbarium, the former Origins Gallery, the moves to Thames Valley Science Park (TVSP) and the sale of the South London Collections Facility. 
Following completion of the decant activities, the Logistics Hub will transition to its permanent configuration and use as a collections store accommodating the Heavy and Large Objects of the Mineralogy and Palaeontology Material Collection. Wherever possible, a 'light-touch' approach has been adopted to support the programme, minimise cost and impact to the significant historic fabric.

records.title: Procurement of Learning Management System (LMS)
records.description:
Yeovil Town Council is seeking to procure a secure, accessible and scalable cloud-based Learning Management System (LMS), including implementation, configuration, ongoing support, maintenance and account management, to support approximately 200 users comprising employees, elected members, temporary staff, volunteers and other authorised users.
The system must provide a centralised platform for delivering, assigning, managing and monitoring mandatory compliance training, employee and councillor development, role-specific learning and Council-specific training content. It must include a comprehensive course library covering subjects such as Health and Safety, Fire Safety, Data Protection and GDPR, Cyber Security, Equality, Diversity and Inclusion, Safeguarding, Information Governance and governance training for elected members.
The procurement includes the supply of the LMS as a Software as a Service (SaaS) solution, user licences, implementation and configuration, user setup and data migration support, administrator training, content management and authoring tools, reporting dashboards, automated notifications, policy acknowledgement functionality and integration with Microsoft 365, including Microsoft Entra ID Single Sign-On, Outlook and Microsoft Teams.
The supplier must also provide helpdesk and technical support, platform maintenance and upgrades, account management, annual service reviews, performance reporting and agreed Service Level Agreement commitments. The system must comply with UK GDPR, meet WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility requirements, provide a minimum of 99.9% monthly availability and maintain appropriate information security, backup and disaster recovery arrangements.
The initial contract term will be three years, with the option for two further extensions of 24 months each, giving a maximum potential contract duration of seven years. The contract is scheduled to commence on 1 February 2027, with implementation and configuration during February and March 2027 and a target go-live date of 1 April 2027.
Suppliers must provide a full breakdown of implementation costs, annual licensing, support, maintenance and content library costs, together with any optional charges for additional users, bespoke content, consultancy and integrations. All prices must be exclusive of VAT and remain fixed throughout the initial three-year contract term.

records.title: Complex Needs Hostel Provision
records.description:
The Commissioning Plan proposed a comprehensive phasing programme that will take a minimum of four years to complete. This Officer Decision Report isconcerned with Phase 3.1 of the plan relating to the award of 1 interim contract to the incumbent provider of housing related support services funded by theHousing Support Grant until the completion of the Phase 3 commissioning process is completed.
Both the Huggard Centre and Ty Tresillian are Emergency Bed Units which are Direct Access Hostels providing accommodation and support to people who arehomeless or potentially homeless and in need of support. The project aims to “provide accommodation to people every night of the year, giving individuals, whohave come from the streets, a sense of self-respect and a concept of future opportunity that can be nurtured through having their own room and structuredsupport planned to meet their individual needs”.
Service users will usually present with multiple secondary needs such as people suffering from drug dependency, people suffering from alcohol dependency,people with mental health problems, women fleeing domestic violence, ex-offenders and people with chronic illness.
Huggard Intervention Centre provides a ‘low threshold’ unique and highly accessible service 365 days a year for homeless people. It offers laundry and washing /bathing facilities, a free clothing store, a free meal every day and the opportunity to buy additional cost-price food. Service users can access health services andother specialist services via the Intervention centre, as well as advice and advocacy.
In addition, the Night Centre provides emergency shelter for up to 20 people per night through the provision of 17 dedicated private pod/rooms (small roomswith bed) and up to 3 additional bed spaces. All spaces have access to a safe locker to store personal valuable items.

records.title: MGN255B - Riverbank Stabilisation at Minehead, Somerset
records.description:
Project Title: Riverbank Stabilisation Works 
Location: 1-3 Buckhill, Withycombe, Minehead, Somerset, TA24 6QE 
Objective: To improve and stabilise the riverbank adjacent to properties 1-3 Buckhill. 
Magna Housing Ltd invites tenders from suitably qualified and experienced contractors to undertake riverbank stabilisation and associated improvement works at the above location. 
The works are required following a recent collapse of sections of the riverbank, which has resulted in obstruction to the river channel, localised flooding, and associated impacts on the surrounding area, including disruption to the adjacent highway. The objective of the project is to restore and stabilise the affected riverbank, ensure effective water flow, and mitigate the risk of further erosion or failure, thereby safeguarding nearby properties and infrastructure. 
These works have been identified to address existing erosion and stability issues affecting the riverbank, with the aim of preserving the integrity of the land and preventing further deterioration. 
Programme Requirements 
 Magna Housing Ltd requires that the works commence in Spring or Summer 2027, to be confirmed with contractor and CA to take advantage of favourable weather conditions and lower water levels typically experienced during this period. The intent is to ensure that the stabilisation works are completed in advance of the autumn and winter seasons, thereby reducing the risk of further collapse, flooding, and weather-related delays.
