records.title: Basingstoke Early Years Specialist Hub Provision
records.description:
Hampshire County Council is preparing to tender for a Basingstoke Early Years Specialist Hub Provision.
Hampshire County Council Children's Services via Services for Young Children Inclusion Team is seeking an Early Years service to be available in the district of Basingstoke and Deane. This service forms part of the Council's inclusive early years education offer and will include a defined number of reserved places for pre-school children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND). In addition, the service will provide outreach support to private, voluntary, and independent early years providers, as outlined in the service specification.
This provision plays a critical role in supporting early years children with complex developmental needs and is aligned with Hampshire's strategic priorities for inclusion and early intervention. The service specification outlines a targeted model of delivery through a specialist nursery hub, focusing on early identification, timely intervention, and multi-agency collaboration. The overarching aim is to reduce the need for statutory intervention by offering preventative support during a pivotal stage in a child's development.
The delivery model incorporates structured support from experienced practitioners, tailored learning environments, and coordinated input from health, education, and social care professionals. Operating within Hampshire's strategic framework, the service is expected to contribute to improved school readiness, reduced inequalities, and better outcomes for children with SEND and their families. The specification also includes defined performance measures, eligibility criteria, and expectations for partnership working to ensure the service remains impactful, accountable, and responsive to local needs.
It is anticipated that the new contract will have an annual value of £256,000 per annum. This is based on the planned number of places for the current academic year of 22 children accessing their 15-hour Early Years Education (EYE) funded entitlement, equivalent to 13.2 full-time equivalent (FTE) places. It is not anticipated that this requirement will change for the new contract.
The new contract will commence on 1st September 2027.

records.title: Best Start in Life Match Fund

awards.statusDetails:
This Procurement Termination Notice is published pursuant to Section 55 of the Procurement Act 2023. 
The Department for Education confirms that, following publication of the Tender Notice for the Best Start in Life Match Fund (Notice Identifier 2026/S 000-061537), it has decided not to award a contract under this procurement and to terminate the procurement process.   
The procurement is being discontinued as no tender submissions were received by the tender submission deadline.  The Department has therefore concluded that it is not possible to make a contract award through this procurement exercise. 
The Department remains committed to the objectives of the Best Start in Life Match Fund programme and has undertaken further market engagement to gather further information from suppliers and understand the evolving market dynamics. records.description:
The Borough Council of Calderdale ("the Council") is commissioning a Dementia Community Support, Advice, and Information Service, which will focus on the prevention of, and living well with, dementia. The Service is designed to provide community advice regarding prevention, and support, advice and information to Individuals with a diagnosis of dementia, their family and Carers, from diagnosis to end of life. It is anticipated that the Service contract will commence on the 1st April 2027 for a period of three (3) years (to 31st March 2030) with an option to extend for a period or periods of up to 24 months (up to 31st March 2032). This tender is for the procurement of a single award contract.

The contract will be a single award contract to the successful provider and an open procedure will be used for the tender. There is no opportunity to consider award in Lots as service delivery needs to be consistent and uniform across the whole borough of Calderdale.

records.title: NNLC703F - Fabrication, Machining, Associated Supplies and Services Open Framework
records.description:
The framework has the ability to award contracts through restricted quick quotes, open quick quotes, mini competition and direct award. Call-off contracts can be either fixed cost or cost reimbursable.
Mini-Competition
Where mini-competition is used, this is to be via the e-tender portal and must include all suppliers on the applicable lot. Each mini competition will be restricted to only one Lot. Should requirements at call-off not have been priced at point of framework creation, mini-competition should be held allowing all suppliers in the applicable Lot to price, accordingly, providing the additional requirement fits within the overall subject matter of the applicable Lot. Mini-competition criteria must not repeat qualification questions. The evaluation criteria must however comprise of the following, with weighting allowances adhered to:
Evaluation Criteria Range
• Pricing 5-90%
• Technical 5-90%
• Social Value 5-90%
Mini competitions can be ran using both the Open Procedure and the Competitive Flexible Procedure under the Procurement Act 2023, where the call-off is above threshold.
The Framework Agreement permits contracts to be awarded by direct award. UKNNL may award a contract directly to a Supplier where this is justified by the requirement for continuity of service, demonstrable value for money, and compliance with applicable procurement legislation.
A direct award can be made to a supplier for the continuation of existing services. This approach is considered appropriate where the supplier has established knowledge, experience, systems integration, and operational capability that are critical to the effective delivery of the services and where a change of supplier would result in disproportionate cost, disruption, delay, or operational risk.
Further justifications for Direct Award can be found below:
• It secures the uninterrupted continuation of critical services.
• The requirement consists of substantially similar or repeat services already being delivered by the current supplier.
• A change of supplier would require significant transition activity, resulting in additional cost, resource burden, loss of operational knowledge, and increased delivery risk.
• The supplier is already integrated within existing governance, processes, systems, and delivery arrangements.
• The proposed award represents value for money when considering both contract costs and the costs and risks associated with supplier transition.
• The award supports efficient service delivery and maximises public benefit.
UKNNL has assessed that awarding the contract to the current supplier represents the most advantageous commercial outcome and is consistent with the Framework terms and/ or the principles set out within Schedule 5 of the Procurement Act 2023 relating to circumstances where supplier continuity, technical knowledge, interoperability, or the procurement of similar services provide a lawful justification for direct award.
The Procurement Lead shall ensure that the rationale for direct award is fully documented and demonstrates that:
• The direct award is objectively justified.
• The decision delivers value for money and public benefit.
• The risks and costs associated with changing supplier have been considered.
• The award complies with the Framework Agreement, the Procurement Act 2023, and all applicable governance requirements.
• Appropriate transparency and approval requirements have been satisfied prior to contract award.
If there is a pre-existing relationship with any or other suppliers on the Framework which is in the public interest as it offers value for money or a saving in terms of resource and any other compelling commercially and/or value led reason that can be determined to make a Direct Award.
Additional Direct Award Options - Lot 5 Only
a) Direct award to the highest ranked supplier
Admission to the Framework is based on a 50% technical evaluation and 50% commercial evaluation, with Framework Suppliers ranked in descending order according to their combined score.
For a direct award under the ranking option, the Procurement Lead will approach the highest ranked Framework Supplier on Lot 5 and request a full quotation and indicative delivery programme for the requirement. Social value may be required for contracts delivered under Lot 5, where this is required, suppliers will be required to provide social value commitments within their proposal.
The Procurement Lead may not negotiate the scope of the requirement in a manner that would materially alter the nature of the direct award. Where the highest ranked Framework Supplier is unable to meet the requirement, is unable to deliver within the required timescale, or does not provide a commercially acceptable quotation, the Procurement Lead may progress to the next highest ranked Framework Supplier on Lot 5.
UKNNL is expected to award to the highest ranked Framework Supplier capable of meeting the requirement. However, where there is a demonstrable value-for-money benefit, a pre-existing project relationship, programme continuity requirement, or another compelling commercial justification, the Authority may award to an alternative Framework Supplier, as detailed in 3.4. In such circumstances, the Procurement Lead must ensure that the rationale for the award is appropriately documented and demonstrates the achievement of value for money and public benefit.
b) Direct award using the desktop calculator
This direct award mechanism enables the Procurement Lead to undertake a weighted evaluation of technical quality and pricing.
The desktop calculator will determine the Most Advantageous Tender by applying a new tender specific weighting to each of the Framework Suppliers' technical and commercial scores achieved during framework establishment. The supplier with the highest combined technical and commercial score post weighting will be invited to provide a proposal. The desktop calculator must be used to calculate the final ranking. The new revised costing will not be a factor of the evaluation used to determine the highest ranked supplier. The Procurement Lead may determine the relative weighting of Technical and Price, provided that the combined weighting totals 100% and remains within the permitted ranges set out below. Social value may be required for contracts delivered under Lot 5, where this is required, suppliers will be required to provide social value commitments within their proposal.
Following completion of the desktop evaluation, the requirement should be awarded to the highest ranked Framework Supplier. If that supplier is unable to meet the requirement, deliver within the required timescales, or satisfy any mandatory project requirements, the Procurement Lead may progress to the next highest ranked supplier until a suitable supplier is identified.
The business area shall advise on the appropriate balance between Technical and Price having regard to the nature, complexity, and risk associated with the requirement. The values applied must fall within the ranges shown below.
The weighting between Price and Technical will be dependent upon the specifics of each call-off but must be within the range set out below. Evaluation Criteria Range Pricing 5-95% Technical 5-95%.

records.description:
As part of Peterborough City Council's (PCC) Corporate Strategy (2025-2028), specifically the Children and Young People priority, PCC is looking to expand its Community Short Breaks (CSB) group services offer for children and young people with disabilities and/or complex needs.
The CSB offer is designed to provide group-based opportunities for children and young people to socialise and develop skills, whilst improving wellbeing for both them and their families. It also provides parents/carers respite to support them in their caring responsibilities. It is a set block of contracts, comprised of Small Groups and Large Groups — both of which have different eligibility criteria.  Please see appendix 1 for eligibility criteria.
The CSB Offer meets the needs of Peterborough children and young people with disabilities and/or complex needs, aged 7-19 years. This includes, but is not limited to, children and young people with:
Physical disabilities
Learning disabilities
Autism
Complex health needs including life-limiting conditions
Multiple health conditions
Cognitive and/or sensory impairments and sensitivities
Behaviour that challenges.
Due to demand and gap analysis, PCC is looking to expand Small and Large Groups capacity, as well as looking to add a new “Medium Group” service (name to be confirmed) that sits between Small and Large Groups. This new group will cater for children and young people who meet the following criteria:
Aged between 12-18
Open to Disability Social Care, on the Short Breaks and Early Intervention (SBEI) Pathway, rather than requiring a higher level of intervention
Has an assessed need for a group-based short break through the PCC Disability Social Care referral and panel process
Able to participate safely in a community-based group environment, without the need for extra staffing
The purpose of this PME is to gauge market interest in the delivery of Small, Medium and Large Groups provision. It is being conducted purely as a scoping exercise and there is no guarantee it will lead to a commissioning exercise. The information gathered will:
Provide an understanding of existing provision within the market.
Inform service design for any future services that may be commissioned.
Gauge the level of the market interest in the delivery of these services for children and young people (7-19) with disabilities and/or complex needs.

records.title: LCRCA Skills Bootcamps Framework
records.description:
Liverpool City Region Combined Authority (LCRCA) intends to establish an Open Framework for the delivery of Skills Bootcamps.
It is the intention to progress with an Open Framework which is anticipated to operate for a maximum of 8 years and will be periodically reopened to allow new suppliers to apply for appointment.
Skills Bootcamps are flexible, employer-led training programmes of up to 16 weeks that support adults aged 19 and over to develop sector-specific skills needed to progress in work, move into new employment, or retrain for a different career. The programme is designed to respond to skills shortages and workforce needs, helping employers access a pipeline of skilled talent while enabling residents to develop higher-level skills and access new opportunities.

records.title: I-4988: ECH - 6 Schemes (2027)
records.description: Oxfordshire County Council has statutory duties under the Care Act 2014 in relation to the assessment of adults' care and support needs and the provision or arrangement of care and support for eligible individuals. The Council also has a broader responsibility to promote the effective operation of the local care and support market, helping to ensure that sufficient, diverse and sustainable services are available to meet the needs of Oxfordshire residents, including those who fund their own care and support. Extra Care Housing (ECH) forms an important part of the Council's approach to supporting people to live independently within their own homes and communities. ECH combines self-contained accommodation with access to on-site care and support, providing an alternative to more traditional models of home care and residential care. Oxfordshire County Council invites tenders for CQC-regulated care and support across six Extra Care Housing schemes comprising 229 homes. The successful tenderer shall deliver person-centred planned care, including medication and daily living support, and a 24-hour on-site Core Service providing emergency responses, wellbeing checks and assistance with communal meals and activities. Provision includes care within four Interim Care Pathway Flats supporting hospital discharge, admission prevention and respite. Services shall promote independence, dignity and choice, respond flexibly to changing needs and involve collaboration with housing and health partners. The contract commences on 1 April 2027 for three years.

records.title: Future Hosting and Storage Services (FHAS)
records.description:
The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) intends to enter into a contract with IBM United Kingdom Limited for Future Hosting and Storage Services (FHAS). The award follows a Competitive Flexible Procedure under the Procurement Act 2023 (Tender Notice 2025/S 000-049845).
Defra Digital, Data, Technology and Security (DDTS), through Group Infrastructure and Operations, provides digital services to six Defra group organisations: Defra, the Environment Agency, the Animal and Plant Health Agency, the Marine Management Organisation, Natural England and the Rural Payments Agency. The FHAS contract brings six existing hosting, storage and related support contracts together into a single contract. It covers:
• Data Centre Facilities Management and Site Services, including primary and secondary data centres and distributed server (comms) rooms
• Infrastructure and Platform Services for on-premises and private cloud hosting and storage
• Cloud Engineering Services, including live service management and DevSecOps
• FinOps and GreenOps (cost and sustainability optimisation)
• General Services, including the Service Catalogue and Foundation Services
• Infrastructure transformation services, including support for data centre exit
• Optional Services, and project services commissioned through the contract's Projects mechanism
Application transformation and migration services are outside the scope of this contract.
The contract has an initial term of five years. The Authority has options to extend it by two further periods of up to 12 months each, giving a maximum term of seven years. Termination assistance provisions apply on exit.
The estimated Total Contract Value (TCV) is £156,036,387.43 (excluding VAT) over the maximum seven-year contract term (5+1+1).  This is comprised of £127m for Implementation, BAU Run services, and Project Expenditure, and £29m for a Termination Assistance Period of up to 30 months.

records.title: Homes England - Master Development Partner, Broad Marsh, Nottingham
records.description:
Broad Marsh ("the Site") comprises around 11 acres of brownfield land within Nottingham City Centre. The Site is around 0.2 miles north of Nottingham Train Station and 0.3 miles south of Nottingham Council House. It is formed of three parts:
•	Site 1 - the former College
•	Site 2 - the former NCP car park 
•	Site 3 - the former Broadmarsh shopping centre 
The Site is identified as a strategic allocation in both Nottingham City Council's adopted and emerging Development Plan. 
Homes England purchased the site in March 2025 and have since begun delivering a package of enabling works (to include demolition of the remaining structures, site surveys and concluding site due diligence) to prepare the site for development. 
Homes England is now seeking, through the Competition, to appoint a private sector Master Development Partner to regenerate Broad Marsh into a new mixed use city quarter, by creating and delivering a new ambitious and holistic master plan for the Site, through multi-phased development involving high-quality public realm and place-making to seamlessly integrate it into Nottingham city's existing fabric ("the Project").
The value of the opportunity is the envisaged gross development value of the Project. No differential between the inclusive of VAT and exclusive of VAT values are noted as the VAT treatment has not been determined.
The development works are likely to last for around 15 years (this may be phased). Any dates included in this notice are indicative and subject to revision as they will depend on the partner selected and the programme proposed.

records.title: VRU - Provision of Hospital Based Youth Work Services
records.description:
The Violence Reduction Unit (VRU) is seeking providers to deliver Hospital-Based Youth Work services across 10 London hospital sites from April 2027. Building on over a decade of City Hall investment, the service places specialist youth workers within Major Trauma Centres (MTCs) and Accident & Emergency (A&E) departments to support young people affected by violence, exploitation and safeguarding concerns.
The service will engage young people aged 11-25 who present at participating hospitals as victims, or suspected victims, of violence, exploitation, sexual violence or other safeguarding risks. Youth workers provide immediate emotional and practical support during a critical "reachable moment", helping young people recover from trauma, reduce future harm, and access ongoing support in their communities.
The commission is structured into four geographical Lots covering 10 hospital sites. Providers must demonstrate strong local knowledge, effective partnership working, and the ability to deliver high-quality, trauma-informed youth work within hospital and community settings. Partnership and consortium bids are encouraged.
The programme aims to reduce violence and exploitation, improve young people's safety and wellbeing, increase access to positive opportunities and support, reduce hospital re-attendance linked to violence, and reduce offending and reoffending.
The contract will run from January 2027 to March 2029, with service delivery commencing in April 2027 and an option to extend for a further 24 months to March 2031. The total potential contract value is up to £9.4m (excluding VAT), subject to funding and approvals.

DVLA’s position is that this procurement falls below the legislative threshold for a concession contract. Therefore, it is classified as a non-regulated procurement under the Procurement Act 2023, and the rules applicable to regulated concession contracts do not apply for this procurement. records.title: Nottingham City Council District Energy Network Investment Opportunity
records.description:
Nottingham City Council is seeking to appoint a provider to acquire and operate the Nottingham City District Energy Network.
As well as an asset transfer agreement, it is anticipated that the successful bidder will be awarded an Ongoing Services Agreement to continue supplying heat from the network to circa 5,000 domestic properties which are currently connected to the Network and in respect of which the Authority has certain responsibilities as landlord or as covenantor.  It is anticipated that this supply obligation will be for a term of 90 years, subject to further dialogue during the procurement.
The successful bidder will also be awarded a Heat Supply Agreement and an Electricity Supply Agreement for the supply of heat and electricity to the Authority for a term of 10 years, each extendable by up to 5 years, subject to further dialogue during the procurement.
The Authority will also enter into two Development Agreements with the provider which will place obligations on the provider in relation to the future development and expansion of the Network, including the identification, assessment and progression of opportunities arising from strategic customer connections and heat network zoning.
The estimated value of the public contracts comprises:
(i)	estimated value of the Heat Supply Agreement = £10,000,000;
(ii)	estimated value of the Electricity Supply Agreement = £9,000,000;
(iii)	estimated value of the Ongoing Services Agreement = £665,000,000; and
(iv)	estimated value of the Development Agreements = £600,000,000 in total
The Authority is not making any payment under items (iii) and (iv) and the estimated value of these is based on the estimated revenue the provider will derive from providing the services required under the Ongoing Services Agreement throughout its term, and on the estimated revenue the provider can expect to generate from the expanded network developed under the Development Agreements throughout their economic lifetime.
The overall value of the opportunity is estimated to be £1,441,050,000 (including VAT), which takes into account the estimated value of the public contracts set out above, plus the estimated revenue the provider can expect to generate from the existing network throughout its remaining economic lifetime.

records.title: Workforce Development Programme
records.description:
The Workforce Development Programme will provide high-quality, specialist and bespoke training and support to enable youth practitioners, at all stages of their careers, to strengthen their expertise in supporting young people affected by violence and to develop their leadership skills as they progress professionally. 
The programme will be delivered through three integrated packages, designed to meet the varying needs, capacities, and career stages of practitioners across London’s youth sector: 
Package 1 offers a broad series of training, development, and networking opportunities. This responds directly to the need for flexibility and accessibility, particularly for parttime, freelance or youth workers who cannot commit to intensive programmes. It also provides opportunities for those new to the sector. These will be a mix of online and in person sessions and activities. 
Package 2  retains the core strengths of Rise Up by offering an intensive, cohort-based development programme. This preserves the unique aspects that made Rise Up impactful including leadership development, mentoring, its cohort model, and wellbeing support while targeting practitioners ready to step into senior roles. Evidence shows that supporting development at this level leads to wider organisational benefits, as participants influence teams, culture, and practice beyond their own roles. 
Package 3  is the Youth Practitioners’ Advisory Board (YPAB), offering continued leadership development and strategic influence for those who have completed Rise Up or the new Package 2. This ensures ongoing progression and maintains a pipeline of practitioner leaders able to shape VRU priorities.

records.title: Children's Direct Payment Support Service
records.description:
Cumberland Council is procuring a Children's Direct Payment Support Service under the Procurement Act 2023 Light Touch Regime
The Authority is commissioning a  Service Provider to offer a Direct Payment Support Service on its behalf.
The Service Provider is required to deliver support to all eligible families in receipt of Direct Payments.
Families will have the choice over the support they wish to access, so not all families will necessarily access all categories of support at any given point, though their needs may change over time.
The Service Provider shall help families get the most out of their Direct Payment by providing information and guidance on how Direct Payments can be used and also explain the family's responsibilities in relation to receiving Direct Payments including putting in place, planning for and renewing indemnity insurance where a Personal Assistant is employed, undertaking and renewing a DBS for their Personal Assistant, clear accounting for income and expenditure of Direct Payments and their statutory payment duties where applicable.
The proposed start date of the contract is 01st April 2027.
The initial term of the contract is twelve months and there is one potential extension period available of up to twelve months. Use of extension periods is at the absolute discretion of the council.
The maximum total contract value is £263,867 excluding VAT.  This includes the initial term, extension periods if implemented and potential uplifts.  If the council implements an extension or uplift, this will be confirmed in writing to the successful supplier in advance.
If the services to be provided are exempt from VAT, then VAT cannot be charged by the successful supplier.
For further details and to access the tender documents use the council's online procurement portal, The Chest https://www.the-chest.org.uk
You must be registered on The Chest to be able to view the opportunity and submit a tender.  Registration is simple and free on the above link.
Evidence of your Find a Tender registration must be provided with your tender submission.
Ensure you read and understand the Invitation to Tender (ITT) before completing the tender documents.
The ITT includes details about what is being procured, instructions on how to bid (including deadlines) and a copy of the terms and conditions you'd be signing up to if you were successful.
Any clarification questions you want to ask the council must be sent via messaging on The Chest by the deadline stated in the ITT.
All bids must be submitted to the council electronically via The Chest by the deadline stated in the ITT.

records.title: Parking Services Contract 2027
records.description:
Milton Keynes City Council ("the Council") is seeking to appoint a single Service Provider to deliver an integrated parking enforcement and associated services contract across Milton Keynes. The Service Provider shall provide a lawful, efficient, customer-focused and technology-enabled parking service covering civil parking enforcement, parking operations, moving traffic enforcement support, permit administration, parking asset support, potential vehicle removals and related digital services across Milton Keynes City. 
The Councils Parking Service is responsible for the following: 
•	Enforcement activities (civil enforcement, ANPR operations, Moving Traffic enforcement, car park management) 
•	Back-office and legal processing (permits, appeals, PCNs lifecycle) 
•	Cashless Parking (Pay by phone) 
•	Pay on foot parking 
•	Infrastructure and maintenance 
•	Public safety and community service 
The service shall be delivered in accordance with all applicable legislation, statutory guidance, approved device requirements and relevant industry codes of practice, and shall support the Council's wider strategic objectives which include, social value, carbon net zero and sustainable economic growth.
The estimated total value of £35m included in this tender  notice is the estimated total gross spend under the contract for the full possible contract period of 10 years at the point of contract signature, taking into account up to date assumptions regarding volumes.
The estimated figure excludes VAT, any estimate of inflation and the implementation of future service changes.
The estimated value will be affected by changes in transaction volumes, particularly around the expected population growth of the City. Other changes in the parking regime, including changes to parking charges and technological advances in payment methods will also impact the contract value. These changes cannot currently be quantified.  
There is no fixed total cost for the contract, so the estimated total value should only be treated as an estimate and shall not constitute a guaranteed or cap on contract spend under the contract. The actual sum payable will be determined using actual volumes and the rates tendered in the pricing schedule.  
The contract is a 6 year contract with the option to extend for 2+2 years.

records.title: Supply, Installation and Commissioning of a Thermal Vacuum Cycling Chamber
records.description:
The School of Physics & Astronomy (Space Park Leicester) has secured funding to procure a Thermal Vacuum (TVAC) System to support environmental testing, qualification, and thermal vacuum cycling of components and equipment developed under the projects run by its Space Projects and Instrumentation group and via commercial agreements with third parties (managed by Space Park Leicester).
Thermal vacuum (TVAC) chambers require high-vacuum capability (typically ≤ 1×10−5 hPa), wide-range temperature cycling (often -190 °C to +150°C or higher), and precise thermal control (control surface stability in the range ±0.1 °C/min), usually achieved via liquid nitrogen, shrouds and heating platens. They include contaminant control (e.g. dry pumps), structural reliability to withstand atmospheric pressure, and feedthroughs for power and data to Equipment Under Test (EUT). The System is intended to be installed in an ISO 14644 Class 6 cleanroom at Space Park Leicester.

records.title: National Framework Agreement for the provision of Sexual Health Services
records.description:
The demand for accessible, high-quality and innovative sexual health services continues to evolve in response to changing population needs, advances in clinical practice, increasing digital delivery models and the ongoing focus on reducing health inequalities.
The Framework will provide Relevant Authorities with a fully compliant route for the provision of sexual health services, supporting the commissioning of integrated, digital, clinical, diagnostic, prevention, outreach and specialist support services. The Framework is designed to enable Contracting Authorities to secure services that improve public health outcomes, promote early intervention and prevention, support vulnerable populations, and ensure equitable access to care. 
The overall aim of the Framework is to provide a compliant route to market facilitating the procurement of various Sexual Health Services. 
The Framework has been established under The Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023 and The Health Services (Provider Selection Regime) (Wales) Regulations 2025 (and as amended) (together the PSR) for use by all Relevant Authorities (and any future successors to these organisations).
"Relevant Authority" is defined in section 12ZB(7) of the National Health Service Act 2006 and in section 10A(9) of the National Health Service (Wales) Act 2006. It means a combined authority, an integrated care board, a local authority in England, NHS England, an NHS foundation trust or an NHS trust established under section 25 of the National Health Service Act 2006, a county council or county borough council in Wales, a local health board established under section 11 of the National Health Service (Wales) Act 2006, a National Health Service trust established under section 18 of the National Health Service (Wales) Act 2006, or a special health authority established under section 22 of the National Health Service (Wales) Act 2006. 
For the avoidance of doubt, any successor bodies of any of the above entities shall be entitled to place Orders and shall be deemed Relevant Authorities for the purposes of this Framework.
The Framework will be re-opened to new applicants every two years, approximately 90 days before the anniversary of the Framework Commencement Date.

records.buyer: Cardiff and Vale University Health Board
records.title: Nurse Call Servicing
records.description:
Throughout Cardiff and Vale University Health Board, there are nurse call bells which allow patients to communicate with nurses. The systems typically have a single button near the patient's bedside, which they can push to call for assistance. When the button is pressed, nursing staff are alerted by a light and/or an audible sound at the nurse's station. The Health Board have a requirement for the servicing of these Nurse Call Stations. 
The contractor shall carry out an annual visit to each property within the estate portfolio and carry out a full service of the installed Nurse call systems as detailed within this specification. The Contractor shall be responsible for producing a detailed maintenance log for each serviced unit, detailing inspections, tests any repairs or replacements recommended.
The scope of works shall include: 
•	Visual inspection and service all hardware components for signs of wear, damage or corrosion (photographic evidence required for any damages).
•	Functional testing of nurse call buttons, communication channels, and alarm features.
•	Testing of backup power systems to ensure functionality during power outages.
•	Report on general condition of all ancillary components within medical service trunking including small power sockets, Medical Gas outlets, Bedhead Lamps, etc., including a description with quantity and type of outlets above outlets.

records.description:

TfL is taking this opportunity to engage with the market and explore how its Visitor Centres can evolve to meet the changing needs of customers, visitors and commercial partners.
Through this engagement, TfL wishes to understand emerging customer trends, innovative products and services, technology solutions, and commercial delivery models that could support the future Visitor Centre proposition beyond 2027.
London remains one of the world's leading visitor destinations and continues to play a central role in the UK's visitor economy. Visitor expectations are evolving, with customers increasingly seeking personalised recommendations, seamless digital experiences, greater flexibility and convenient access to attractions, entertainment and travel products.
TfL welcomes views from attractions, cultural and entertainment organisations, tour and experience providers, ticketing and technology suppliers, destination management organisations, aggregators, marketplaces and other organisations that can help shape the next generation of visitor experiences.
Through this early market engagement, TfL aims to better understand how future partnerships could create value for customers, partners and TfL alike, while supporting the development of a commercially sustainable and customer-focused Visitor Centre proposition.

records.title: Commercial Satellite-Derived Earth Observation Data for the UK Public Sector
records.description:
The Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) intends to procure commercial satellite-derived Earth Observation (EO) data and associated Earth Observation services for use across the UK public sector. The procurement will support improved access to commercial EO capabilities, reduce duplicated procurement activity, enable greater sharing and reuse of data across government, and support evidence-based decision making across a range of public sector activities. The procurement has been designed following extensive engagement with public sector users and suppliers and reflects the Authority’s objective of establishing a more coordinated approach to the acquisition and use of commercial EO data and services.
The contract will be for the supply and licensing of core commercial optical satellite-derived Earth Observation data for use across the UK public sector. The successful supplier will provide data, associated rights, metadata, quality assurance information and supporting services required to support delivery through an access model. 
The procurement will be conducted using a Competitive Flexible Procedure through the Government Commercial Agency Space Technology Solutions Dynamic Market (RM6370). The Authority intends to award one contract expected to be awarded for an initial period of three years with an option to extend for up to one additional year. The relevant parts of the dynamic market are:
220 Web Services and Application Programming Interface (API)
204 Data Processing Services
308 Other Earth-related Data
315 Other Geospatial-related Data
The procurement is expected to support public sector use cases including environmental monitoring, infrastructure management, climate resilience, emergency response, agricultural monitoring, rural payments, land management and wider policy development. It has been structured to support both established suppliers and specialist providers, including SMEs, consortia and supply chain arrangements where appropriate.
The information in the Tender documentation takes precedence over the information in this notice. 
Dynamic Market Participation
Participation in the procurement will be limited to suppliers admitted to the CCS Space Technology Solutions Dynamic Market (RM6370). records.title: Millgate Shopping Centre Re-Development
records.description:
Mill Gate transformation is a catalyst 
project that will reposition the shopping centre and its 
surroundings as a more connected, attractive and commercially 
resilient town-centre destination. Building on the aspirations of 
the Mill Gate Regeneration Framework, the proposals focus on 
opening up the existing mall environment, creating new public 
spaces, improving pedestrian connectivity and establishing 
development-ready plots for future phases of regeneration.
The works are centred around three key areas: The Square, 
Minden & Market Parade and Union Square. Collectively, they 
involve selective demolition, public realm reconstruction, 
alterations to existing buildings and canopies, refurbishment of 
retained frontages, servicing and highways modifications, 
landscaping, lighting, drainage and infrastructure works. The 
objective is not simply to improve the physical environment, but 
to reconnect Mill Gate with Bury Market, the Interchange, The 
Rock and surrounding town-centre destinations whilst 
supporting future mixed-use regeneration.
Contractors should anticipate a complex town-centre 
regeneration project delivered within a live trading environment, 
requiring careful phasing, stakeholder coordination, 
maintenance of pedestrian access and ongoing operation of 
businesses, markets and servicing functions throughout the 
construction period.

Introduction
Flintshire County Council is seeking expressions of interest from suitably qualified and experienced organisations capable of delivering a comprehensive radon monitoring and remediation programme across its housing stock.
The Council manages approximately 7,500 domestic properties across Flintshire and has identified the need to undertake a structured programme of radon monitoring and, where required, remediation works to manage potential risks associated with elevated radon levels.
The purpose of this Expression of Interest is to establish the level of market capability available and to determine whether suppliers can provide a fully managed end-to-end solution covering all aspects of the programme under a single contract.
This exercise is for information gathering and market engagement purposes only and does not form part of any formal procurement process.
Proposed Scope of Requirements
The Council is seeking information from organisations capable of delivering the following services:
•	Identification and prioritisation of properties within radon affected areas.
•	Resident engagement, communication and appointment management.
•	Supply, installation, collection and administration of radon monitoring equipment.
•	UKAS accredited laboratory analysis.
•	Interpretation of monitoring results.
•	Property-specific reporting and recommendations.
•	Design of appropriate radon remediation measures.
•	Installation and commissioning of radon remediation systems.
•	Post-remediation validation testing.
•	Programme management and contract administration.
•	Compliance reporting and management information.
•	Ongoing technical advice and support.
The Council's preferred delivery model is a single-provider solution capable of managing all aspects of the programme from initial property identification through to completion of any required remediation works and validation testing.
Programme Objectives
The Council is seeking a delivery model that:
•	Provides a single point of accountability.
•	Ensures a consistent resident experience.
•	Minimises delays between testing and remediation activities.
•	Delivers robust quality assurance throughout the programme.
•	Produces accurate and auditable compliance records.
•	Provides clear programme reporting and performance monitoring.
•	Reduces administrative and contractual complexity.
Supplier Information Request
Interested organisations are requested to provide the following information.
Organisational Details
•	Company name.
•	Primary contact details.
•	Number of years operating in the radon sector.
•	Relevant accreditations, certifications and memberships.
Technical Capability
Please confirm whether your organisation can provide the following services directly under a single contract arrangement:
Service	Yes / No
Radon risk assessment and programme development	
Supply and management of monitoring equipment	
UKAS accredited laboratory analysis	
Interpretation of results and technical recommendations	
Resident engagement and appointment management	
Design of remediation solutions	
Installation of remediation measures	
Post-remediation validation testing	
Programme management and reporting	
Provision of compliance data and records	
Relevant Experience
The Council would be seeking interest from organisations that have delivered comparable contracts for local authorities or housing providers, that being end-to-end radon monitoring and remediation programme
Market Feedback
The Council welcomes feedback on:
•	The proposed single-provider delivery model.
•	Any barriers to delivering the full service under one contract.
•	Alternative approaches the Council should consider.
•	Any risks or challenges that may affect delivery.

records.title: Overnight Short Break (Respite) Service, Floating Support and Outreach Support Services for Adults with Learning Disabilities and Autistic Adults
records.description:
The Royal Borough of Greenwich is undertaking preliminary market engagement to inform the future commissioning and procurement of services for adults with learning disabilities and autistic adults.
The Council wishes to engage with potential providers to help shape future service models, procurement arrangements and service delivery approaches.
The Council is considering the future procurement of:
Lot 1 – Kemsing Road Overnight Short Break (Respite) Service
Provision of a four-bedroom overnight short break (respite) service for adults with learning disabilities and autistic adults, including those with complex needs. The service provides planned and emergency respite accommodation and support, promoting independence and wellbeing whilst supporting carers and families to sustain their caring role. The Kemsing Road property is owned by the Council, which will remain the landlord.
Lot 2 – Community Support Services (Floating Support and Outreach)
Providing flexible support to help people maintain accommodation, develop independent living skills, access their communities and achieve greater independence through a combination of Floating Support and Outreach Support, including elements of Community Navigation and Concierge Support.
The Council may decide to procure the services as separate contracts, a single integrated contract, or through an alternative lot structure depending on the outcome of market engagement and subsequent commissioning decisions.
Market Engagement
The Council seeks feedback on:
•	The proposed lot structure and packaging of services.
•	Service delivery models, innovation and best practice.
•	Integration and interfaces between respite, floating support, outreach support and wider health and social care services.
•	Workforce availability, recruitment, retention and mobilisation considerations.
•	Current and anticipated cost pressures affecting service delivery, including workforce, property, inflationary, regulatory and operational costs, and how these may impact the affordability, sustainability and viability of future services.
•	Demand trends and emerging needs among adults with learning disabilities and autistic adults.
•	Opportunities to improve independence, wellbeing, choice, community inclusion and outcomes for people using services.
•	Approaches to delivering flexible, responsive and out-of-hours support.
•	Views on procurement, contract structure, contract length, mobilisation and implementation arrangements.
•	Suggestions regarding the most effective methods of ongoing market engagement and provider consultation throughout the development of the procurement process.

records.title: UK7 - Step Up to Social Work Cohort 10 Contractor
records.description:
The Department for Education (DfE) is responsible for children’s services including children’s social care in England. 
Children’s Social Care (CSC) reform is a major priority for the government and backed by £2.5bn investment in this SR period. Government aims to transform children’s services to deliver better outcomes for children and families, as set out in the CSC National Framework. Social Work Workforce is a key enabler of reform: ensuring we have a sufficient and capable workforce to enable better outcomes and contribute to cross-government priorities on tackling Child Sexual Abuse, Domestic Abuse and Violence Against Women and Girls.
To ensure we have sufficient social workers for vulnerable children and their families, the DfE funds the Step Up to Social Work (SUSW) programme. SUSW is a specialist, fast track 14-month programme in child and family social work. The programme is a mixture of academic learning and work placements. Local Authorities form Regional Partnerships with a Higher Education Institution to deliver the academic element of the programme.
The department is awarding a contract for marketing and attraction, recruitment and supporting the application process, working with Regional Partnerships to ensure all 700 funded places are filled. 
The remit of the contractor is to:
a.	Design, manage and host a web portal enabling potential candidates to register an interest, access programme information and submit applications.
b.	Work with the DfE and Regional Partnerships (RPs) to develop web content.
c.	Programme marketing with a focus on attracting candidates from diverse backgrounds and targeting male applicants.
d.	Provide a candidate helpline.
e.	Conduct eligibility check on qualifications, non-UK equivalency qualifications and eligibility to live and work in the UK.
f.	Develop an applicant tracking system.
g.	Host a timed ‘written exercise’ on the recruitment platform.
h.	Host a booking process for applicants to select a date/time for attendance at an assessment centre.
f.	Provide personnel to support RPs during assessment centres.
g.	Keep candidates engaged throughout the process.
h.	Develop and manage a National Reserve List.
i.	Manage candidate information and data analytics.
j.	Produce an End of Year report detailing RP and candidate satisfaction data and recommend areas of the recruitment process that could be improved.

The framework will be available for use by NHS Trusts, other NHS entities, government departments, agencies and other statutory bodies, including local authorities, and private sector entities active in the UK healthcare sector, in accordance with the procurement documents.
The anticipated value of the Framework Agreement for the initial twenty-four (24) month term is approximately £46,230,000 excluding VAT. The Authority may extend the Framework Agreement by up to two further periods of twelve (12) months each. These values are estimates based on historical usage and forecast demand and do not constitute a guarantee of expenditure or business under the Framework Agreement.

records.title: CP2608-24 Highways Term Maintenance Contract
records.description:
Devon County Council (DCC) is undertaking a programme of Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) ahead of an upcoming procurement for a new NEC4 Term Service Contract for highway maintenance services.  Contract award is anticipated in 2028, with a contracted start of services on  1st April 2029.   
The current arrangement expires on 31 March 2029, and the Authority intends to put in place a future-focused, value-driven contract that supports safe, resilient and sustainable highway operations across Devon, both now and for the long term. 
This early engagement builds on feedback from previous market engagement, which is actively informing our emerging Contract Strategy. The purpose of this PME is to better understand market capacity, current innovations, risks and opportunities, and to help shape a procurement and contract structure that is fair, competitive and genuinely attractive to the market. 
Background  
DCC manages the largest highway network of any local authority in England, supporting residents, businesses and visitors across a uniquely varied geography. The network spans two national parks, two coastlines, remote rural communities and growing urban centres, presenting both opportunity and challenge for the delivery of highway maintenance services. 
The performance of the next contract will play a critical role in maintaining the safety, reliability and resilience of this network, while also helping the Council respond to wider pressures such as climate change, evolving customer expectations, workforce sustainability and the need to deliver long-term value for money. 
DCC is therefore seeking a delivery partner that can work with us in a collaborative, transparent and innovative way, recognising that strong outcomes will be achieved through long-term partnership rather than transactional contracting. 
The Authority is therefore seeking a solution that: 
-supports safe, reliable, and responsive services for residents, businesses and the travelling public 
-strengthens value for money and long-term affordability 
-unlocks efficiencies and delivers “more for less” through smarter ways of working 
-maximises performance through collaborative behaviours and shared ownership of outcomes 
-enables innovation and continuous improvement across the supply chain 
-contributes to DCC’s broader economic, environmental and social priorities, including carbon reduction and social value 
The indicative annual contract value is in the region on £65 million.  DCC is looking to establish a long-term relationship however the duration of the contract is yet to be determined.  
Vision 
DCC is committed to delivering high-quality, cost‑effective and resilient highway maintenance services. Through this procurement, we aim to: 
-appoint a Tier 1 delivery partner to establish a long-term, collaborative “win‑win” partnership aligned with ISO 44001 principles. 
-deliver economic, environmental and wider social benefits for communities across Devon. 
-create the conditions for continuous improvement, innovation, and modernisation throughout the life of the contract. 
-support consistency, efficiency and resilience and access for Tier 2 supply providers. 
We look forward to engaging with the market as we shape this important contract.  Your insight and experience will help inform a procurement and contractual model that is deliverable, collaborative, innovative and aligned with the long-term needs of Devon’s residents, communities and businesses. 
Thank you for your interest in working with Devon County Council.

records.title: Tender for the PE and School Sport Partnership Network
records.description:
The Department for Education has awarded a contract for the establishment and operation of a national PE and School Sport Partnerships Network. The Network will support schools to improve the quality, accessibility and impact of PE, school sport and physical activity, with a particular focus on increasing participation, reducing inequalities and improving outcomes for children and young people.
The National Delivery Partner will establish, manage and assure a network of national, regional and local delivery partners. It will provide schools with universal support, targeted support based on identified need, and access to additional school-requested services. The services include school engagement and needs assessment; coordination of local and regional provision; workforce development and continuing professional development; support for inclusive PE and school sport; swimming and water-safety support; management of grants and other funding where required; quality assurance, safeguarding and performance management; and the collection, analysis and reporting of delivery and outcomes data.
The National Delivery Partner will also provide and operate a Digital Platform through which schools and delivery partners can access services, manage referrals and delivery activity, maintain relevant records, and report performance and outcomes. The contract includes mobilisation and transition from existing delivery arrangements, supply-chain management, stakeholder engagement, continuous improvement, evaluation and support for the Department’s wider policy objectives for PE, school sport and physical activity.

records.title: 2115 Oracle Licensing Support Service for NHS Arden Greater East Midlands CSU
records.description:
NHS Arden & GEM Commissioning Support Unit (AGEM CSU), acting on behalf of NHS England, requires Oracle Database Enterprise Edition Licensing and Oracle Premier Support Services for the NHS Calculating Quality & Reporting Service (CQRS) for a 40-month contract term commencing on 1 December 2026 and expiring on 31 March 2030.
The contract shall provide Oracle software licence entitlements, access to Oracle Premier Support, Oracle Critical Patch Updates, software maintenance, product updates and technical support services required to maintain the security, supportability and operational resilience of the CQRS platform.
CQRS is a mandated NHS approvals, reporting and payments calculation system for GP practices. It helps practices to track, monitor and declare achievement for the Quality and Outcomes Framework (QOF), Direct Enhanced Services (DES) and Vaccination and Immunisation (V&I) programmes.  CQRS collects information from GP practices either:
- automatically from the practice clinical records system through the General Practice Extraction Service (GPES) or 
- manually directly into the Calculating Quality Reporting Service
This information is used to help practices track and manage their performance against various targets and enhanced services frameworks set for them by NHS England.  
AGEM CSU requires Oracle Database Enterprise Edition Licensing, Oracle Premier Support and associated Oracle Managed Services for the NHS Calculating Quality & Reporting Service (CQRS)
The supplier shall provide:
• Oracle Database licensing.
• Oracle option and management pack licensing.
• Oracle Software Update Licence and Support.
• Managed database services.
• Licence management and compliance support.
• Technical support and escalation services.
• Support for all in-scope environments.
This is a direct award under the Procurement Act 2023 and nor procurement process has been  undertaken.

records.title: Isle of Wight Sensory Loss Support Service
records.description:
The Authority invites response to this Invitation to Tender (ITT) from suitably qualified suppliers ("Suppliers") for the provision of Isle of Wight Sensory Loss Support Service. 
The Isle of Wight Council ("The Authority") are seeking to deliver a Sensory Loss Support Service that will provide specialist assessments of need, rehabilitation and targeted support, information, and advice for people with sight, hearing, and dual sensory impairments on the Isle of Wight.  By delivering services which support the full range of sensory impairments the service will seek to reduce duplication and create a simple pathway for people living with multiple sensory impairments enabling them to access support which meets their needs.  The service will deliver the Authority's duties as described in the Care Act 2014, Care and Support (Assessment) Regulations 2014, and Deafblind Guidance 2014.
The aim of the service is to promote and support independence by providing access to a wide variety of high-quality resources and support options as well information and advice.  The service will also support individuals to remain connected with their friends, family and communities to ensure that people with sensory loss can live full and active lives.
The allocated annual budget for the service is up to a maximum of £180,000 (exc. VAT) per year, which is inclusive of the fixed £20,000 (exc. VAT) equipment budget.  The total annual budget available is split into two parts; costs associated to operate and deliver the sensory service (service delivery) and the provision of sensory equipment (equipment). 
The contract period is an initial term of 3 years from 1 April 2027 to 31 March 2030.  The Authority may extend this agreement beyond the Initial Term by a further period or periods of up to two years. The adoption of extensions is through sole discretion of the Authority. 
For full details of the specification requirements can be found in the Service Specification.

records.title: Multiple Disadvantage and Housing Support Alliance
records.description: The Multiple Disadvantage and Housing Support Service, will work in a streamlined and holistic manner across the area of Sheffield. It will provide holistic and multi-faceted floating support to people who experience multiple disadvantage – officially defined as a co-morbidity of homelessness/housing insecurity, mental health needs, substance use, involvement with the criminal justice system and domestic abuse – often further compounded by additional factors such as trauma, poverty, discrimination and stigma. The integrated service will aim to prevent and tackle multiple disadvantage, whilst recognising the intersectionality and compounding impact of the areas of need outlined above. The service will build on local learning from the Changing Futures programme and aligns with the city’s strategy Coordination from Complexity (2025–2030), consultation findings, and the Alliance Commissioning Vision. It will provide a clear, equitable and trauma-informed offer across three pathways: (1) Young People aged 16–25 (2) Adults aged 25+ (3) Recovery and Co-production (all ages). This contract is being awarded as an alliance contract, which means the Council expects tender responses to be submitted on behalf of groups of suppliers that are able collectively to deliver the Services.

records.title: Contract for the provision of Maintenance and Servicing of Ventilation and Air Conditioning Installations
records.description:
East Lindsey District Council invites suitably qualified and experienced suppliers to submit tenders for the Maintenance of Ventilation and Air Conditioning Installations across the Council's commercial estate.
In line with the principles of the Procurement Act 2023, this procurement aims to support open and fair competition while ensuring high quality service delivery and long term value. We welcome bids from organisations committed to robust performance standards, sustainability, effective collaboration, and continuous improvement.
The successful contractor will be appointed under a 3 year Measured Term Contract with the option to extend by a further 2 years (1+1) subject to performance targets.  The Contract will consist of the following provisions:
•	routine inspection, testing and servicing;
•	cyclical and planned preventative maintenance;
•	reactive repairs and call outs during normal and out of hours periods; and
•	additional replacement and new installation works where required.
The contract covers all relevant air conditioning, ventilation, and associated systems installed within Council owned commercial premises across the East Lindsey district, as detailed in the asset schedules. All works must adhere to the Specification, Schedule of Rates, and applicable statutory and industry standards.
We are seeking a contractor with strong technical capability and a proven track record in delivering reliable, responsive and customer focused maintenance services. Bidders should clearly demonstrate their methodologies, including any innovative practices, supply chain resilience, environmental considerations, and approaches that enhance system performance, longevity and overall value.
Service delivery commenced prior to execution of the agreement. The contract formalises the ongoing contractual arrangements between the parties. Due to system limitations, the contract commencement date recorded within the publication system cannot precede the date of contract execution.

records.title: High Voltage Maintenance Services
records.description:
The Supplier shall provide to the University routine servicing on each piece of High Voltage (HV) equipment in accordance with the latest version of the British Standards BS6626:2010, IEE Electrical Maintenance document and the Manufacturer's Maintenance Schedule.
The Supplier shall provide the following services:
• Carry out inspection, testing and remedial repairs necessary as a result of both the planned maintenance servicing and break downs.
• Call outs of all equipment forming part of the HV equipment to maintain a fully functional system at all times on an all-inclusive basis on all campuses (i.e. at no extra cost to the University), except for vandalism, accidental damage or misuse. 
• Emergency call-out facility and training to University appointed personnel to assist with diagnosis of power failures prior to the emergency call-out procedure being instigated.
• Training for University appointed personnel.
• SAP (Senior Authorised Person) attendances to cover instances where the University intends to renovate or expand its existing Estates and this would have an impact in the existing HV Infrastructure.

renewal.description: Initial term of 3 years with provision to extend for any periods up to and including 36 months.

options.description:
The University reserves the right to change the indicative dates provided in the procurement documentation, and also for the removal and addition of any HV assets from/to the scope of this contract subject to further details being provided by NIE.  The University also reserves the right to increase or decrease the frequency of asset overhauls.  Such future changes to HV assets and overhaul frequency may change the actual contract price, which may be higher or lower that the prices stated in the Supplier's Commercial Submission.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
In the event that the Contract is terminated prior to expiry of the proposed initial three (3) year contract period, the University reserves the right (but shall not be obliged) in that instance to offer the second ranked most advantageous Supplier from this Competition (second ranked Supplier), the opportunity to enter into a replacement contract with the University on the basis of the same contract terms, rather than undertaking a reprocurement exercise at that point. Any replacement contract entered into will be for the remaining unexpired initial contract period, with the same ability for the University to extend by a further period or periods of up to 36 months.
Entry into any replacement contract with the second ranked Supplier shall be subject to that second ranked Supplier's offer (including its tender pricing) remaining unchanged from that originally proposed at the tender return deadline. In the event that either: (a) the second ranked Supplier is unable or unwilling to stand over its original tender offer to the University; or (b) the second ranked Supplier is unable or unwilling to enter into a replacement contract with the University on the basis of the same contract terms; or (c) the second ranked Supplier declines the opportunity to enter into a replacement contract with the University for any reason, then the University reserves the right to approach the next highest ranking most advantageous Supplier from this Competition in turn on the same basis. This process may, at the University's discretion, continue until all ranked Suppliers have been exhausted or the University decides, at its sole discretion, to undertake a re-procurement exercise.
STANDSTILL PERIOD
8 working days - end 30 November 2026.

records.title: Provision of Catering Services for Serpentine Bar & Kitchen and St James’s Café
records.description:
TRP is currently preparing to initiate a procurement process for the Provision of Catering Services for Serpentine Bar & Kitchen and St James’s Café. Prior to commencing the procurement, TRP wishes to engage with the market to understand the level of Supplier interest and gather information to support the development of TRP’s requirements.
As part of this PME exercise, TRP is inviting interested suppliers to complete the Market Consultation Questionnaire, Which can be downloaded in Delta (https://www.delta-esourcing.com). 
A separate PME presentation has also been issued as part of this PME exercise. The presentation provides further background on Serpentine Bar & Kitchen and St James’s Café and an overview of the proposed scope of the procurement. Suppliers should review the PME presentation when preparing their response.
It is anticipated that a seven (7) plus Five (5) year contract will be offered on a fully commercial concession basis whereby the appointed caterer shall pay a concession fee on Net Sales supported by a Minimum Annual Guaranteed Sum. Capital investment will be required from the successful bidder for refurbishments.
TRP are looking to work with a Concessionaire with relevant knowledge, experience, financial capacity and competency in managing a similar Catering Service, with a consistent track record in service delivery. Additionally, the Concessionaire would be expected to create a marketing programme which includes sales activity over the period of the contract.

records.buyer: Neath Port Talbot County Borough Council
records.title: Margam Green Roof Shelter
records.description:
1. INTRODUCTION 
Neath Port Talbot County Borough Council has made an award to appoint the services of a contractor, to deliver a green roof shelter structure as part of its ‘Local Places for Nature’ funded projects. The project is looking at new ways of turning ‘grey to green’ by using nature as a way to combat the effect of climate change; help us deal more effectively with issues relating to noise and air pollution, and nature emergency. The project will use the best practices obtained through similar projects throughout the county borough.
2. BACKGROUND INFORMATION
The existing shelter located at Margam Country Park is need of replacement, and will be replaced with a new green roof shelter to enhance the biodiversity in this hand feeding area for livestock. The project will be managed by Neath Port Talbot County Borough Council, led by the Countryside and Wildlife Team Biodiversity Officers.
The existing structure is approximately 8m Long by 4.5m Wide, and 2.5M tall. It is Enclosed on three sides, has multiple signage posters and 3 wash basins on the inside. The back wall is used as a fence for an existing paddock for livestock. 
2.1 LOCATION 
The project is located at the hand feeding station with Margam Country Park, Port Talbot SA13 2TJ.
2.2 PROJECT TIMESCALE 
The Council are looking for a suitable contractor to complete the works within an anticipated timescale of completion now scheduled no later than Mar 2027. Works are to start Nov 2026 for design and then construction and planting.
3. CONTRACT REQUIREMENTS
This entails the construction of a metal or timber shelter able to support a wildflower (Biodiverse) green roof, including the necessary ground preparation works and concrete pad. The structure must adhere to all building standards and utilise the specifications within the GRO code. (GRO-Code-2021-Anniversary-Edition.pdf). The project shall include the removal, relocation and reinstallation of the existing handwashing facilities. All works shall be carried out in accordance with the Construction (Design and Management) Regulations 2015, all relevant British Standards, fire safety requirements including BS EN 13501-1, and applicable health and safety legislation. Accessible handwashing facilities shall be provided in accordance with Part M of the Building Regulations (Wales) and Approved Document M. At least one wash-hand basin shall have a maximum rim height of 850 mm, provide clear knee space beneath, be fitted with easy-use taps, and have sufficient clear floor space to enable use by wheelchair users. The contractor shall ensure that access to the handwashing facilities complies with the requirements of the Equality Act 2010 and relevant accessibility standards. Where necessary to provide an accessible route and meet duties relating to reasonable
adjustments, the contractor shall design, supply and install a suitable access ramp, including any required handrails, landings and associated works, to ensure safe and inclusive access for wheelchair users and persons with limited mobility.
All accessibility provisions shall meet the duties for reasonable adjustment under the Equality Act 2010.
The project aims to expand on existing good practice within the county, supports local flora and fauna; contributes positively to the removal of air pollution; and improves the overall look and feel around the feeding station area of Margam Country Park. 
The contractor will be required to complete the works following the elements described below:
1. The constructor will remove the existing shelter, the existing washing facilities are to be repurposed where possible. [RR1.1]
2. A flat concrete pad will need to be installed as a base for the green roof structure.
3. Removal of a livestock fence is also required as this backs onto the structure, and will need to be replaced. ( Approximately 8m livestock fencing. This is to be confirmed with the Margam Park Team)
4. Working closely with the Biodiversity team and using the GRO code, the contractor will construct and install a green roof shelter, enclosed on the back and one side. Plant selection is required to be pre-agreed with Biodiversity teams. Including habitat sites such as wood mounds/rockeries, areas for water.
5. Working closely with the council, the contractor will be required to comply with any relevant CDM Regulations and consider the required need for future inspection and maintenance of the structure.
6. The contractor will be required to ensure that the shelter is watertight and able to support the saturated weight of a green roof.
7. To ensure the success and longevity of this project, the contractor will need to include a maintenance programme (inclusive of plant replacement and watering) for the first 12 months following installation.
8. Design and installation of new bilingual signage within the structure (How to wash hands, Safety for pregnant women around sheep, handwashing after handling animals sign).

records.description:

Plumbing and Hot Water Systems

Shower Facilities

•	Supply and install individual showers within separate shower cubicles.

•	Ensure adequate ventilation is maintained or upgraded as required.
Toilet Refurbishment
•	Remove all existing sanitaryware and associated fittings.
•	Supply and install new WC suites, wash hand basins, taps and accessories.
•	Layout shall follow the design and arrangement shown on the drawings supplied by the Council.
•	Include necessary alterations to drainage, water supply and waste connections.

Entrance Area Alterations

•	Undertake any necessary structural works identified during the contractor's investigations.

 Flooring Works

•	Prepare subfloors as required.
•	Supply and install new slip-resistant commercial-grade flooring suitable for wet environments.

Wall Coverings

Contractor Requirements

records.title: Highway Structures - Confined space, roped access & difficult access inspections 2026
records.description:
The North and Mid Wales Trunk Road Agent (NMWTRA) intends to procure services to undertake Principal Inspections of highway structures located throughout North and Mid Wales.
NMWTRA is seeking expressions of interest from organisations with proven experience in undertaking Principal Inspections in accordance with the Design Manual for Roads and Bridges (DMRB), including compliance with CS 450 and Welsh Government Structures Maintenance Manual. Tenderers will be required to provide inspection personnel holding current Bridge Inspector Certification Scheme (BICS) accreditation appropriate to the structures being inspected. Certain structures may require personnel holding Senior Bridge Inspector accreditation together with specialist access competencies relevant to the inspection activity.
The successful Contractor will be expected to provide all resources necessary to safely undertake the inspections, including specialist access equipment, qualified personnel, inspection planning, welfare facilities, and inspection reporting.
The contract is intended to establish a long-term relationship with a competent supplier capable of delivering a consistent programme of specialist-access Principal Inspections across the North and Mid Wales trunk road network throughout the four-year contract period.
The four-year contract period is anticipated to include approximately 60 Principal Inspections per annum. The structures portfolio comprises a diverse range of assets including highway bridges, retaining walls, culverts and other highway-related structures. Inspection locations will be distributed across the North and Mid Wales trunk road network.
A significant feature of this contract is that the inspection programme will comprise predominantly specialist-access inspections. Suppliers should anticipate the requirement to undertake inspections involving confined spaces, rope access techniques, work at height, work in or over water and other structures where specialist access methods are necessary to achieve the inspection requirements.
Please note that the value stated in this notice is an estimate based on a four-year period and is subject to funding availability and other relevant factors.

records.title: Interim and Temporary Accommodation Light Touch Framework
records.description:
Havant Borough Council seeks to establish a light touch framework agreement for the provision of good-quality, nightly-paid interim and temporary accommodation (Referred to as temporary accommodation).
The Council secures temporary accommodation to discharge its duties under Part 7 of the Housing Act 1996 (as amended by the Homelessness Reduction Act 2017). These duties include preventing and relieving homelessness, as well as securing interim and emergency accommodation for eligible households where a statutory duty arises. To help fulfil this duty the Council sources temporary accommodation via third party suppliers.
The estimated value for this framework including all possible extensions is £24,000,000 Excluding VAT. This is based on an estimated annual spend of £3,000,000 per year Excluding VAT from previous spend data. This is not a guaranteed spend.
At this stage we are conducting preliminary market engagement to gather feedback from temporary accommodation suppliers which will help to inform the finalised specification and approach to the framework.
The Council would like to receive feedback from suppliers who offer accommodation across  a range of sizes, from single rooms with shared facilities, to self-contained accommodation ranging from one to five-beds. It is not a requirement for a supplier to provide accommodation in each size. Ordinarily accommodation within the Borough of Havant or as close as reasonably practicable is preferred, however, there is no fixed geographical boundary for this preliminary market engagement and suppliers are encouraged to identify all locations and accommodation types that they may be able to make available to the Council.
