records.title: SmokeFree App
records.description:
Suffolk County Council is looking to award a contract for the delivery of the SmokeFree App. The requirement includes app licences; unlimited 24/7 access to NCSCT-trained tobacco dependency advisers; behavioural and peer support; access to agreed stop smoking aids, including NRT and vape products; service monitoring; and quarterly outcome reporting.
The service complements Suffolk's existing stop smoking provision by providing a flexible route that can be accessed without a fixed appointment. It is particularly suitable for people who may not engage with traditional provision, including shift workers, carers, pregnant women, people with mental health needs and users who value anonymous or out-of-hours support.
The proposed contract term is one year with an option to extend for up to a further year. This is intended to maintain continuity while a regional or compliant framework route is developed and assessed.
The estimated value shown here is £304,800 inclusive of VAT. For the purposes of this estimate, VAT has been included at 20% (Standard Rate), however in some circumstances VAT may be exempt or chargeable at a different rate.
Direct award justification
Single supplier - technical reasons
The Smoke Free Digital Service provides a comprehensive, flexible stop smoking service that people can attend at a time that suits them, day or night, without the need for a fixed appointment. This has been shown to be beneficial for various target groups with busy lives, such as shift workers, carers, and pregnant women, who often find attending appointments a struggle. Other users, including those with mental health issues, can find the anonymity beneficial. Such users often prefer to take control of how and when they access services.
The Smoke Free app benefits from a comprehensive range of support, including unlimited 24/7 access to NCSCT (National Centre for Smoking Cessation and Training) trained Tobacco Dependency Advisors (TDAs), swift delivery of stop smoking aids, a community group offering peer support, plus many other behavioural tools on the app. Smoke Free Digital support aligns with the NCSCT Standard Treatment Programme and adheres to NICE guidance for behavioural support and pharmacotherapy procedures.
Smoke Free app is the only app that offers live advisor support 24/7. The London Tobacco Alliance recently verified that the Smoke Free app is the only app in the UK and worldwide offering this level of support. There is clear evidence that combining stop smoking aids with expert support from local stop smoking services makes someone 3 times more likely to stop smoking successfully. Our research has concluded that there are no other suitable providers in this field, therefore, the Council intends to award a contract directly to Smoke Free for this service.

records.title: Ortec Finance Limited
records.description:
Local Pensions Partnership Investments Ltd (LPPI) and Ortec Finance wish to enter into a contract for the provision of GLASS, a software tool that enables LPPI to model and analyse assets and liabilities using deterministic and stochastic projections.  
LPPI intends to award a contract to the existing supplier without conducting a competitive tendering procedure in reliance on the exemption under section 41 of the Procurement Act 2023 ("the Act") (direct award in special cases) by application of the below direct award ground.
Additional or repeat services - under paragraph 7, Schedule 5 of the Act
The contract concerns the supply of services by the existing supplier which are intended as an extension to, or partial replacement of, existing services provided by the existing supplier in circumstances where:
(a)	a change in supplier would result in the contracting authority receiving services that are different from, or incompatible with, the existing services; and
(b)	the difference in incompatibility would result in disproportionate technical difficulties in operation and maintenance.
LPPI currently uses GLASS to support its provision of strategic asset allocation advice, quarterly risk reporting and asset liability modelling analytics. The tool is a key part of a number of the services that LPPI provides. LPPI's reporting, strategic asset allocation investment advice and analytics services, and the internal processes that support them, are configured around this specific tool and rely on its use and outputs. An alternative tool from a different supplier would not provide the same form of outputs and would be different from and incompatible with LPPI's existing services and processes. Those services and processes would have to be adapted to work with any alternative tool.
Introducing a different tool would require significant re-mapping and adaptation of those systems and processes, which would involve substantial additional cost and resource, while creating operational risk to its reporting, investment advice and analytics services. LPPI therefore considers that the incompatibility with a replacement tool would give rise to disproportionate technical difficulties in operation and maintenance.

records.title: Castell Conwy Interpretation Project
records.description:
Cadw is seeking to appoint a suitably qualified and experienced Interpretation Consultant to support a programme of new interpretation at Castell Conwy, north Wales. This will include researching and preparing an interpretation plan for Castell Conwy which will inform a suite of costed options for the design, fabrication, installation and ongoing maintenance of new interpretive media (considered to be RIBA stage 0/1 and then developed to RIBA stage 2). It is envisaged the interpretation will need to be procured alongside any required conservation building work at the monument.  The building work will be procured and led by Cadw’s Project Management Team.
As noted elsewhere in this notice (and accompanying tender documentation), the appointment of the successful contractor will be via a two-stage Competitive Flexible Procedure under the provisions of the Procurement Act 2023.  Stage 1 will consist of a qualification stage to assess bidder's capability and past experience in delivering complex high value interpretation projects at historically significant monuments.  Shortlisted bidders will then be invited to stage 2 where outline designs can be presented for evaluation.
The values included in this notice are further explained in the accompanying tender documentation and could be subject to increase.  The total included in the notice is for the design and fabrication/installation of all interpretation at Castell Conwy.  For clarity, this total value is split between £100,000 to £180,000 for the design element and £500,000 to  £800,000 for the fabrication/installation of the full interpretation scheme.  There is the possibility that the total value could increase to up to £2,000,000 for design and fabrication/installation but this upper limit is subject to additional approvals and budget availability.  Interested bidders should work to the £980,000 total when formulating their bid.

records.title: Replacement of Social Enterprise Dynamic Purchasing System (SEDPS)
records.description:
This notice relates to the procurement of the replacement of the Social Enterprise Dynamic Purchasing System (SEDPS) which expires on 14th August 2028. National Highways established SEDPS in 2023 to improve access to public sector contracting opportunities for VCSEs and other organisations that reinvest their surpluses to deliver social value. 
SEDPS was created to make public procurement more accessible by reducing barriers to entry and creating a simpler route to market for National Highways, its supply chain, and other public sector organisations. It also supports National Highways' broader social value ambitions by enabling a wider and more diverse range of organisations to compete for and secure procurement opportunities.
Following the introduction of the Procurement Act 2023, the existing Dynamic Purchasing System model will need to be replaced with an alternative vehicle when it expires in August 2028. National Highways are therefore considering the development of a replacement commercial vehicle that will build on the experience of the existing SEDPS, retain its core principles of accessibility and inclusivity, and continue to support opportunities for VCSEs.

records.title: CP2608-24 Highways Term Maintenance Contract
records.description:
Devon County Council (DCC) is undertaking a programme of Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) ahead of an upcoming procurement for a new NEC4 Term Service Contract for highway maintenance services.  Contract award is anticipated in 2028, with a contracted start of services on  1st April 2029.   
The current arrangement expires on 31 March 2029, and the Authority intends to put in place a future-focused, value-driven contract that supports safe, resilient and sustainable highway operations across Devon, both now and for the long term. 
This early engagement builds on feedback from previous market engagement, which is actively informing our emerging Contract Strategy. The purpose of this PME is to better understand market capacity, current innovations, risks and opportunities, and to help shape a procurement and contract structure that is fair, competitive and genuinely attractive to the market. 
Background  
DCC manages the largest highway network of any local authority in England, supporting residents, businesses and visitors across a uniquely varied geography. The network spans two national parks, two coastlines, remote rural communities and growing urban centres, presenting both opportunity and challenge for the delivery of highway maintenance services. 
The performance of the next contract will play a critical role in maintaining the safety, reliability and resilience of this network, while also helping the Council respond to wider pressures such as climate change, evolving customer expectations, workforce sustainability and the need to deliver long-term value for money. 
DCC is therefore seeking a delivery partner that can work with us in a collaborative, transparent and innovative way, recognising that strong outcomes will be achieved through long-term partnership rather than transactional contracting. 
The Authority is therefore seeking a solution that: 
-supports safe, reliable, and responsive services for residents, businesses and the travelling public 
-strengthens value for money and long-term affordability 
-unlocks efficiencies and delivers “more for less” through smarter ways of working 
-maximises performance through collaborative behaviours and shared ownership of outcomes 
-enables innovation and continuous improvement across the supply chain 
-contributes to DCC’s broader economic, environmental and social priorities, including carbon reduction and social value 
The indicative annual contract value is in the region on £65 million.  DCC is looking to establish a long-term relationship however the duration of the contract is yet to be determined.  
Vision 
DCC is committed to delivering high-quality, cost‑effective and resilient highway maintenance services. Through this procurement, we aim to: 
-appoint a Tier 1 delivery partner to establish a long-term, collaborative “win‑win” partnership aligned with ISO 44001 principles. 
-deliver economic, environmental and wider social benefits for communities across Devon. 
-create the conditions for continuous improvement, innovation, and modernisation throughout the life of the contract. 
-support consistency, efficiency and resilience and access for Tier 2 supply providers. 
We look forward to engaging with the market as we shape this important contract.  Your insight and experience will help inform a procurement and contractual model that is deliverable, collaborative, innovative and aligned with the long-term needs of Devon’s residents, communities and businesses. 
Thank you for your interest in working with Devon County Council.

records.buyer: NORTH CHESHIRE & MERSEY NHS FOUNDATION TRUST
records.title: Provision of EPR services
records.description:
North Cheshire & Mersey NHS Foundation Trust intends to enter into a contract with DH OpCo UK Ltd for the continued provision, support and maintenance of the Trust's existing Electronic Patient Record (EPR) services, including the Lorenzo and Ormis applications and associated existing interfaces, together with Lorenzo PatientAide and its associated implementation, configuration, support and maintenance services.
Lorenzo PatientAide is an additional module and was not included within the Trust's original agreement. 
The proposed agreement is intended to preserve the safe and continuous operation of clinically critical EPR services while the Trust undertakes a compliant re-procurement and, if required, implements and transitions to a replacement solution. The Trust may undertake that future procurement independently or in collaboration with another NHS organisation, depending on approved requirements and arrangements at that time.
The Trust's existing arrangements contain options to extend the incumbent services beyond 23 November 2026 through up to two further 12-month periods, potentially providing continuity until November 2028. While these provisions provide short-term flexibility, no further contractual extension rights exist beyond November 2028.
The proposed term reflects the Trust's current programme for procuring and implementing its future EPR arrangements, including the time required to complete the procurement, implementation, migration, integration, testing, training, clinical-safety assurance and transition activities.
The Trust has considered the extension rights available under the existing arrangements, including the potential for continuity until November 2028. However, those rights do not provide a reasonable alternative to the proposed contract. They expire before the Trust's revised EPR programme allows sufficient time to complete the planned EPR mini-competition and associated approval processes, and then safely implement the replacement solution, including configuration, data migration, integration, testing, training, clinical-safety assurance and deployment.
The additional period to 30 November 2029 is therefore required to maintain continuity while those activities are completed. Without it, the existing arrangements could end before the replacement EPR is operational, creating unacceptable clinical, operational and business-continuity risks.
The proposed term is a time-limited continuity measure to support transition to a replacement EPR and is not a longer-term commitment to the incumbent solution. The Trust does not consider competition to be permanently absent: the proposed direct award does not extend to the future replacement EPR, which is intended to be procured separately through competition.

options.description:
The agreement covers the continued provision, support and maintenance of the Lorenzo and Ormis applications and associated existing interfaces, together with the Lorenzo PatientAide module and associated services expressly described in this notice. Services necessary to operate, secure, maintain and support the contracted environment may be provided during the agreement period. The contract will be limited to the services and functionality described in this notice, together with the services reasonably necessary to operate, secure, maintain and support the identified Lorenzo, Ormis and PatientAide environment during the continuity period. It will not provide for materially new modules or functionality outside that scope.
The agreement is not intended to provide an unrestricted mechanism for the procurement of materially new modules, functionality or significant expansion beyond the scope set out in this notice.
The agreement will operate up to 30 November 2029. The Trust will keep the timetable for future procurement and transition under review and may exit earlier where this can be achieved safely, lawfully and operationally.
Charges may be adjusted by agreed CPI indexation and permitted evidenced third-party cost changes, provided these are included within the published maximum estimated value.

records.title: RBWM Tennis Concession Contract
records.description:
The Council is seeking to appoint a tennis coaching provider to deliver a high-quality, financially sustainable coaching programme across the tennis courts at Desborough Park, Goswells Park and Kidwells Park. The provider will be expected to grow participation, increase coaching income, deliver free weekly tennis sessions, engage under-represented groups, provide community and school outreach, and support wider health, wellbeing and social value outcomes for residents. The Council will retain ownership, strategic control, maintenance responsibilities and income from public court bookings and memberships, with the provider focusing on coaching delivery, customer service and programme development. The proposed contract term is three years, with two optional one-year extensions (3+1+1), with an estimated contract value of approximately £272,000 during the initial three-year term and a further £229,000 over the two extension years, giving an overall estimated contract value of around £501,000. The Council will only consider proposals that guarantee a minimum revenue share of 10% of coaching income payable to the Council, ensuring a direct financial return alongside the wider participation and social value benefits delivered through the contract. Overall, the Council is seeking a partner that can maximise participation, community impact and commercial performance while ensuring the long-term success of the recently refurbished park tennis facilities and delivering against the objectives of the Council Plan and Leisure Strategy.

records.title: NPH / West Northamptonshire Council Asset Investment Programme: Preliminary Market Engagement
records.description:
Northamptonshire Partnership Homes (“NPH”) is the Arm’s Length Management Organisation that manages approximately 11,500 homes on behalf of West Northamptonshire Council (“WNC” or the “Council”).
NPH is to return to the direct control of the Council, with the transfer due to complete on 01 April 2027. This preliminary market engagement is therefore being undertaken by NPH on behalf of both NPH and the Council. The Council is expected to be the contracting authority for the resulting contracts, and the tender notice for each contract will refer to this preliminary market engagement notice in accordance with section 17 of the Procurement Act 2023, whether that tender notice is published by NPH or by the Council.
NPH’s asset investment programme covers a broad range of whole-house investment and component renewals (such as kitchens and bathrooms, roofing, windows and doors, electrical works and energy efficiency measures); Aids & Adaptations; damp, mould and condensation (“DMC”) remediation; and disrepair, structural works, external works and major void refurbishments.
NPH's previous all-encompassing planned works contract ended in December 2024 and interim arrangements, comprising a mix of national and local contractors, are currently in place. NPH now wishes to establish a robust, long-term suite of asset investment contracts.
In addition to planned investment and component replacement works, NPH is considering a new long-term programme of cyclical decorations and planned preventative maintenance.
NPH will not seek to appoint a single contractor for all workstreams and has a clear strategic preference to enable participation by SMEs and local providers alongside larger contractors.
All arrangements under consideration are expected to be order-based, long term contracts, and for each workstream NPH intending to appoint multiple contractors, with works allocated on a planned basis as appropriate to the workstream. Supplementary small works arrangements (for example a dynamic market or small works framework) for low-value, in-year and ad hoc works aimed particularly at Northamptonshire SMEs may sit alongside the term contracts but this is subject to further consideration.
Individual contract lengths will be decided on a workstream basis however it is envisaged all contracts will be for an initial term of up to five years, with options to extend. The major investment contracts are to be procured and operational by approximately April 2028, and the specialist packages intended to be brought to market on a phased basis within the next 12 to 18 months.
This notice gives notice under section 17 of the Procurement Act 2023 that NPH, on behalf of itself and the Council, is conducting preliminary market engagement under section 16 of the Act in relation to the planned programme of asset investment contracts described above. The purpose of the engagement is to help NPH and the Council develop their requirements and approach to the procurements. Participation is voluntary and free of charge and this engagement does not form part of any procurement process and does not commit NPH or the Council to proceed with any procurement. In accordance with section 16(3) of the Act, steps will be taken to ensure that suppliers who participate are not put at an unfair advantage and that competition is not otherwise distorted; not participating will not disadvantage any supplier in any subsequent procurement.

records.title: SmokeFree App
records.description:
Suffolk County Council is looking to award a contract for the delivery of the SmokeFree App. The requirement includes app licences; unlimited 24/7 access to NCSCT-trained tobacco dependency advisers; behavioural and peer support; access to agreed stop smoking aids, including NRT and vape products; service monitoring; and quarterly outcome reporting. 
The service complements Suffolk's existing stop smoking provision by providing a flexible route that can be accessed without a fixed appointment. It is particularly suitable for people who may not engage with traditional provision, including shift workers, carers, pregnant women, people with mental health needs and users who value anonymous or out-of-hours support. 
The proposed contract term is one year with an option to extend for up to a further year. This is intended to maintain continuity while a regional or compliant framework route is developed and assessed.
The estimated value shown here is £304,800 inclusive of VAT. For the purposes of this estimate, VAT has been included at 20% (Standard Rate), however in some circumstances VAT may be exempt or chargeable at a different rate.

records.title: Framework for Tree Works on Housing Managed Land and Haigh Woodland Park - Preliminary Market Engagement
records.description:
Wigan Council is seeking feedback from the market to inform the development of a new Tree Works Framework for the delivery of planned, reactive and emergency arboricultural services at Haigh Woodland Park and Housing managed land across Wigan Borough. 
Wigan Council is undertaking this market engagement exercise to better understand market and supplier capacity and capability, market conditions, service delivery models, barriers to participation, and to help shape the final procurement approach. Responses to a Preliminary Market Engagement Questionnaire as part of this engagement will be used for market research purposes only and will not form part of any future tender evaluation. 
It is anticipated that the Framework will be established for a period of four (4) years and will have an estimated total value of up to £800,000 over the duration of the agreement. The Council is proposing to appoint up to three (3) contractors to the Framework, subject to the outcome of the procurement process. The Framework will be designed to provide access to suitably qualified and experienced contractors capable of delivering a broad range of tree works services in a safe, responsive, and cost-effective manner. 
Responses to the Preliminary Market Engagement Questionnaire should be returned by Friday 4th December 2026 at 17:00.

records.buyer: Department of Finance, Land and Property Services
records.title: DoF LPS Valuation Delivery Partner Project
records.description: Land and Property Services (LPS) is the statutory authority responsible for assessing and collecting property taxation in Northern Ireland. LPS is gearing up for a significant digital transformation aimed at enhancing its property valuation processes. In NI there are in the region of 825,500 Domestic properties, 72,000 Non-Domestic properties and 2,700 properties that contain an element of both domestic and non-domestic. The Directorate also provides a full range of non-rating valuation services to the public sector in Northern Ireland. LPS advises authorities on disposal and acquisition of land, market valuations and property advice, and both before and after valuations for vesting, on all aspects of compulsory purchase and negotiate compensation claims on their behalf. Valuation Services provides valuations (capital and rental) of land and property for a wide range of purposes, including calculations for assessment of benefits and business planning. The specific aims and objectives of this Valuation Delivery Partner Project are to: • implement a digital solution and service operating model which provides ICT functionality and business processes (including automated business processes) to support users to undertake the range of Valuation Services; • ensure that the procured ICT digital solution is flexible and adaptable to support future changes in business needs, supports data driven decision making, business process automation and is monitored and updated over time to embrace new technology that improves the user experience; • ensure the procured ICT digital solution is user friendly, customer-focused, geospatially enabled, supports web-based technologies, digital self-service platforms and provides a range of digital first ICT functionality that is capable of integrating with public facing applications (e.g. contact centre services, portals, 3rd party payment engines, authentication tools), line of business applications and back-office functions that supports intuitive and efficient case management and self-service offering the potential for delivering citizen centric public services; and • ensure the procured ICT solution provides Application Programme Interfaces (API’s) to allow integration with other LPS ICT systems and databases, government services and external systems, adopts an event driven architecture approach and complies with the wider Northern Ireland Civil Service (NICS) ‘digital first’ policy.

records.description:
Contract Background
The contract is for single supplier for the provision of Chillers, Air Conditioning Systems and Refrigeration Maintenance Contract at The Pirbright Institute.
Scope of works
Work Package 1 – Chillers, Air Conditioning & Refrigeration Equipment 
This works package is for a single supplier to service and or repair all refrigeration, air conditioning and associated systems at The Pirbright Institute.
Service visits should be arranged according to F gas regulations, site requirements and insurance inspections schedules. 
The attached schedule (Schedule 5.C - Refrigeration Plant List) details the buildings, the details of the Chillers, Freezers and Air conditioning equipment and frequency of service visits required. A site plan showing the locations and relative sizes of these buildings is included in Schedule 5.D - Site Plan.
The contractor will be expected to advise on the condition of the equipment and provide details of any remedial works required following each service. Critical remedial works should be advised to Pirbright on the same day.
Quotations for non-critical remedial works should be provided to Pirbright within 1 week of a service visit.
The contractor should also allow for the supply of:
•	1 x vacuum pump
•	1 x recovery machine
•	1 x set of gauges
•	1 x refrigerant leak detector
These will be kept in our restricted areas and will only be used by the contractor.  These can be taken out of containment and returned to contractor at the end of the contract. This is to prevent the unnecessary passage and time-consuming decontamination for contractor’s tools when work is being done on our contained systems. 
Within the first 6 months of the contract the contractor will be expected to provide a critical spares list and an itemised quotation for all systems.
Service reports should be left on site or received by site on the day of the service and test certificates should be received by site within one week of the service visit.
In addition to providing their own access equipment, it is expected that the supplier will include in their works, performing basic tasks required to access equipment such as lifting ceiling panels.
Work Package 2 – Emergency Call out Service
The supplier of works package 1 must also provide a 24-hour emergency call out service. With an engineer site attendance time of under 4 hours. All specification requirements that are associated with work package 1 also apply this work package.
Work Package 3 – Insurance Inspection Facilitation
The contractor will need to allow for the supply of an engineer to aid our insurance inspector with PSSR inspections on chillers. This can take up to 5 days per year.

Proposed delivery model The Councils are considering a joint service in which they retain control of repair diagnosis, prioritisation, scheduling and allocation, and hold the repair record in their own systems. Guildford’s existing directly employed team would initially deliver a defined share of routine repairs, based on available capacity. A principal contractor would provide services across both boroughs from the outset, including complex, multi-trade and specialist repairs, out-of-hours cover and additional capacity to meet peaks in demand. The Councils may expand direct delivery over time, including into Waverley, where workforce capacity, performance and value for money support doing so. As direct delivery grows, the contractor may receive fewer routine repairs and a greater proportion of complex and less predictable work. If direct delivery grows more slowly than planned, the contractor may need to take on additional routine repairs within agreed limits. The Councils want to test what allocation rules, minimum contracted volumes or workload shares, and pricing arrangements would make that model viable for contractors. They also want to understand how support for developing the Councils’ workforce could be specified and priced, including training, apprenticeships and supervisory support.   Scope and commercial arrangements The Councils are testing a potential contract term of up to ten years. The core requirement would be responsive repairs and out-of-hours cover. The Councils are also considering whether void property works, cyclical decorations, component replacements or selected planned works could be included to provide a more predictable mix of work. Feedback is invited on whether specialist services such as scaffolding, roofing and asbestos works should sit within the principal contract or be procured separately.

records.title: Works Framework
records.description:
Birmingham City Council (BCC) has undertaken preliminary market engagement in relation to the proposed establishment of a BCC-owned Construction Framework. The framework is intended to provide a structured, compliant and commercially controlled route to market for addressable construction works across the Council's estate, operational assets, housing and wider capital programme.
The proposed framework is intended to improve value for money, commercial control, pricing transparency, supplier management, social value delivery and visibility of spend and performance, while providing access to both general contractors and specialist suppliers.
The current proposed framework structure comprises the following Lots and value bands:
•	Lot 1A - General Building Refurbishment and Planned Works - up to £1m
•	Lot 1B - General Building Refurbishment and Planned Works - over £1m
•	Lot 2 - Residential Major Projects, Building Safety and Fire Safety Works
•	Lot 3 - New Build, Major Capital Works and Redevelopment
•	Lot 4 - Mechanical, Electrical, Public Health and Decarbonisation Works
•	Lot 5 - Demolition, Enabling and Site Preparation Works
The framework is intended to increase opportunities for Birmingham and wider West Midlands-based suppliers, including SMEs and specialist contractors, through proportionate supplier requirements, specialist Lots and the lower-value Lot 1A band.
The current proposed approach is to establish a seven-and-a-half-year open framework, with a planned reopening in year three to support supplier refresh, continued market access and competition. The framework itself will not commit BCC to any minimum level of expenditure; individual call-off contracts will remain subject to project budget, governance and approval requirements.
Subject to final procurement arrangements, the framework may also be made available to other eligible public sector organisations, including West Midlands councils and other regional public bodies.
Since publication of the previous preliminary market engagement notice, BCC has further developed the proposed framework following market engagement, internal stakeholder engagement, spend analysis and procurement strategy development. The proposed approach has moved from an indicative four-year closed framework model to a seven-and-a-half-year open framework, with a planned supplier refresh in year three. The estimated framework value has also been revised from £1.54 billion to £3.23 billion excluding VAT to reflect the latest spend analysis, intended scope and longer framework term. The procurement timetable has been updated accordingly, with Tender Notice publication now planned for January 2027, subject to completion of the relevant governance and procurement processes.
The framework scope and lotting structure have also been developed in greater detail. The previous notice described broad areas including planned works, refurbishment, new build and demolition. The current proposal now defines specialist Lots and value bands covering general building refurbishment and planned works, residential major projects and building safety, new build and major capital works, mechanical and electrical/public health/decarbonisation works, and demolition/enabling/site preparation works. The lower-value Lot 1A and specialist Lots are intended to provide more proportionate and accessible entry points for SMEs and specialist contractors, while the revised structure also supports stronger commercial control, supplier performance management and visibility of spend.
The Council will use its e-tendering system, In-tend, for administration of the procurement process. Potential suppliers should register with the Birmingham City Council In-tend portal to access relevant procurement documentation when published. records.title: Prior Information Notice – Alternative Delivery Model
records.description:
Aberdeen City Council (‘the Council’) is issuing this Prior Information Notice (PIN) to advance notice of emerging proposals relating to the future delivery of leisure, culture and arena services and associated assets across the city, and to seek high-level, non-binding market feedback to inform the Council’s ongoing considerations and any future procurement strategy.
This PIN builds upon market sounding undertaken in 2025, which explored market interest in delivery of bundled culture and leisure services and tested appetite for opportunities within Aberdeen’s leisure, museums and galleries, and arts and culture portfolio.
Since that engagement and the development of an OBC, the scope of the Alternative Delivery Model workstream has been reviewed and refined by the Council and its advisors. The scope has been expanded to include The Event Complex Aberdeen (TECA) both the arena and the conference centre, which was not considered as part of the 2025 market sounding. Museums and galleries services and assets are no longer being taken forward within the current workstream and are therefore excluded from the scope of this engagement.
The indicative contract values set out in this Notice are based on 2025 service turnover projected over the proposed contract term. Estimates have been provided on both VAT-exclusive and VAT-inclusive bases, with VAT calculated at the prevailing rate of 20%. All figures are indicative, rounded to the nearest million, and subject to further review and refinement, including consideration of inflation, scope development and future capital investment requirements.
For the avoidance of doubt, existing Tier 1 Arm’s Length External Organisations (ALEOs), incumbent operators and current service providers are invited to participate in this engagement on equal, transparent and non-preferential basis alongside all other interested parties.

The framework itself will not commit BCC to any minimum level of expenditure; individual call-off commissions will remain subject to relevant budget, governance and approval requirements.
Subject to final procurement arrangements, the framework may also be made available to other eligible public sector organisations, including West Midlands councils and other regional public bodies.
Since publication of the previous preliminary market engagement notice, BCC has further developed the proposed framework following market engagement, internal stakeholder engagement, spend analysis and procurement strategy development. The proposed approach has moved from an indicative four-year closed framework model to a seven-and-a-half-year open framework, with a planned supplier refresh after approximately three years. The estimated framework value has also been revised from £72 million to £225 million excluding VAT to reflect the latest spend analysis, anticipated usage and longer framework term. The procurement timetable has been updated accordingly.
The framework scope and lotting structure have also been developed in greater detail. The previous notice described indicative areas such as planning, surveying, project management, development and regeneration advice. The current proposal now sets out five defined Lots covering multi-disciplinary consultancy; strategic property, development and regeneration advisory; project, programme and commercial management; design and pre-planning; and specialist technical, compliance, housing and site investigation services. The revised structure reflects feedback received through preliminary market engagement and is intended to support clearer routes to market, SME and specialist supplier participation, stronger commercial control and more consistent supplier management.

The service will support trainees experiencing difficulties with clinical and professional communication, including preparation for OSCE and other practical examinations, and will help develop the competencies required for safe, effective and patient-centred care. This includes improving communication with patients, carers and multidisciplinary teams, managing complex and sensitive conversations, enhancing clinical documentation and handovers, and supporting professional development. The overall aim is to strengthen trainee performance, promote patient safety, improve training outcomes and support the delivery of high-quality healthcare across the NHS.

records.description:
The Authority, being The Dudley Group NHS University Foundation Trust, is conducting this Procurement for the provision of a Remote Monitoring and Virtual Ward Solution.

records.title: Safe moves: support to navigate romance and investment fraud
records.description:
Ofcom has a requirement for a supplier with expertise in working with men and women’s organisations/ networks to develop and deliver a media literacy intervention around romance fraud. This supplier will also amplify existing resources around investment fraud by embedding them into existing provision for the same cohort.
The service must deliver the following by September 2027:
• Development of activities and resources for men and women under 45 to better protect them against and increase confidence around issues pertaining to romance and investment fraud. This may be training, workshops, webinars, interactive resources etc. - we expect any development of activities or resources to be co-produced with target participants.
• Embedding of existing activities and resources into existing delivery of existing digital inclusion activities, for example, training, events or support, with men and women under 45.
• Stakeholder engagement which must include:
o Promoting media literacy activities to other relevant community organisations.
o Supporting activities intended to inform policy development, which will be led by Ofcom e.g. a presentation to the Ofcom team.
o Seeking input from expert steering group, convened by the tendering supplier.
• The successful supplier will need to deliver an evaluation report demonstrating impact for participants against agreed key outcomes to be delivered a month before the end of the contract.

records.title: RHOI: Ymgyrch Marchnata Integredig, Cyfathrebu a Newid Ymddygiad / Integrated Marketing, Communications and Behaviour Change Campaign
records.description:
Mae RHOI wedi cael ei ysbrydoli gan lwyddiant CopenPay ac mae'n rhan o'r dull rhyngwladol ehangach DestinationPay. Mae'r egwyddor sylfaenol yn syml: anogir pobl i wneud rhywbeth cadarnhaol ar gyfer y lleoedd maen nhw'n ymweld â nhw ac, yn gyfnewid, derbyn gwobr gan fusnes neu sefydliad sy'n cymryd rhan.
Bydd y rhaglen yn canolbwyntio i ddechrau ar Y Bala a Betws-y-Coed fel ardaloedd peilot, gyda'r nod o dyfu ar draws rhanbarth ehangach Eryri dros amser. Bydd gweithgareddau'n cael eu darparu gan amrywiaeth o sefydliadau partner, grwpiau cymunedol, busnesau a sefydliadau eraill. Bydd busnesau sy'n cymryd rhan yn darparu gwobrau i bobl sy'n cwblhau gweithgareddau cymwys.
Mae enghreifftiau o'r mathau o ymddygiad y gallai RHOI eu hannog yn cynnwys dewis trafnidiaeth gyhoeddus, gwirfoddoli, cymryd rhan mewn gweithgareddau casglu sbwriel neu gadwraeth, cefnogi gweithgareddau diwylliannol lleol, dysgu neu ddefnyddio'r Gymraeg, a chymryd rhan mewn gweithgareddau sy'n cyfrannu'n gadarnhaol at gymunedau ac amgylchedd yr ardal.
Nid yw'r rhaglen wedi'i bwriadu i weithredu fel cynllun disgownt na theyrngarwch confensiynol. Rhoddir pwyslais ar annog pobl i wneud dewisiadau cadarnhaol a chymryd rhan mewn gweithgareddau ystyrlon, gyda gwobrau'n darparu cymhelliant ychwanegol.
Felly, dylai'r ymgyrch ganolbwyntio ar newid ymddygiad yn ogystal â chodi ymwybyddiaeth ac annog pobl i lawrlwytho’r ap.
Ffordd ddefnyddiol o feddwl am daith y defnyddiwr arfaethedig yw:
GWELD → DEALL → YMUNO → GWEITHREDU → DERBYN GWOBR → RHANNU → AILADRODD
Disgwylir i'r cyflenwr llwyddiannus ddatblygu'r daith hon ymhellach a nodi'r cyfathrebiadau, yr ymyriadau ymddygiadol a'r gweithgaredd marchnata sydd eu hangen ym mhob cam.
//
Eryri National Park Authority is seeking to appoint an experienced marketing and communications supplier to develop and deliver an integrated bilingual Welsh/English marketing and behaviour-change campaign for RHOI, a new initiative designed to encourage visitors and local people to take part in activities that do environmental, cultural and community 'good’.
RHOI has been inspired by the success of CopenPay and forms part of the wider international DestinationPay approach. The basic principle is simple: people are encouraged to do something positive for the places they visit and, in return, receive a reward from a participating business or organisation.
The programme will initially focus on Bala and Betws-y-Coed as pilot areas, with the aim to grow across the wider region of Eryri over time. Activities will be provided by a range of partner organisations, community groups, businesses and other organisations. Participating businesses will provide rewards to people who complete eligible activities.
Examples of the types of behaviour RHOI could encourage include choosing public transport;, volunteering;, taking part in litter-picking or conservation activities,; supporting local cultural activity,; learning or using Welsh;, and taking part in activities that contribute positively to the communities and environment of the area.
The programme is not intended to operate as a conventional discount or loyalty scheme. The emphasis is on encouraging people to make positive choices and participate in meaningful activities, with rewards providing an additional motivation.
The campaign should therefore be concerned with behaviour change as much as awareness or app downloads.
A useful way of thinking about the intended user journey is:
SEE → UNDERSTAND → JOIN → ACT → REWARD → SHARE → REPEAT
The successful supplier will be expected to develop this journey further and identify the communications, behavioural interventions and marketing activity required at each stage.

records.title: RFQ 2026/48 - PEACEPLUS Roots Relationships Programme - Slieve Gullion DEA
records.description:
To deliver a community-led Arts, Crafts and Heritage Capacity Building Programme in the Slieve Gullion DEA, working with community groups from the Forkhill and Newtownhamilton areas.
The programme should use arts, crafts, cultural heritage and creative skills development as a vehicle for building organisational capacity, increasing skills and confidence, supporting knowledge exchange, and creating opportunities for participants to learn from one another through practical activities, shared experiences and networking opportunities.
The programme should celebrate and explore the rich cultural and heritage assets of the area while creating opportunities for participants from different backgrounds to connect, collaborate and develop lasting relationships. Through shared learning and creative engagement, participants will strengthen both their individual skills and the sustainability of their community organisations.
This project will serve as both a community development initiative and a peacebuilding mechanism, creating sustained and meaningful contact across communities while strengthening local organisations and promoting appreciation of the area's diverse cultural heritage.

records.title: Well Wave Plus: (Open Access and Equity)
records.description:
The Well Wave Plus: Open Access and Equity contract will complement and enhance the existing Well Wave service. Well Wave is a city wide, universal offer for young people
aged 13-24, overseen by the Leeds City Council Public Health team. Trained workers offer confidential, non-clinical relationships and sexual health support, where young people can explore ideas, build skills and access free condom products,
lubricant, and pregnancy testing, plus STI self-screening kits. These drop-in services are
located within organisations where young people already attend. 
This contract will enhance current provision by introducing specialist, dedicated Well Wave Plus workers with the skills to engage and appropriately support most at risk, least
well-supported and seldom seen young people aged 13-24 years old. Currently, most workers trained to deliver Well Wave provide the service voluntarily within their
substantive roles (e.g. in youth clubs or educational settings). Under this contract, dedicated workers will be employed solely to deliver and promote Well Wave services, without constraints on location or caseload. These workers will focus on ensuring equity of access for seldom seen, marginalised or under pressure young people by developing and delivering flexible, accessible, and culturally sensitive Well Wave outreach in appropriate
community setting

records.title: Provision of Custody Laundry Services
records.description:
Provision of Custody Laundry Services, PCC/PD/1373. 
Items from all custody suites will be laundered and returned.
The contracting authority is making a direct award for an interim laundry and linen service to ensure continuity of critical custody operations following the unexpected failure of the incumbent supplier, The loss of this service created an immediate and unforeseeable operational risk affecting the provision of detainee clothing, blankets and towels across the custody estate. A delay in securing replacement provision would have presented a significant risk to detainee welfare and the effective operation of custody facilities. The contracting authority considers that the circumstances satisfy the urgent requirements provisions of the Procurement Act 2023, as the need for the contract has arisen from events that could not reasonably have been foreseen and the urgency is such that a competitive procurement cannot be completed in the time available. This award is strictly limited to the period necessary to maintain service continuity and mitigate the immediate operational risk. A full competitive procurement process will be commenced in due course to establish a longer-term contractual arrangement.

records.title: London Cable Car Customer Enhancements
records.description:
This is a competitive procurement for the award of a single contract for the London Cable Car Customer Enhancements project. Transport for London is seeking to appoint a suitably qualified and experienced supplier to provide the Concept Design, Detailed Design and Delivery/Implementation of customer experience enhancements at the London Cable Car, with a primary focus on the South Terminal at Greenwich Peninsula. 
The programme forms part of TfL's strategy to enhance the London Cable Car customer experience and support its continued development as a leading leisure attraction while maintaining its transport function. The successful supplier will be required to develop and deliver a coordinated package of enhancements anticipated to include: 
- Modular, prefabricated and temporary structures (including canopies, shelters and temporary or semi-permanent kiosks such as food and beverage units). 
- Customer experience, exhibition and interpretation solutions (including interactive installations, model displays, screens, projection and interpretive content supporting the 'Evolving Views of London' concept). 
- Lighting solutions (including architectural, feature and experiential lighting to support wayfinding, ambience and interpretation). 
- Signage, wayfinding, branding and graphic systems shall be developed in accordance with TfL and cable car branding principles, while also being sensitive to the character of the surrounding environment.  
- Digital content, audiovisual and media production (including digital collateral, audio‑visual imagery, projection and immersive content for display or presentation). 
- All physical aspects of the customer journey within the customer experience centre, inclusive of toilets, F&B, retail and conferencing space, and supporting back of house functions. 
The current budget allocation for this contract is £3.4million. 
The contract to be awarded will be the NEC3 Engineering and Construction Short Contract with TfL amendments. 
The contract is intended to be delivered in stages, comprising Concept Design, Detailed Design and Delivery/Implementation. Progression between stages will be subject to the contracting authority issuing a formal Notice to Proceed. Progression to subsequent stages is not guaranteed and will remain at the discretion of the contracting authority.

records.title: CBC-2107-FW-SK -  Alternative Education and Provision
records.description:
Central Bedfordshire Council and Bedford Borough Council invite suitably qualified suppliers to apply for admission to the Alternative Education and Provision Framework.
This Framework is established for Light Touch Services and will provide access to high-quality alternative education and support services for children and young people aged 5 to 25 who are unable to access, or fully engage with, mainstream education.
The Framework will support children and young people with a range of needs, including Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND), Social, Emotional and Mental Health (SEMH) needs, medical needs, and other barriers to learning. Provision may include, but is not limited to, alternative education programmes, outreach support, mentoring, therapeutic interventions, vocational learning, specialist tuition, and other services designed to improve educational attainment, wellbeing, engagement, confidence, resilience, attendance, and progression into education, employment, or training.
Services will be delivered across the geographical areas of Central Bedfordshire and Bedford Borough.
Suppliers applying to deliver Outreach Services must have an operational base within the administrative boundaries of Central Bedfordshire Council or Bedford Borough Council. The Authority considers a local presence necessary to ensure responsive service delivery, effective partnership working, timely support for children and young people, and attendance at meetings and interventions where required. Where Outreach Services are delivered from premises, those premises must be located within the postcode areas specified within the procurement documents.
The Framework Agreement will be open to multiple suppliers who meet the requirements set out in the procurement documents, with call-off contracts awarded in accordance with the terms of the Framework Agreement.
The Council will provide as much support and information as it can to help guide you through the quotation process. Questions asked together with the response, will be made available to all tenderers, to ensure a fair and consistent approach to all.
If there is anything you are not sure about or need clarification on, please use the Correspondence facility within the In-tend electronic tendering system. Last date for receiving questions on the In-Tend system: Tuesday 8th December 2026 by 5:00pm.

records.title: NHS Essex Preliminary Market Engagement Notice for Online Consultation Provision
records.description:
NHS Essex ICB is undertaking preliminary market engagement under section 16 of the Procurement Act 2023 to better understand the solutions available in advance of a procurement for Online Consultation software. Suppliers are invited to demonstrate how their solution supports general practice, including its key functionality, with an opportunity for participating practices and the ICB to ask clarification questions.
Participation in this preliminary market engagement is voluntary. Suppliers are responsible for deciding whether to participate. Participation, or non-participation, will not confer any advantage or disadvantage in any subsequent procurement. The purpose of the engagement is to inform and develop the ICB’s Statement of Requirements and procurement approach; it does not form part of a supplier selection, shortlisting or contract award process.
General practices across NHS Essex ICB currently use a range of Online Consultation solutions according to local requirements. The ICB anticipates that differing practice requirements may continue to be reflected in the future procurement approach, potentially by grouping practices into cohorts with similar requirements. No decision has yet been made on the final requirements, procurement structure, procurement route or supplier selection. These will be determined following this preliminary market engagement and in accordance with the applicable procurement requirements and the relevant framework rules.

records.title: Communications, Creative and Print Services
records.description:
whg is seeking to appoint suppliers to provide Communications, Creative and Print Services. The procurement is divided into two Lots, with a separate contract to be awarded for each Lot. Suppliers may tender for one or both Lots and may be awarded one or both Lots.
Lot 1 - Strategic Creative and Campaign Services
whg requires the appointment of a single supplier to act as a strategic communications and creative campaign delivery agency, providing specialist support to the in-house Communications team.
The Agency will be expected to deliver insight-led communications and marketing campaigns that achieve measurable outcomes and demonstrate value for money. In addition to campaign delivery, the Agency will act as a strategic partner, providing industry expertise, audience insight, market intelligence and innovative thinking to support whg's longer-term communications objectives.
The Agency will be expected to demonstrate a strong understanding of the housing, public and charitable sectors and the ability to engage effectively with a range of stakeholders and key audience groups.
Services may include, but are not limited to:
•	Insight gathering and audience research.
•	Campaign strategy and planning.
•	Creative concept development.
•	Design and creative direction.
•	Campaign delivery.
•	Monitoring and reporting.
•	Post-campaign evaluation.
Typical projects may include customer communication campaigns, including service or safety information; recruitment campaigns; organisational change and transformation communications; internal communication and engagement campaigns; and behavioural change campaigns. These examples are illustrative and are not exhaustive.
Where campaigns include printed materials, the Lot 1 Agency may develop production-ready artwork and recommend appropriate layouts, formats, paper stocks, finishes and printing techniques. The Agency shall provide approved print-ready artwork and specifications to whg and, where required by whg, support the supplier appointed under Lot 2 to ensure the final printed materials reflect the approved creative concept and brand standards.
Lot 2 - Design, Artwork and Promotional Print Services
whg requires the appointment of a single supplier to provide design, artwork and promotional print services to support the in-house Communications team. The supplier will deliver high-quality creative assets and digital and printed collateral that support corporate, internal and external communications and whg's organisational priorities.
The supplier will be responsible for translating communications objectives and creative briefs into effective visual communications across digital and print channels.
Services may include, but are not limited to:
•	Graphic design, including infographics.
•	Creative artwork and brand application.
•	Document, publication and presentation design.
•	Digital asset creation and social media graphics.
•	Promotional print production, including merchandise.
•	Print management and fulfilment.
•	Event and exhibition printed materials.
The appointed supplier shall produce printed materials in accordance with approved artwork and production specifications provided or approved by whg and, where required by whg, shall work collaboratively with the Agency appointed under Lot 1 to ensure high-quality outputs.
Interface between the Lots
The suppliers appointed to each Lot shall demonstrate the flexibility, capacity and capability to deliver whg's requirements through a seamless and coordinated service offering.
Where a requirement involves both Lots, whg may require the suppliers to work collaboratively with each other and with the in-house Communications team. Each supplier shall remain responsible for the quality, performance and delivery of the Services commissioned from it.

records.title: UK Space Agency- Strategic Support to the International Charter: Space and Major Disasters
records.description:
The International Charter: Space and Major Disasters (“the Charter”) is a global agreement which aims to provide a unified system of space data acquisition and delivery to those affected by natural or man-made disasters. It provides and enables transmission of earth observation satellite data and pre-authorised resilience/emergency response bodies in response to “activations”. Further details on the Charter can be found at https://disasterscharter.org/.
Charter members are national government bodies/ agencies or recognised space system organisations, who are the owners/ operators of earth observation satellite missions and have access to contributing resources/ assets/ facilities to sustainability support, co-ordinate and govern ongoing Charter operations. These members and their partners all strive to meet the common goal of providing assured, co-ordinated and timely access to satellite data to assist recognised rescue/ resilience authorities in the event of a natural or manmade disaster to ultimately help minimise losses and save lives. 
The UK has been a Charter member since 2005 and wishes to continue to play an active leadership role in this highly regarded and valued global initiative. To meet our agreed national obligations to our international partners, end users within the UK Government and its’ partners, UK Space Agency (UKSA) has an enduring requirement for the provision of Strategic Support, and ongoing technical/specialist Operational Support to support ongoing satellite imagery provision as these technical capabilities and specialist skills do not currently exist/reside within UKSA. 
 This will ensure that the UK continues to meet its obligations to this international agreement, whilst also continuing to make the best use of UK assets and resources. However please note that the UK Operational Support aspects of this role will not form part of this procurement opportunity, and instead will be provided under a separate contract. This specification refers only to those requirements necessary for the strategic support role. This role will involve significant interaction between UKSA (now a directorate within the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT)), UK Government stakeholders, the Charter Executive Secretariat and the UK Operational Support provider.

records.title: Inward Investment Proposition Refresh
records.description:
West Midlands Growth Company (WMGC) is seeking to appoint a suitably qualified supplier to refresh its inward investment sector and subsector propositions, ensuring that they are current, compelling, evidence-led and responsive to evolving investor requirements and market opportunities.
The commission will draw on relevant existing intelligence, including the previous Sector Narrative Refresh and resulting investment pitchbooks, alongside the 2024–25 Regional Inward Investment Review and associated sector strategies. These materials will serve as reference sources rather than a fixed strategic baseline, recognising that market conditions, investor requirements and investment opportunities have evolved since their development.
The appointed supplier will undertake up-to-date market and investor-focused research to identify current and emerging investment drivers, opportunities and location requirements. This will inform an assessment of the West Midlands' strengths and capabilities, and an analysis of its competitive position relative to alternative investment locations in the UK and internationally, including the market dynamics and commercial factors that may influence investor decisions.
The primary outcome of the commission is a clear, evidence-based set of investment messages that WMGC can proactively position to inward investment intermediaries, including site selectors, and other relevant audiences. Taken together, these messages must comprehensively but succinctly answer the question: What types of inward investment is the West Midlands well positioned to support, or uniquely capable of supporting?’ They should identify specific types of investment, business activities and operating functions, explaining the region's suitability and compelling points of differentiation, with any claim of unique capability substantiated by evidence. The refreshed, differentiated sector and subsector investment value propositions and messages will be supported by a structured and maintainable resource containing the underpinning market intelligence, regional evidence, statistics, case studies and competitive insights. The resource should enable WMGC teams to readily access, adapt and update content for tailored investor engagement, business development and future marketing collateral, rather than relying on a new suite of static pitchbooks.
This is an open advertised, below threshold Procurement requiring the submission of proposals, pricing information and mandatory supplier information. 
Access to the full tender document pack can be found at https://supplier.in-tend.co.uk/wmgrowth/home

records.title: NHM150 Western Galleries - Lighting Design
records.description:
The Natural History Museum has launched NHM150, an ambitious transformation programme leading up to its 150th anniversary in 2031. The programme will significantly enhance the Museum’s public offer, increasing access, reach and impact through a major renewal of galleries and visitor experiences. 
Through NHM150, the Museum will: 
-Breathe new life into four existing galleries. 
-Open three magnificent new galleries. 
-Showcase the natural world’s treasures to one million more visitors a year. 
-Engage 10 million school children, families and changemakers through local national and global programmes. 
-Create over 100 million advocates for the planet. 
The first phase of the programme is already underway. The second phase will focus on the western wing of the Waterhouse Building and will combine base-build refurbishment works, including improvements to circulation and visitor facilities, with the design and installation of new exhibitions and displays (the "gallery fit-out"  projects). 
The second phase will form part of the Museum's National Lottery Heritage Fund (NLHF) funding application.
As part of Phase 2, the Museum has appointed Lead Designers for the fit-out of the following four galleries:
•Old General Herbarium
•Origins Gallery
•Dinosaur Gallery 1
•Dinosaur Gallery 2 (former Swing Space)
Following the appointment of the Lead Design teams, the Museum intends to appoint specialist Lighting Designers to join the multidisciplinary design teams delivering each gallery project

records.title: RCC-1652 THE PROVISION OF DRY MIXED RECYCLING TREATMENT AND PROCESSING SERVICES
records.description:
Rutland County Council is seeking suppliers who are able to receive and accept the Council's Dry Mixed Recycling (DMR) at a designated Primary Delivery Point. This may be a Materials Recovery Facility (MRF) where the initial treatment (i.e. sorting) of the DMR shall occur, or this may be a facility where this DMR will be bulked up for onward haulage to a Secondary Facility where the initial treatment (i.e. sorting) of the DMR shall occur.
The supplier shall also provide for a Contingency Delivery Point, to which the Council's DMR will be diverted, for receipt and acceptance, in the event that, for any reason, the Contractor cannot receive and accept the same at the Primary Delivery Point. Such diversions shall be utilised for planned and unplanned maintenance as well as for other unforeseen circumstances.
The Council's Waste Collection Contractor collects co-mingled recyclate from all Rutland households. The majority of collections are from 240litre wheeled bins, with some collections being from larger/communal bins and a very small number of collections being bagged. These collections also incorporate a small number of 'commercial' and 'Schedule 2' properties. For the purpose of this Agreement, all such co-mingled recyclate, except for that collected from a small number of properties on what is referred to as the 'Farms and Lodges Round', is defined as the Council's Dry Mixed Recycling (DMR). Co-mingled recyclate collected on the Farms and Lodges Round shall not be dealt with under this Agreement.

records.title: Reopening of the Flexible Purchasing Framework for Social Care Support
records.description:
GCHSCP is reopening this framework to new providers and for existing providers to bid to deliver additional lots and categories of support. Details of the reopening are outlined in section V1.3 of this Prior Information Notice.
Glasgow City Health and Social Care Partnership (GCHSCP) has been adapting the way people  access support that meets their needs whilst promoting and maintaining their independence. We recognise that closer engagement with communities, families, carers and the individuals that we support is required: focusing on the assets and strengths that individuals and their communities already have; to transform the way we all collaborate, maximising the opportunity for individuals to live independent lives and achieve their full potential. Connecting individuals with their communities is a key objective of maximising independence, and access to health and social care support, when needed, can improve health and wellbeing and support individuals to become more resilient. GCHSCP concluded a review of the access to social work services in 2024 to ensure our approach is fair and equitable for those eligible for services. The GCHSCP eligibility criteria will focus on those with substantial and critical need.
Self Directed Support (SDS) is a co-production and supportive process involving good conversations with individuals needing support. SDS, alongside other legislation and policies, is intended to respect, protect and fulfil human rights, and aims to ensure that care and support is delivered in a way that supports choice and control over one's own life and which respects individual's right to participate in society.
SDS applies across all ages, including unpaid carers and children, ensuring:
- Disabled people have the same freedom and choices as others.
- People get the support they want, where and when they want it.
- People can get support at the right time, before a crisis or emergency happens.
Glasgow City Council has a statutory duty to assess care needs and establish eligibility for social care services under the Social Care (Self Directed Support) (Scotland) Act 2013.The Flexible Purchasing Framework for Social Care Supports will be the mechanism through which the Council discharges its duties for SDS Options 2, 3, and aspects of option 4.
This is a multi supplier and multi lot unranked Framework and there is no limit to the number of providers that can be awarded to the Framework.
The Framework Agreement will be based on Care Groups to deliver support to people:
-Older People over 65 yrs old and / or under 65 with early onset dementia.
-Adults Learning Disability - including people with learning disabilities and autism, people who have learning disabilities with a physical disability, or any combination of these.
-Adults Physical Disability - people who have a physical disability without a learning disability.
-Adults Mental Health - people with mental health and/or related conditions, including Huntington’s and people with neurodiversity who have no learning disability.
-Children and Young People with a disability.
The Framework Agreement also includes an additional requirement for when the Council determines needs cannot be met under one of the Care Groups above.
Bidders will be invited to submit their pricing schedule for the Categories of Support they are able to offer to help the Council achieve its aims and objectives to help individuals to live as independently as possible and to deliver on its statutory duties. These are:
-Care and support services (personal and non-personal care)
-Day opportunities/employability supports community based
-Day opportunities/employability supports building based
-Short Breaks community based
-Short Breaks building based (Children and Young People with a Disability only)
-Any additional supports offered by Providers including Technology Enabled Care and Support

amendments.description:
DVLA has modified the existing Payment Gateway Services Contract by extending the contract term for an initial period of twelve (12) months, for the period of 1 June 2027 to 31 May 2028, with the option to extend for a further period of up to six (6) months, for the period of 1 June 2028 to 30 November 2028, if required. 
The modification is necessary to ensure the continued provision of critical payment gateway services whilst the replacement procurement is completed and the successor service is mobilised, implemented, integrated, tested and transitioned into live operation
amendments.rationale:
Need for modification brought about by circumstances which a diligent contracting authority/entity could not foresee: Justification for Modification 
During the planning and development of the replacement Payment Gateway Services procurement, Ministerial decisions relating to the implementation of the Electronic Vehicle Excise Duty (eVED) regime introduced additional requirements and dependencies that could not have been fully anticipated when the contract was awarded. As a result, further time has been required to define requirements, complete technical, governance and commercial activities, and progress the replacement procurement. 
The extension is necessary to maintain continuity of critical payment services whilst procurement, implementation, integration, testing and transition activities are completed. The modification is a permitted modification under Regulation 72(1)(c) of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015, does not alter the overall nature of the contract, and is limited to the period necessary to complete these activities. 
Legal Basis 
This modification is made in accordance with Regulation 72(1)(c) of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015, as: 
The need for modification has arisen from circumstances which a diligent contracting authority could not have foreseen, including evolving requirements and Ministerial decisions relating to the implementation of the Electronic Vehicle Excise Duty (eVED) service. 
The modification does not alter the overall nature of the contract. 
The extension is necessary to ensure continuity of service and facilitate the procurement, implementation, integration and transition of the replacement solution. 
The value of the 12month extension was £608,526; as required for reliance on Regulation 72(1)(c) PCR, this is less than 50% of the value of the original contract, this being £5,000,000. 
Extension Period 
Initial extension: 12 months (1 June 2027 to 31 May 2028) 
Optional additional extension: up to 6 months (1 June 2028 to 30 November 2028) 
Total potential extension: 18 months (1 June 2027 – 30 November 2028) 
Expected Outcome 
The extension will ensure uninterrupted Payment Gateway Services are maintained while the replacement contract is procured and the successor service is implemented, integrated, tested and transitioned into live operation. It will also provide sufficient time to accommodate ongoing business requirements arising from Ministerial decisions regarding eVED, and the future incorporation of Open Banking services, ensuring the replacement solution is appropriately designed, procured and implemented. 
The optional extension period of up to 6 months will provide additional contingency, if required, to support completion of procurement, implementation, integration and transition activities while maintaining continuity of critical payment services and minimising disruption to DVLA customers.

records.title: 2026 - Aberdeenshire Council - Children's Care at Home - Framework Opportunity
records.description:
Aberdeenshire Council is issuing this Prior Information Notice (PIN) to inform the market of a potential future opportunity relating to the provision of Care at Home services for children and young people with Additional Support Needs (ASN).
The Council currently operates a framework arrangement for the delivery of support services to children and young people with a range of additional support needs. Whilst this arrangement covers the whole of Aberdeenshire, providers will be able to select the areas they have capacity to deliver support in. The purpose of this PIN is to assess market interest in a possible re-opening of the existing framework to allow new providers to apply for inclusion. Subject to a decision being made to re-open the framework and the availability of suitable provider capacity, the Council anticipates that service delivery would commence on or around 1 April 2027.
The services may include, but are not limited to:
-	Supporting parents/carers with care and play within the family home, which may include personal care and People Moving and Assisting where a young person has mobility difficulties.
-	Supporting young people to develop life and independence skills both at home and in their local/wider community, including independent travel skills, simple food preparation, shopping within a small budget and money awareness and household tasks.
-	Supporting children and young people to access community-based activities such as local community groups e.g., Brownies, Guides, Cubs, Scouts, Live Life Aberdeenshire activities, horse riding, swimming lessons, going to the cinema, soft play centres, trampoline parks etc.
-	The activities to be undertaken will be informed by the Child and Young Person’s Assessment Outcomes.
This notice is issued solely for information and market engagement purposes.
The Council wishes to understand:
-	The level of interest from prospective providers.
-	The capacity and capability available within the market.
-	If Services are currently registered with the Care Inspectorate to provide support to children and young people
-	Potential barriers to participation.
-	Opportunities to further develop service provision within the local area
At this stage, no decision has been made to re-open the framework, and this PIN does not constitute a commitment to undertake a procurement exercise. Any future decision to re-open the framework will be informed by the level of market interest gained via this engagement exercise, alongside the Council's assessment of service needs and commissioning priorities. The value stated within this notice reflects the value of the existing framework and is provided for indicative purposes only. Any future opportunity may differ in scope and value, which will be determined following completion of this market engagement activity.
The Council reserves the right not to proceed with any procurement process following this PIN.
