records.title: CeTPD Laboratory Information Management System
records.description:
The Centre for Targeted Protein Degradation (CeTPD) is an academic research center focused on translational chemical biology, currently housing ~60 researchers and technicians across disciplines and experience levels (undergraduate, post graduate students, post-docs, (senior) staff scientists, Principal Investigators). The requirement is a software solution, for all research staff, that provides Laboratory Information Management System (LIMs) capability. This broadly includes scientist electronic lab notebook (across disciplines), reagent inventory and management, compound inventory and management and ideally some capability for processed data databasing and rudimentary visualisation.
We are seeking to procure a secure, cloud-based design and Laboratory Information Management System to support collaborative drug discovery workflows.
The solution is expected to deliver;
- An integrated platform for electronic lab notebooks, reagent inventory management, compound registration and management and ideally data visualisation.
- The system must accommodate the needs of scientists in both chemical and biological sciences and their respective workflows.
- The system must accommodate that Users may require access relevant to both chemical biological sciences workflows within the same user area.
- Seamless integration with existing computational workflows
- Seamless integration with third-party applications and/or databases
- A secure, stable and scalable cloud deployment which
Complies with the University and collaborator cybersecurity, information governance and GDPR requirements
Meets with strict performance, reliability and governance standards
Meets with the functional and non-functional requirements of the CeTPD (as outlined below)
- Improved operational efficiency, regulatory compliance, and scalability to support future growth and evolving scientific needs

Journeys are currently arranged locally, often through funeral directors, with variation in cost and no overall control of availability, or quality. Workforce shortages and uneven capacity is increasing the need for deceased babies to be transferred between pathology centres for post mortem examinations. There are currently no standards for the current local arrangements to follow or transport-specific requirements in place. This creates an avoidable risk of loss of tissue integrity and delayed post-mortem results.
A pre-market engagement shall be conducted on Wed 2nd Dec from 10am to help identify suppliers who are willing to provide suggestions on service improvements and efficiencies, whilst respecting and retaining the dignity of the deceased.

records.title: Provision of Servicing and Maintenance of the Laundry Production Equipment at Nottingham City Hospital
records.description:
The Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust (The Client) requires a Supplier for provision of Servicing and Maintenance of the Laundry Production Equipment at Nottingham City Hospital (The service).
The purpose of the service is to ensure high quality wash results, reduce the likelihood of costly breakdowns, optimize the Client’s chemical usage and increase the life of the equipment, mitigating the requirement to purchase new assets due to lack of maintenance.
Laundry production and subsequently, the Client's organisation would be adversely affected in the event of any prolonged downtime whilst the laundry is operating. Therefore, as a minimum, an engineer must be available on site at any time the laundry is operating. Even a minor issue, such as a machine tripping out, resulting in equipment out of action, would then have a knock-on effect with volume of fresh linen available to the Client's wards, for example.
Therefore, a Supplier is required to deliver full on site engineering services to cover planned preventive and reactive servicing and maintenance.
The objective is to ensure the Laundry Production Equipment is supported by qualified engineers and is fit for the purpose of enabling the Client’s staff to operate the equipment safely, efficiently and reliably.
The Contractor will be required to utilize the Client's digital planned preventative maintenance (PPM) system to provide the service.

records.buyer: NHS NORTH EAST AND NORTH CUMBRIA INTEGRATED CARE BOARD
records.title: North East and North Cumbria Steps to Safety Programme Operational Management Coordination and Delivery Lead
records.description:
This preliminary market engagement notice invites individuals and organisations to express an interest, complete a request for information questionnaire and register their request to attend a 60-minute provider engagement event in regards to a future Steps to Safety Programme for the North East and North Cumbria region.
As part of a larger strategy to create a service that is fully integrated into the existing North East and North Cumbria (NENC) service landscape, NENC ICB requires a Steps to Safety Programme Operational Management Coordination and Delivery Lead (a suitably qualified provider or provider partnership) to manage, coordinate and support delivery of the Steps to Safety programme across the NENC region.
The Teams-based market engagement event will be held on Monday 07 December 2026 at 3pm. More details are available in the NENC105 Documentation on the Salesforce Atamis e-tendering portal. Contract Ref. C491688 and title NENC105 Market Engagement NENC ICB Steps to Safety Programme Delivery Lead RFI.
Steps to Safety provides an important opportunity for NHS North East and North Cumbria ICB (NENC ICB) to demonstrate the contribution that health services can make to the ambitions set out in the Government’s Freedom from Violence and Abuse: A Cross Government Strategy. Domestic abuse and sexual violence can have profound and enduring consequences for physical health, mental health, wellbeing and health inequalities, and primary care has an important role in enabling people to access help.
Through a consistent general practice model, strengthened workforce confidence and clear pathways into specialist support, Steps to Safety aims to move the system towards earlier identification and intervention, improved access to support and a more consistent response for victims and survivors across North East and North Cumbria.
In order to introduce the Steps to Safety programme and NENC draft service specification to the regional market, and to begin identifying potential providers and collaborators, NENC ICB is hosting a Microsoft Teams based provider engagement event. The purpose of this event is to further discuss establishing the Steps to Safety programme for the NENC region.
This event will offer providers:
•	Additional information on the Steps to Safety programme;
•	An overview of the proposed Steps to Safety Programme Operational
Management Coordination and Delivery Lead role which NENC ICB
anticipates commissioning through a compliant procurement process
in the near future;
•	The opportunity to introduce themselves and discuss coordination of
services, collaboration, and potential provider partnership needs and
requirements.
Interested providers and/or collaborators are invited to attend the event.

The Council of the Borough of Kirklees (the "Council") is conducting this procurement using the competitive process in accordance with the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023 ("the PSR").

The Early Intervention and Prevention Support Service will support families via the promotion, coordination and facilitation of the National Healthy Start scheme, and the dissemination and provision of accident prevention advice, home interventions and delivery and fitting of preventative equipment. ·	Breastfeeding
·	Healthy weight and nutrition
·	Health literacy, managing minor illnesses and reducing accidents
